A friend of his, one Vernon, having some money due to him in Pensilvania, about thirty-five pounds currency, desired I would receive it for him, and keep it till I had his directions what to remit it in. Accordingly, he gave me an order. This afterwards occasion'd me a good deal of uneasiness.
paras.z: 单桅船在罗得岛的纽波特靠了岸，我去看望了哥哥约翰，他结婚以后在那里已经定居了几年。他待我非常亲热，因为他一向疼我。他有一个朋友，姓弗农，在宾夕法尼亚有一笔别人欠他的钱，大约三十五镑当地货币，托我替他收下，先保管着，等他通知我用什么方式汇给他。他为此给了我一张委托书。这件事后来给我招来了不少烦恼。

paras.e: At Newport we took in a number of passengers for New York, among which were two young women, companions, and a grave, sensible, matron-like Quaker woman, with her attendants. I had shown an obliging readiness to do her some little services, which impress'd her I suppose with a degree of good will toward me; therefore, when she saw a daily growing familiarity between me and the two young women, which they appear'd to encourage, she took me aside, and said: "Young man, I am concern'd for thee, as thou has no friend with thee, and seems not to know much of the world, or of the snares youth is expos'd to; depend upon it, those are very bad women; I can see it in all their actions; and if thee art not upon thy guard, they will draw thee into some danger; they are strangers to thee, and I advise thee, in a friendly concern for thy welfare, to have no acquaintance with them." As I seem'd at first not to think so ill of them as she did, she mentioned some things she had observ'd and heard that had escap'd my notice, but now convinc'd me she was right. I thank'd her for her kind advice, and promis'd to follow it. When we arriv'd at New York, they told me where they liv'd, and invited me to come and see them; but I avoided it, and it was well I did; for the next day the captain miss'd a silver spoon and some other things, that had been taken out of his cabbin, and, knowing that these were a couple of strumpets, he got a warrant to search their lodgings, found the stolen goods, and had the thieves punish'd. So, tho' we had escap'd a sunken rock, which we scrap'd upon in the passage, I thought this escape of rather more importance to me.
paras.z: 在纽波特，船上又上了一批去纽约的乘客，其中有两个结伴的年轻女子，还有一位端庄、明理、像个当家主妇似的贵格会女教友，带着几个随从。我曾经殷勤地替她做过几件小事，我想这使她对我有了几分好感。所以，她看到我同那两个年轻女子一天比一天亲热，而她们似乎也有意逗引我，就把我拉到一边说：“年轻人，我替你担心，因为你身边没有朋友，看来对世事，对年轻人容易落入的圈套，都不大懂。相信我的话，那是两个很坏的女人，从她们的一举一动我就看得出来。你要是不提防，她们会把你拖进危险里去。她们同你素不相识，我是出于对你的关心，好意劝你不要同她们来往。”我起初似乎并不把她们想得像她说的那样坏，她就讲了几件她看到和听到而我没有留意的事，这下我相信她是对的了。我谢了她的好意，答应照她的话做。到了纽约，那两个女子把住址告诉我，请我去看她们；我没有去，幸亏没有去。因为第二天，船长发现舱里少了一把银匙和几样别的东西，他知道这两个女人是娼妓，就领了搜查证去搜她们的住处，找到了赃物，让小偷受了惩罚。所以，我们在航程中虽然躲过了一块暗礁——船身还在上面擦了一下——我却认为，躲过这一劫对我更要紧些。

paras.e: At New York I found my friend Collins, who had arriv'd there some time before me. We had been intimate from children, and had read the same books together; but he had the advantage of more time for reading and studying, and a wonderful genius for mathematical learning, in which he far outstript me. While I liv'd in Boston most of my hours of leisure for conversation were spent with him, and he continu'd a sober as well as an industrious lad; was much respected for his learning by several of the clergy and other gentlemen, and seemed to promise making a good figure in life. But, during my absence, he had acquir'd a habit of sotting with brandy; and I found by his own account, and what I heard from others, that he had been drunk every day since his arrival at New York, and behav'd very oddly. He had gam'd, too, and lost his money, so that I was oblig'd to discharge his lodgings, and defray his expenses to and at Philadelphia, which prov'd extremely inconvenient to me.
paras.z: 在纽约我找到了朋友柯林斯，他比我早到了一些日子。我们从小就很要好，一起读过同样的书；但他读书和钻研的时间比我多，在数学方面又有惊人的天分，远远超过了我。我住在波士顿的时候，闲下来同人谈天的时间大半是同他一起过的；他一直是个既勤奋又不沾酒的少年，几位牧师和别的绅士都因为他的学问而很敬重他，看来将来会大有出息。可是在我离开期间，他染上了狂饮白兰地的习惯。从他自己的话里，也从别人那里，我得知他到纽约以后天天喝醉，举止十分古怪。他还赌钱，把钱输光了，所以我不得不替他付清房钱，还要负担他去费城的路费和到费城以后的开销，这使我极为拮据。

paras.e: The then governor of New York, Burnet (son of Bishop Burnet), hearing from the captain that a young man, one of his passengers, had a great many books, desir'd he would bring me to see him. I waited upon him accordingly, and should have taken Collins with me but that he was not sober. The gov'r. treated me with great civility, show'd me his library, which was a very large one, and we had a good deal of conversation about books and authors. This was the second governor who had done me the honor to take notice of me; which, to a poor boy like me, was very pleasing.
paras.z: 当时的纽约总督伯内特（伯内特主教的儿子）听船长说，他的乘客里有一个年轻人带了很多书，就要船长带我去见他。我于是去拜见了他；本来该带柯林斯一起去，可他那时没有醒酒。总督待我十分客气，带我看了他的藏书，数量很大，我们就书和作者谈了很久。这是第二位屈尊注意到我的总督；对我这样一个穷孩子来说，这是很叫人高兴的事。

paras.e: We proceeded to Philadelphia. I received on the way Vernon's money, without which we could hardly have finish'd our journey. Collins wished to be employ'd in some counting-house, but, whether they discover'd his dramming by his breath, or by his behaviour, tho' he had some recommendations, he met with no success in any application, and continu'd lodging and boarding at the same house with me, and at my expense. Knowing I had that money of Vernon's, he was continually borrowing of me, still promising repayment as soon as he should be in business. At length he had got so much of it that I was distress'd to think what I should do in case of being call'd on to remit it.
paras.z: 我们接着前往费城。路上我收到了弗农的那笔钱，没有它，我们几乎走不完这趟路。柯林斯想在哪家商号的账房里谋个差事，可是不知人家是从他嘴里的气味还是从他的举止看出了他贪杯，他虽然有几封介绍信，却到处碰壁，只好继续同我住在一处、吃在一处，一切由我出钱。他知道我手里有弗农那笔钱，就不断向我借，总是许诺一有了差事就还。到后来他借去的已经很多，我一想到万一人家要我汇款该怎么办，就发愁。

paras.e: His drinking continu'd, about which we sometimes quarrell'd; for, when a little intoxicated, he was very fractious. Once, in a boat on the Delaware with some other young men, he refused to row in his turn. "I will be row'd home," says he. "We will not row you," says I. "You must, or stay all night on the water," says he, "just as you please." The others said, "Let us row; what signifies it?" But, my mind being soured with his other conduct, I continu'd to refuse. So he swore he would make me row, or throw me overboard; and coming along, stepping on the thwarts, toward me, when he came up and struck at me, I clapped my hand under his crutch, and, rising, pitched him head-foremost into the river. I knew he was a good swimmer, and so was under little concern about him; but before he could get round to lay hold of the boat, we had with a few strokes pull'd her out of his reach; and ever when he drew near the boat, we ask'd if he would row, striking a few strokes to slide her away from him. He was ready to die with vexation, and obstinately would not promise to row. However, seeing him at last beginning to tire, we lifted him in and brought him home dripping wet in the evening. We hardly exchang'd a civil word afterwards, and a West India captain, who had a commission to procure a tutor for the sons of a gentleman at Barbadoes, happening to meet with him, agreed to carry him thither. He left me then, promising to remit me the first money he should receive in order to discharge the debt; but I never heard of him after.
paras.z: 他照旧喝酒，我们有时为此争吵，因为他一有点醉意就很难缠。有一回，我们同另外几个年轻人在特拉华河上划船，轮到他划，他不肯。他说：“我要让你们把我划回家。”我说：“我们不划你。”他说：“你们非划不可，要不就在水上过夜，随你们的便。”别人说：“我们划就是了，这有什么要紧？”可是我因为他别的那些行径心里正窝着火，仍然不肯。于是他赌咒说，非叫我划不可，不然就把我扔下水去；说着踩着坐板朝我走过来。他走到跟前动手打我，我一把抄住他的腿裆，一起身，把他头朝下扔进了河里。我知道他水性好，所以并不怎么替他担心；可是他还没来得及转过身来抓住船帮，我们已经划了几桨，让他够不着了。每逢他游近船边，我们就问他肯不肯划，同时划上几桨，让船从他身边滑开。他气得要死，却硬是不肯答应划船。不过后来见他开始没有力气了，我们才把他拉上船，傍晚把湿淋淋的他送回了家。从那以后我们几乎没有说过一句客气话。有一位西印度群岛的船长受巴巴多斯一位绅士之托，要替他的儿子们找一位家庭教师，碰巧遇上了他，答应带他去。他就这样离开了我，答应拿到头一笔钱就汇给我还债；可是从此我再没有听到他的消息。

paras.e: The breaking into this money of Vernon's was one of the first great errata of my life; and this affair show'd that my father was not much out in his judgment when he suppos'd me too young to manage business of importance. But Sir William, on reading his letter, said he was too prudent. There was great difference in persons; and discretion did not always accompany years, nor was youth always without it. "And since he will not set you up," says he, "I will do it myself. Give me an inventory of the things necessary to be had from England, and I will send for them. You shall repay me when you are able; I am resolv'd to have a good printer here, and I am sure you must succeed." This was spoken with such an appearance of cordiality, that I had not the least doubt of his meaning what he said. I had hitherto kept the proposition of my setting up, a secret in Philadelphia, and I still kept it. Had it been known that I depended on the governor, probably some friend, that knew him better, would have advis'd me not to rely on him, as I afterwards heard it as his known character to be liberal of promises which he never meant to keep. Yet, unsolicited as he was by me, how could I think his generous offers insincere? I believ'd him one of the best men in the world.
paras.z: 动用弗农的这笔钱，是我一生中最早的重大“印刷错误”之一。这件事也说明，我父亲认为我太年轻、管不了要紧的事，并没有看错多少。可是威廉爵士读了他的信，却说他太谨慎了。人和人大不相同，审慎未必总随年龄而来，年轻人也未必都没有。他说：“既然他不肯资助你开业，那就由我自己来办。你给我开一张清单，写明需要从英国置办的东西，我派人去买。你将来有能力的时候再还我。我决心要让这里有一个好印刷商，我相信你一定会成功。”他说这话的时候显得那样诚恳，我一点也不怀疑他是真心的。在此之前，我一直对费城的人保守着我要开业的秘密，这时仍然没有说。要是有人知道我指望的是总督，也许会有比我更了解他的朋友劝我不要依赖他；因为我后来听说，他的脾性人所共知，许起愿来很慷慨，却从不打算兑现。可是，我并没有求过他，他主动提出这样慷慨的建议，我怎么会想到他没有诚意呢？我相信他是世上最好的人之一。

paras.e: I presented him an inventory of a little print'g-house, amounting by my computation to about one hundred pounds sterling. He lik'd it, but ask'd me if my being on the spot in England to chuse the types, and see that every thing was good of the kind, might not be of some advantage. "Then," says he, "when there, you may make acquaintances, and establish correspondences in the bookselling and stationery way." I agreed that this might be advantageous. "Then," says he, "get yourself ready to go with Annis;" which was the annual ship, and the only one at that time usually passing between London and Philadelphia. But it would be some months before Annis sail'd, so I continu'd working with Keimer, fretting about the money Collins had got from me, and in daily apprehensions of being call'd upon by Vernon, which, however, did not happen for some years after.
paras.z: 我交给他一张小印刷所的置办清单，照我的估算，大约要一百英镑。他很满意，但问我，要是我亲自到英国去挑选铅字，照看每一样东西都是上等货，是不是更有好处。他说：“而且，你到了那里，还可以结识一些人，在书籍和文具买卖方面建立往来关系。”我同意这样或许有好处。他说：“那么，你就准备搭安尼斯的船去吧。”那是一年一班的船，也是当时通常往来于伦敦和费城之间的唯一的一艘船。可是离安尼斯开船还有好几个月，我就继续在凯默那里干活，为柯林斯从我手里弄走的那笔钱发愁，天天担心弗农来讨；不过这件事过了好几年才发生。

paras.e: I believe I have omitted mentioning that, in my first voyage from Boston, being becalm'd off Block Island, our people set about catching cod, and hauled up a great many. Hitherto I had stuck to my resolution of not eating animal food, and on this occasion consider'd, with my master Tryon, the taking every fish as a kind of unprovoked murder, since none of them had, or ever could do us any injury that might justify the slaughter. All this seemed very reasonable. But I had formerly been a great lover of fish, and, when this came hot out of the frying-pan, it smelt admirably well. I balanc'd some time between principle and inclination, till I recollected that, when the fish were opened, I saw smaller fish taken out of their stomachs; then thought I, "If you eat one another, I don't see why we mayn't eat you." So I din'd upon cod very heartily, and continued to eat with other people, returning only now and then occasionally to a vegetable diet. So convenient a thing it is to be a reasonable creature, since it enables one to find or make a reason for everything one has a mind to do.
paras.z: 我想我忘了提一件事：我头一次从波士顿出海的时候，船在布洛克岛外海遇上无风，停住了，船上的人就动手钓鳕鱼，钓上来很多。在这之前，我一直坚守不吃荤的决心；这一回，我同我的老师特赖恩一样，认为每捕一条鱼都是一种无端的谋杀，因为它们谁也没有伤害过我们，也永远不可能伤害我们，杀它们是没有道理的。这一切似乎很有道理。可是我从前是极爱吃鱼的，这鱼从煎锅里热腾腾地端出来，香得很。我在原则和嗜好之间权衡了一阵，后来想起，剖开鱼的时候，我看见从它们肚子里掏出了小鱼。于是我想：“既然你们互相吃，我看不出我们为什么不可以吃你们。”我就痛痛快快地吃了一顿鳕鱼，此后也同别人一样吃荤，只是偶尔再吃一阵素。做一个“有理性的动物”真是方便，因为不管你想做什么，理性都能让你找到或者造出一条理由来。

paras.e: Keimer and I liv'd on a pretty good familiar footing, and agreed tolerably well, for he suspected nothing of my setting up. He retained a great deal of his old enthusiasms and lov'd argumentation. We therefore had many disputations. I used to work him so with my Socratic method, and had trepann'd him so often by questions apparently so distant from any point we had in hand, and yet by degrees lead to the point, and brought him into difficulties and contradictions, that at last he grew ridiculously cautious, and would hardly answer me the most common question, without asking first, "What do you intend to infer from that?" However, it gave him so high an opinion of my abilities in the confuting way, that he seriously proposed my being his colleague in a project he had of setting up a new sect. He was to preach the doctrines, and I was to confound all opponents. When he came to explain with me upon the doctrines, I found several conundrums which I objected to, unless I might have my way a little too, and introduce some of mine.
paras.z: 凯默和我相处得相当熟络，还算合得来，因为他一点也没有疑心我要自己开业。他那种旧日的宗教狂热还保留了很多，又喜欢辩论，所以我们常常争论。我总用我的苏格拉底方法来摆布他，一次次用一些看来同眼前的题目毫不相干的问题引他上钩，再一步步引到正题上，使他陷入困境和自相矛盾。到后来他小心得可笑，连最平常的问题也几乎不肯回答，非要先问一句：“你打算由此推出什么来？”不过，这使他对我驳倒别人的本事评价极高，竟郑重其事地提议让我做他的同事，一起实行他创立一个新教派的计划。由他宣讲教义，由我驳倒一切反对的人。等到他向我解释他的教义，我发现其中有好几条古怪的东西，我表示反对，除非也让我多少照自己的意思办，加进几条我的主张。

paras.e: Keimer wore his beard at full length, because somewhere in the Mosaic law it is said, "Thou shalt not mar the corners of thy beard." He likewise kept the Seventh day, Sabbath; and these two points were essentials with him. I dislik'd both; but agreed to admit them upon condition of his adopting the doctrine of using no animal food. "I doubt," said he, "my constitution will not bear that." I assur'd him it would, and that he would be the better for it. He was usually a great glutton, and I promised myself some diversion in half starving him. He agreed to try the practice, if I would keep him company. I did so, and we held it for three months. We had our victuals dress'd, and brought to us regularly by a woman in the neighborhood, who had from me a list of forty dishes to be prepar'd for us at different times, in all which there was neither fish, flesh, nor fowl, and the whim suited me the better at this time from the cheapness of it, not costing us above eighteenpence sterling each per week. I have since kept several Lents most strictly, leaving the common diet for that, and that for the common, abruptly, without the least inconvenience, so that I think there is little in the advice of making those changes by easy gradations. I went on pleasantly, but poor Keimer suffered grievously, tired of the project, long'd for the flesh-pots of Egypt, and order'd a roast pig. He invited me and two women friends to dine with him; but, it being brought too soon upon table, he could not resist the temptation, and ate the whole before we came.
paras.z: 凯默留着一部长胡子，因为摩西律法里有个地方说：“胡须的周围不可损坏。”他还守第七日为安息日。这两条在他是根本大事。我两条都不喜欢，但同意接受，条件是他要采纳不吃荤的教义。他说：“我恐怕我的体质受不了。”我向他保证受得了，而且对他只有好处。他平时是个大馋鬼，我想把他饿个半死，寻点开心。他同意试一试，只要我陪着他。我照办了，我们坚持了三个月。我们的饭食由附近一个妇人做好，按时送来；我给了她一张单子，上面有四十样菜，让她轮流做给我们吃，没有一样是鱼、肉或家禽。这种怪念头在当时对我格外合适，因为便宜，每人每星期花不到十八便士。从那以后，我有好几次极严格地守过大斋期，从平常的饮食一下子改吃素，又从吃素一下子改回平常的饮食，毫无不适；所以我认为，说这类改变要慢慢来的那种劝告，没有多少道理。我过得挺愉快，可怜的凯默却苦不堪言，对这个计划厌烦透了，一心想念埃及的肉锅，就订了一只烤乳猪。他请我和两位女友同他一起吃饭；可是猪端上桌太早，他抵挡不住诱惑，没等我们到，就一个人把它全吃光了。

paras.e: I had made some courtship during this time to Miss Read. I had a great respect and affection for her, and had some reason to believe she had the same for me; but, as I was about to take a long voyage, and we were both very young, only a little above eighteen, it was thought most prudent by her mother to prevent our going too far at present, as a marriage, if it was to take place, would be more convenient after my return, when I should be, as I expected, set up in my business. Perhaps, too, she thought my expectations not so well founded as I imagined them to be.
paras.z: 这段时间里，我向里德小姐求过爱。我很敬重她，也很爱她，并且有理由相信她对我也是一样。可是我就要出远门，我们俩又都很年轻，才十八岁出头，她母亲认为最稳妥的办法是眼下不要让我们走得太远；如果要结婚，等我回来以后更合适，那时我应该已经像我预期的那样开了业。也许她还觉得，我的指望并不像我自己想的那样靠得住。

paras.e: My chief acquaintances at this time were Charles Osborne, Joseph Watson, and James Ralph, all lovers of reading. The two first were clerks to an eminent scrivener or conveyancer in the town, Charles Brogden; the other was clerk to a merchant. Watson was a pious, sensible young man, of great integrity; the others rather more lax in their principles of religion, particularly Ralph, who, as well as Collins, had been unsettled by me, for which they both made me suffer. Osborne was sensible, candid, frank; sincere and affectionate to his friends; but, in literary matters, too fond of criticising. Ralph was ingenious, genteel in his manners, and extremely eloquent; I think I never knew a prettier talker. Both of them great admirers of poetry, and began to try their hands in little pieces. Many pleasant walks we four had together on Sundays into the woods, near Schuylkill, where we read to one another, and conferr'd on what we read.
paras.z: 这时候我主要的朋友是查尔斯·奥斯本、约瑟夫·沃森和詹姆斯·拉尔夫，都是爱读书的人。前两位是镇上一位有名的代书人兼产权转让律师查尔斯·布罗格登的书记，后一位是一个商人的伙计。沃森是个虔诚、明理的青年，为人极正直；另外两位在宗教原则上要松懈得多，特别是拉尔夫，他同柯林斯一样，是被我动摇了信仰的，为此他们两个后来都叫我吃了苦头。奥斯本明白事理，坦率直爽，对朋友真诚而热心；但在文学方面太爱挑剔。拉尔夫头脑聪明，举止文雅，口才极好，我想我从没见过比他更会说话的人。他们两个都非常爱好诗歌，并且开始试着写些小诗。星期天，我们四个人常常一起到斯库尔基尔河附近的树林里去散步，十分愉快；我们在那里互相朗读，讨论读过的东西。

paras.e: Ralph was inclin'd to pursue the study of poetry, not doubting but he might become eminent in it, and make his fortune by it, alleging that the best poets must, when they first began to write, make as many faults as he did. Osborne dissuaded him, assur'd him he had no genius for poetry, and advis'd him to think of nothing beyond the business he was bred to; that, in the mercantile way, tho' he had no stock, he might, by his diligence and punctuality, recommend himself to employment as a factor, and in time acquire wherewith to trade on his own account. I approv'd the amusing one's self with poetry now and then, so far as to improve one's language, but no farther.
paras.z: 拉尔夫有意钻研诗歌，毫不怀疑自己能在这方面出人头地，并且靠它发财；他说，最好的诗人初学写作的时候，一定也同他一样毛病百出。奥斯本劝他打消这个念头，断言他没有写诗的才气，劝他除了自己学的那一行，别的什么也不要想；说在经商这条路上，他虽然没有本钱，凭着勤勉守时，也可以让人家信得过，雇他做代理人，日子久了就能攒下自己做买卖的本钱。我赞成偶尔作作诗消遣，以能改进自己的文字为度，再多就不必了。

paras.e: On this it was propos'd that we should each of us, at our next meeting, produce a piece of our own composing, in order to improve by our mutual observations, criticisms, and corrections. As language and expression were what we had in view, we excluded all considerations of invention by agreeing that the task should be a version of the eighteenth Psalm, which describes the descent of a Deity. When the time of our meeting drew nigh, Ralph called on me first, and let me know his piece was ready. I told him I had been busy, and, having little inclination, had done nothing. He then show'd me his piece for my opinion, and I much approv'd it, as it appear'd to me to have great merit. "Now," says he, "Osborne never will allow the least merit in any thing of mine, but makes 1000 criticisms out of mere envy. He is not so jealous of you; I wish, therefore, you would take this piece, and produce it as yours; I will pretend not to have had time, and so produce nothing. We shall then see what he will say to it." It was agreed, and I immediately transcrib'd it, that it might appear in my own hand.
paras.z: 于是有人提议，下次聚会时我们每人拿出一篇自己的作品，通过互相评论、批评和修改来求长进。我们着眼的是语言和表达，为了撇开构思方面的考虑，大家约定，题目就是改写《诗篇》第十八篇，那一篇描写的是上帝降临。聚会的日子快到了，拉尔夫先来找我，告诉我他的那篇已经写好。我对他说，我一直很忙，又没有多大兴致，什么也没有写。他就把他的作品拿给我看，问我的意见，我大为称赞，因为在我看来写得很出色。他说：“你瞧，奥斯本从来不肯承认我的东西有一点点好处，纯粹出于嫉妒，要挑上一千个毛病。他对你倒不那么嫉妒；所以我希望你把这篇拿去，当作你的拿出来；我就假装没有时间，什么也不拿。我们看看他会怎么说。”我们说定了，我马上把它抄了一遍，好让它看起来是我的笔迹。

paras.e: We met; Watson's performance was read; there were some beauties in it, but many defects. Osborne's was read; it was much better; Ralph did it justice; remarked some faults, but applauded the beauties. He himself had nothing to produce. I was backward; seemed desirous of being excused; had not had sufficient time to correct, etc.; but no excuse could be admitted; produce I must. It was read and repeated; Watson and Osborne gave up the contest, and join'd in applauding it. Ralph only made some criticisms, and propos'd some amendments; but I defended my text. Osborne was against Ralph, and told him he was no better a critic than poet, so he dropt the argument. As they two went home together, Osborne expressed himself still more strongly in favor of what he thought my production; having restrain'd himself before, as he said, lest I should think it flattery. "But who would have imagin'd," said he, "that Franklin had been capable of such a performance; such painting, such force, such fire! He has even improv'd the original. In his common conversation he seems to have no choice of words; he hesitates and blunders; and yet, good God! how he writes!" When we next met, Ralph discovered the trick we had plaid him, and Osborne was a little laught at.
paras.z: 我们聚会了。先读了沃森的作品，里面有几处写得好，但毛病很多。接着读奥斯本的，要好得多；拉尔夫对它作了公正的评价，指出了一些毛病，但赞扬了好的地方。他自己没有东西可拿。我故意推托，好像很想请大家免了我这一回，说没有足够的时间修改，等等；可是什么借口都不行，非拿出来不可。我的作品读了一遍，又读了一遍；沃森和奥斯本甘拜下风，一同喝起彩来。只有拉尔夫提了几点批评，建议改几个地方；我却为我的文字辩护。奥斯本反对拉尔夫，对他说，他作批评家同他作诗人一样不高明，拉尔夫就不再争了。他们两个一起回家的路上，奥斯本对这篇他以为是我写的作品更是赞不绝口；他说他先前忍着没说，是怕我以为那是恭维。他说：“可是谁想得到富兰克林竟写得出这样的东西！这样的描绘，这样的力量，这样的火热！他甚至比原作还高明。他平常说话好像连字眼都不会挑，吞吞吐吐，错误百出；可是，老天爷！他写得多好啊！”我们下一次聚会时，拉尔夫揭穿了我们对他耍的把戏，奥斯本让大家取笑了一番。

paras.e: This transaction fixed Ralph in his resolution of becoming a poet. I did all I could to dissuade him from it, but he continued scribbling verses till Pope cured him. He became, however, a pretty good prose writer. More of him hereafter. But, as I may not have occasion again to mention the other two, I shall just remark here, that Watson died in my arms a few years after, much lamented, being the best of our set. Osborne went to the West Indies, where he became an eminent lawyer and made money, but died young. He and I had made a serious agreement, that the one who happen'd first to die should, if possible, make a friendly visit to the other, and acquaint him how he found things in that separate state. But he never fulfill'd his promise.
paras.z: 这件事使拉尔夫当诗人的决心更坚定了。我竭力劝他打消念头，可他仍旧不停地涂写诗句，直到蒲柏把他的毛病治好。不过他后来成了一个相当不错的散文作家。关于他，后面还要说到。至于另外两位，我以后也许没有机会再提，就在这里说一句：沃森几年以后死在我的怀里，大家都很痛惜，他是我们这一伙里最好的人。奥斯本去了西印度群岛，在那里成了有名的律师，赚了钱，可是死得很早。他同我曾经郑重约定：谁先死，如果可能，就要回来友好地探望另一个，告诉他那边的情形如何。可是他始终没有履行诺言。

paras.e: The governor, seeming to like my company, had me frequently to his house, and his setting me up was always mention'd as a fixed thing. I was to take with me letters recommendatory to a number of his friends, besides the letter of credit to furnish me with the necessary money for purchasing the press and types, paper, etc. For these letters I was appointed to call at different times, when they were to be ready, but a future time was still named. Thus he went on till the ship, whose departure too had been several times postponed, was on the point of sailing. Then, when I call'd to take my leave and receive the letters, his secretary, Dr. Bard, came out to me and said the governor was extremely busy in writing, but would be down at Newcastle before the ship, and there the letters would be delivered to me.
paras.z: 总督似乎很喜欢同我在一起，常常请我到他家里去，每次总是把资助我开业当作已经定下的事来谈。我要随身带上他写给许多朋友的介绍信，另外还有一封信用证，好让我有钱购买印刷机、铅字、纸张等等。他几次约我在不同的日子去取这些信，说到时候就写好了，可是到时候总是又改约一个日子。就这样一直拖到船快要开了——开船的日期也已经推迟了好几次。这时我去辞行并取信，他的秘书巴德博士出来对我说，总督正忙着写东西，忙得不可开交，不过他会在船到之前赶到纽卡斯尔，在那里把信交给我。

paras.e: Ralph, though married, and having one child, had determined to accompany me in this voyage. It was thought he intended to establish a correspondence, and obtain goods to sell on commission; but I found afterwards, that, thro' some discontent with his wife's relations, he purposed to leave her on their hands, and never return again. Having taken leave of my friends, and interchang'd some promises with Miss Read, I left Philadelphia in the ship, which anchor'd at Newcastle. The governor was there; but when I went to his lodging, the secretary came to me from him with the civillest message in the world, that he could not then see me, being engaged in business of the utmost importance, but should send the letters to me on board, wish'd me heartily a good voyage and a speedy return, etc. I returned on board a little puzzled, but still not doubting.
paras.z: 拉尔夫虽然已经结婚，还有一个孩子，却决定陪我走这一趟。大家以为他是想去建立买卖关系，弄些货物回来代销；可是我后来发现，他因为同妻子的亲戚有些不和，打算把她丢给他们，永不回来。我向朋友们辞了行，同里德小姐互相许下了一些诺言，就乘船离开费城，船在纽卡斯尔下了锚。总督果然在那里；可是我到他的住处去，秘书出来替他传话，话说得客气极了：他此刻不能见我，因为正在处理极其重要的公务，不过会把信送到船上给我，衷心祝我一路顺风，早日归来，等等。我回到船上，有点纳闷，但仍然没有起疑。

paras.e: Mr. Andrew Hamilton, a famous lawyer of Philadelphia, had taken passage in the same ship for himself and son, and with Mr. Denham, a Quaker merchant, and Messrs. Onion and Russel, masters of an iron work in Maryland, had engag'd the great cabin; so that Ralph and I were forced to take up with a berth in the steerage, and none on board knowing us, were considered as ordinary persons. But Mr. Hamilton and his son (it was James, since governor) return'd from Newcastle to Philadelphia, the father being recall'd by a great fee to plead for a seized ship; and, just before we sail'd, Colonel French coming on board, and showing me great respect, I was more taken notice of, and, with my friend Ralph, invited by the other gentlemen to come into the cabin, there being now room. Accordingly, we remov'd thither.
paras.z: 费城著名的律师安德鲁·汉密尔顿先生给自己和儿子在这条船上订了舱位，他同贵格会商人德纳姆先生，还有马里兰一家铁厂的老板奥尼恩先生和拉塞尔先生，一起包下了大舱。这样，拉尔夫和我只好在统舱里将就一个铺位；船上没有人认识我们，把我们当作普通人看待。可是汉密尔顿先生和他儿子（就是詹姆斯，后来当了总督）从纽卡斯尔折回了费城，因为有人出了重金请这位父亲回去替一艘被扣押的船辩护。就在开船之前，弗伦奇上校上船来，对我十分敬重，我这才受到注意，那几位绅士见现在有了空位，就请我和我的朋友拉尔夫搬进大舱。于是我们搬了过去。

paras.e: Understanding that Colonel French had brought on board the governor's despatches, I ask'd the captain for those letters that were to be under my care. He said all were put into the bag together and he could not then come at them; but, before we landed in England, I should have an opportunity of picking them out; so I was satisfied for the present, and we proceeded on our voyage. We had a sociable company in the cabin, and lived uncommonly well, having the addition of all Mr. Hamilton's stores, who had laid in plentifully. In this passage Mr. Denham contracted a friendship for me that continued during his life. The voyage was otherwise not a pleasant one, as we had a great deal of bad weather.
paras.z: 我听说弗伦奇上校把总督的公文带上了船，就向船长要那些托我带的信。他说所有的信都装在一个邮袋里，眼下没法取出来；不过在英国登岸以前，我会有机会把它们挑出来。我暂时也就放了心，我们继续航行。大舱里的同伴都很合群，我们吃得格外好，因为汉密尔顿先生备下的大量食物全都留给了我们。在这次航行中，德纳姆先生同我结下了友谊，一直维持到他去世。除此以外，这次航行并不愉快，因为我们遇上了许多坏天气。

paras.e: When we came into the Channel, the captain kept his word with me, and gave me an opportunity of examining the bag for the governor's letters. I found none upon which my name was put as under my care. I picked out six or seven, that, by the handwriting, I thought might be the promised letters, especially as one of them was directed to Basket, the king's printer, and another to some stationer. We arriv'd in London the 24th of December, 1724. I waited upon the stationer, who came first in my way, delivering the letter as from Governor Keith. "I don't know such a person," says he; but, opening the letter, "O! this is from Riddlesden. I have lately found him to be a compleat rascal, and I will have nothing to do with him, nor receive any letters from him." So, putting the letter into my hand, he turn'd on his heel and left me to serve some customer. I was surprized to find these were not the governor's letters; and, after recollecting and comparing circumstances, I began to doubt his sincerity. I found my friend Denham, and opened the whole affair to him. He let me into Keith's character; told me there was not the least probability that he had written any letters for me; that no one, who knew him, had the smallest dependence on him; and he laught at the notion of the governor's giving me a letter of credit, having, as he said, no credit to give. On my expressing some concern about what I should do, he advised me to endeavor getting some employment in the way of my business. "Among the printers here," said he, "you will improve yourself, and when you return to America, you will set up to greater advantage."
paras.z: 船进了英吉利海峡，船长履行了他对我的诺言，让我有机会在邮袋里翻找总督的信。我没有找到一封写明托我转交的。我挑出六七封，从笔迹看我以为可能是许给我的那些信，尤其是其中一封是写给王家印刷商巴斯基特的，另一封是写给某个文具商的。我们在 1724 年 12 月 24 日到了伦敦。那位文具商住得最顺路，我就先去拜访他，把信交给他，说是基思总督写来的。他说：“我不认识这么个人。”可是拆开信一看：“哦！这是里德尔斯登写的。我最近才发现他是个十足的恶棍，我不想同他有任何来往，也不收他的任何信件。”说着把信塞到我手里，转身就去招呼别的顾客了。我发现这些并不是总督的信，大吃一惊；我回想前后的情形，一一对照，开始怀疑他的诚意。我找到我的朋友德纳姆，把整个事情原原本本告诉了他。他让我明白了基思的为人；他对我说，基思绝不可能替我写过什么信，凡是了解他的人，谁也不会对他有一丝一毫的指望。听说总督要给我开信用证，他笑了起来，说总督根本没有什么信用可以给人。我说我有些发愁，不知该怎么办才好，他就劝我设法在本行里找个差事。他说：“在这里的印刷商中间，你会长本事的；等你回到美洲，开起业来就更有利了。”

paras.e: We both of us happen'd to know, as well as the stationer, that Riddlesden, the attorney, was a very knave. He had half ruin'd Miss Read's father by persuading him to be bound for him. By this letter it appear'd there was a secret scheme on foot to the prejudice of Hamilton (suppos'd to be then coming over with us); and that Keith was concerned in it with Riddlesden. Denham, who was a friend of Hamilton's thought he ought to be acquainted with it; so, when he arriv'd in England, which was soon after, partly from resentment and ill-will to Keith and Riddlesden, and partly from good-will to him, I waited on him, and gave him the letter. He thank'd me cordially, the information being of importance to him; and from that time he became my friend, greatly to my advantage afterwards on many occasions.
paras.z: 我们两个，同那位文具商一样，都碰巧知道里德尔斯登这个律师是个十足的无赖。他曾经劝里德小姐的父亲替他作保，把人家害得几乎倾家荡产。从这封信看，有人正在暗中策划一个对汉密尔顿不利的阴谋（他们以为汉密尔顿当时正同我们一起渡海而来），基思同里德尔斯登都牵连在里面。德纳姆是汉密尔顿的朋友，认为应该让他知道这件事。所以，不久以后汉密尔顿到了英国，我一半出于对基思和里德尔斯登的愤恨和恶感，一半出于对他的好意，就去拜访他，把信交给了他。他热情地向我道谢，因为这个消息对他很重要；从那时起他成了我的朋友，后来在许多场合对我大有帮助。

paras.e: But what shall we think of a governor's playing such pitiful tricks, and imposing so grossly on a poor ignorant boy! It was a habit he had acquired. He wish'd to please everybody; and, having little to give, he gave expectations. He was otherwise an ingenious, sensible man, a pretty good writer, and a good governor for the people, tho' not for his constituents, the proprietaries, whose instructions he sometimes disregarded. Several of our best laws were of his planning and passed during his administration.
paras.z: 可是，一位总督竟耍这样可怜的把戏，这样恶劣地欺骗一个无知的穷孩子，我们该怎么看呢！这是他养成的习惯。他想讨每个人的喜欢；手里没有多少东西可给，就给人希望。除此以外，他倒是个聪明、明理的人，文章写得相当好，对百姓来说也是个好总督，虽然对他的委任者——那些业主们——来说并不是，因为他有时不理会他们的训令。我们有几条最好的法律就是他筹划的，并且是在他任内通过的。

paras.e: Ralph and I were inseparable companions. We took lodgings together in Little Britain at three shillings and sixpence a week--as much as we could then afford. He found some relations, but they were poor, and unable to assist him. He now let me know his intentions of remaining in London, and that he never meant to return to Philadelphia. He had brought no money with him, the whole he could muster having been expended in paying his passage. I had fifteen pistoles; so he borrowed occasionally of me to subsist, while he was looking out for business. He first endeavored to get into the playhouse, believing himself qualify'd for an actor; but Wilkes, to whom he apply'd, advis'd him candidly not to think of that employment, as it was impossible he should succeed in it. Then he propos'd to Roberts, a publisher in Paternoster Row, to write for him a weekly paper like the Spectator, on certain conditions, which Roberts did not approve. Then he endeavored to get employment as a hackney writer, to copy for the stationers and lawyers about the Temple, but could find no vacancy.
paras.z: 拉尔夫和我形影不离。我们一起在小不列颠街租了住处，每星期三先令六便士，这是我们当时出得起的最高价钱了。他找到了几个亲戚，可是他们很穷，帮不了他。这时他才告诉我，他打算留在伦敦，根本没想再回费城。他一文钱也没带来，凑得出的钱全都花在船费上了。我有十五个皮斯托尔金币，所以他在找事做的时候，不时向我借钱糊口。他先是想进戏院，自信有当演员的资格；可是他去求见的威尔克斯坦率地劝他不要想这一行，说他不可能成功。然后他向主祷文街的出版商罗伯茨提议，按一定的条件替他写一份像《旁观者》那样的周刊，罗伯茨没有同意那些条件。后来他又想找个雇佣文人的差事，替圣殿区一带的文具商和律师抄写，可是找不到空缺。

paras.e: I immediately got into work at Palmer's, then a famous printing-house in Bartholomew Close, and here I continu'd near a year. I was pretty diligent, but spent with Ralph a good deal of my earnings in going to plays and other places of amusement. We had together consumed all my pistoles, and now just rubbed on from hand to mouth. He seem'd quite to forget his wife and child, and I, by degrees, my engagements with Miss Read, to whom I never wrote more than one letter, and that was to let her know I was not likely soon to return. This was another of the great errata of my life, which I should wish to correct if I were to live it over again. In fact, by our expenses, I was constantly kept unable to pay my passage.
paras.z: 我马上在帕尔默印刷所找到了工作，那是当时巴塞洛缪巷里一家有名的印刷所，我在那里干了将近一年。我干活相当勤快，可是挣来的钱有一大半同拉尔夫一起花在看戏和别的娱乐场所里了。我们一起把我的金币全花光了，如今只能挣一点吃一点，勉强度日。他似乎完全忘了他的妻子和孩子，我也渐渐忘了同里德小姐的约定；我只给她写过一封信，还是告诉她我一时不大可能回去。这是我一生中又一个重大的“印刷错误”，如果能够重活一遍，我是很想把它改正的。事实上，照我们那样花钱，我始终凑不出回去的船费。

paras.e: At Palmer's I was employed in composing for the second edition of Wollaston's "Religion of Nature." Some of his reasonings not appearing to me well founded, I wrote a little metaphysical piece in which I made remarks on them. It was entitled "A Dissertation on Liberty and Necessity, Pleasure and Pain." I inscribed it to my friend Ralph; I printed a small number. It occasion'd my being more consider'd by Mr. Palmer as a young man of some ingenuity, tho' he seriously expostulated with me upon the principles of my pamphlet, which to him appear'd abominable. My printing this pamphlet was another erratum. While I lodg'd in Little Britain, I made an acquaintance with one Wilcox, a bookseller, whose shop was at the next door. He had an immense collection of second-hand books. Circulating libraries were not then in use; but we agreed that, on certain reasonable terms, which I have now forgotten, I might take, read, and return any of his books. This I esteem'd a great advantage, and I made as much use of it as I could.
paras.z: 在帕尔默印刷所，我被派去排沃拉斯顿《自然宗教》的第二版。他的有些推理在我看来根据不足，我就写了一篇形而上学的小文章，对这些推理加以评论，题目叫《论自由与必然，快乐与痛苦》。我把它题献给我的朋友拉尔夫，印了很少几本。帕尔默先生因此更看重我，认为我是个有些才气的青年，虽然他曾就小册子里的原则认真地规劝过我，在他看来那些原则是可憎的。印这本小册子是我的又一个“印刷错误”。我住在小不列颠街的时候，结识了一个叫威尔科克斯的书商，他的铺子就在隔壁。他收藏的旧书多极了。那时还没有流通图书馆；但我们讲定，按照某些合理的条件（什么条件我现在已经忘了），他的任何一本书我都可以拿去读，读完归还。我把这看作极大的便利，尽量加以利用。

paras.e: My pamphlet by some means falling into the hands of one Lyons, a surgeon, author of a book entitled "The Infallibility of Human Judgment," it occasioned an acquaintance between us. He took great notice of me, called on me often to converse on those subjects, carried me to the Horns, a pale alehouse in ------ Lane, Cheapside, and introduced me to Dr. Mandeville, author of the "Fable of the Bees," who had a club there, of which he was the soul, being a most facetious, entertaining companion. Lyons, too, introduced me to Dr. Pemberton, at Batson's Coffee-house, who promis'd to give me an opportunity, some time or other, of seeing Sir Isaac Newton, of which I was extreamely desirous; but this never happened.
paras.z: 我的小册子不知怎么落到了一个叫莱昂斯的外科医生手里，他写过一本书，叫《人类判断之确实可靠》；我们因此相识了。他很看重我，常来找我谈这类问题，带我到齐普赛街某巷一家卖淡色麦酒的“号角”酒店去，把我介绍给《蜜蜂的寓言》的作者曼德维尔博士。曼德维尔在那里有一个俱乐部，他是其中的灵魂人物，是个极其诙谐有趣的伙伴。莱昂斯还在巴特森咖啡馆把我介绍给彭伯顿博士，他答应哪一天给我一个机会见见艾萨克·牛顿爵士，这是我极其渴望的；可是这件事始终没有实现。

paras.e: I had brought over a few curiosities, among which the principal was a purse made of the asbestos, which purifies by fire. Sir Hans Sloane heard of it, came to see me, and invited me to his house in Bloomsbury Square, where he show'd me all his curiosities, and persuaded me to let him add that to the number, for which he paid me handsomely.
paras.z: 我带来了几件珍奇的东西，其中最主要的是一只石棉做的钱袋，可以用火来烧净。汉斯·斯隆爵士听说了，就来看我，请我到他在布卢姆斯伯里广场的家里去，给我看了他全部的珍藏，并且说服我把那只钱袋让给他添进去，为此付了我一笔很可观的钱。

paras.e: In our house there lodg'd a young woman, a milliner, who, I think, had a shop in the Cloisters. She had been genteelly bred, was sensible and lively, and of most pleasing conversation. Ralph read plays to her in the evenings, they grew intimate, she took another lodging, and he followed her. They liv'd together some time; but, he being still out of business, and her income not sufficient to maintain them with her child, he took a resolution of going from London, to try for a country school, which he thought himself well qualified to undertake, as he wrote an excellent hand, and was a master of arithmetic and accounts. This, however, he deemed a business below him, and confident of future better fortune, when he should be unwilling to have it known that he once was so meanly employed, he changed his name, and did me the honor to assume mine; for I soon after had a letter from him, acquainting me that he was settled in a small village (in Berkshire, I think it was, where he taught reading and writing to ten or a dozen boys, at sixpence each per week), recommending Mrs. T------ to my care, and desiring me to write to him, directing for Mr. Franklin, schoolmaster, at such a place.
paras.z: 我们那所房子里住着一个年轻女子，是做女帽的，我想她在回廊街有一间铺子。她受过上等人家的教养，明白事理，性情活泼，谈吐非常讨人喜欢。拉尔夫晚上给她念剧本，两人亲密起来；她另租了一处住所，他也跟了去。他们同居了一段时间；可是他仍然没有事做，她的收入又不够养活他们两人和她的孩子，他就决心离开伦敦，到乡下去试着找个教书的差事。他认为自己很能胜任，因为他写得一手好字，又精通算术和账目。不过他觉得这是有失身份的职业，又自信日后会交好运，到那时他不愿让人知道自己曾经干过这样低微的差事，就改了名字，并且赏我脸面，用了我的名字。因为不久以后我就收到他的一封信，告诉我他在一个小村子里安顿下来了（我想是在伯克郡，他在那里教十来个男孩读书写字，每人每星期六便士），把 T 太太托付给我照顾，并且要我给他写信，信封上写某某地方的教师富兰克林先生收。

paras.e: He continued to write frequently, sending me large specimens of an epic poem which he was then composing, and desiring my remarks and corrections. These I gave him from time to time, but endeavor'd rather to discourage his proceeding. One of Young's Satires was then just published. I copy'd and sent him a great part of it, which set in a strong light the folly of pursuing the Muses with any hope of advancement by them. All was in vain; sheets of the poem continued to come by every post. In the mean time, Mrs. T------, having on his account lost her friends and business, was often in distresses, and us'd to send for me, and borrow what I could spare to help her out of them. I grew fond of her company, and, being at that time under no religious restraint, and presuming upon my importance to her, I attempted familiarities (another erratum) which she repuls'd with a proper resentment, and acquainted him with my behaviour. This made a breach between us; and, when he returned again to London, he let me know he thought I had cancell'd all the obligations he had been under to me. So I found I was never to expect his repaying me what I lent to him, or advanc'd for him. This, however, was not then of much consequence, as he was totally unable; and in the loss of his friendship I found myself relieved from a burthen. I now began to think of getting a little money beforehand, and, expecting better work, I left Palmer's to work at Watts's, near Lincoln's Inn Fields, a still greater printing-house. Here I continued all the rest of my stay in London.
paras.z: 他继续常常来信，寄来他正在写的一部史诗的大段样稿，要我提意见、作修改。我不时照办，但更想做的是劝他不要再写下去。那时扬格的一篇《讽刺诗》刚刚出版，我抄了其中的一大段寄给他，那一段把追随缪斯而指望靠她们出头的愚蠢写得淋漓尽致。全都无济于事，每一班邮件照旧送来一页页的诗稿。这期间，T 太太因为他的缘故失去了朋友和生意，常常陷入窘境，总是派人来找我，向我借一点我匀得出的钱来渡过难关。我渐渐喜欢同她在一起；那时我不受任何宗教的约束，又仗着自己对她有用，就试图同她亲近（又一个“印刷错误”）。她理所当然地生了气，拒绝了我，并且把我的行为告诉了他。这使我们之间有了裂痕；他回到伦敦以后，让我知道，他认为我已经把他欠我的一切情分都一笔勾销了。于是我明白，我借给他的、替他垫付的那些钱，是永远别想他还了。不过这在当时也没有多大关系，因为他根本还不起；而失去了他的友谊，我倒觉得卸下了一个包袱。这时我开始想到要预先攒一点钱；为了找更好的活计，我离开帕尔默印刷所，到林肯律师学院广场附近的瓦茨印刷所去做工，那是一家更大的印刷所。我在伦敦余下的时间一直在这里。

paras.e: At my first admission into this printing-house I took to working at press, imagining I felt a want of the bodily exercise I had been us'd to in America, where presswork is mix'd with composing. I drank only water; the other workmen, near fifty in number, were great guzzlers of beer. On occasion, I carried up and down stairs a large form of types in each hand, when others carried but one in both hands. They wondered to see, from this and several instances, that the Water-American, as they called me, was stronger than themselves, who drank strong beer! We had an alehouse boy who attended always in the house to supply the workmen. My companion at the press drank every day a pint before breakfast, a pint at breakfast with his bread and cheese, a pint between breakfast and dinner, a pint at dinner, a pint in the afternoon about six o'clock, and another when he had done his day's work. I thought it a detestable custom; but it was necessary, he suppos'd, to drink strong beer, that he might be strong to labor. I endeavored to convince him that the bodily strength afforded by beer could only be in proportion to the grain or flour of the barley dissolved in the water of which it was made; that there was more flour in a pennyworth of bread; and therefore, if he would eat that with a pint of water, it would give him more strength than a quart of beer. He drank on, however, and had four or five shillings to pay out of his wages every Saturday night for that muddling liquor; an expense I was free from. And thus these poor devils keep themselves always under.
paras.z: 我刚进这家印刷所的时候，干的是印刷机上的活，因为我觉得自己缺少在美洲时习惯了的体力活动；在美洲，印刷和排字是掺在一起干的。我只喝水；其余的工人将近五十个，都是啤酒的大酒桶。有时候，我一只手提一大版铅字上下楼梯，别人却要两只手才搬一版。他们从这件事和别的几件事上看到，这个“喝水的美洲人”（他们这样叫我）竟比他们这些喝烈性啤酒的人还有力气，都很诧异！有一个酒店的小伙计常驻在所里，专门给工人供酒。同我一起管印刷机的伙伴每天早饭前喝一品脱，早饭时就着面包和干酪喝一品脱，早饭和午饭之间喝一品脱，午饭时喝一品脱，下午六点左右喝一品脱，一天的活干完了再喝一品脱。我认为这是一种可恶的习惯；可是他以为，要有力气干活，就非喝烈性啤酒不可。我竭力让他明白，啤酒所能给人的体力，只能同酿酒时溶在水里的大麦的谷粒或面粉成比例；一便士的面包里所含的面粉比这还多；所以，如果他吃一便士面包，喝一品脱水，得到的力气会比喝一夸脱啤酒还多。可是他照喝不误，每个星期六晚上都要从工钱里拿出四五个先令来付这种使人昏头的酒钱，这笔开销我是没有的。这些可怜虫就这样让自己永远翻不了身。

paras.e: Watts, after some weeks, desiring to have me in the composing-room, I left the pressmen; a new bien venu or sum for drink, being five shillings, was demanded of me by the compositors. I thought it an imposition, as I had paid below; the master thought so too, and forbad my paying it. I stood out two or three weeks, was accordingly considered as an excommunicate, and had so many little pieces of private mischief done me, by mixing my sorts, transposing my pages, breaking my matter, etc., etc., if I were ever so little out of the room, and all ascribed to the chappel ghost, which they said ever haunted those not regularly admitted, that, notwithstanding the master's protection, I found myself oblig'd to comply and pay the money, convinc'd of the folly of being on ill terms with those one is to live with continually.
paras.z: 几个星期以后，瓦茨想要我到排字间去，我就离开了印刷工那边。排字工们又向我要一笔新的“入伙钱”，也就是酒钱，五个先令。我认为这是敲竹杠，因为我在楼下已经付过了；老板也这样看，不许我付。我顶了两三个星期，结果被当作一个被逐出教门的人，只要我离开房间一小会儿，就有人暗中同我捣许多小鬼：把我的铅字混在一起，把我的版面次序弄乱，把我排好的字弄散，等等，等等，而且全都推到“教堂鬼”身上，说那个鬼专门缠着没有按规矩入伙的人。尽管有老板撑腰，我还是觉得不得不照办，付了这笔钱；我由此明白，同天天要在一起过日子的人闹别扭是愚蠢的。

paras.e: I was now on a fair footing with them, and soon acquir'd considerable influence. I propos'd some reasonable alterations in their chappel [4] laws, and carried them against all opposition. From my example, a great part of them left their muddling breakfast of beer, and bread, and cheese, finding they could with me be suppli'd from a neighboring house with a large porringer of hot water-gruel, sprinkled with pepper, crumbl'd with bread, and a bit of butter in it, for the price of a pint of beer, viz., three half-pence. This was a more comfortable as well as cheaper breakfast, and kept their heads clearer. Those who continued sotting with beer all day, were often, by not paying, out of credit at the alehouse, and us'd to make interest with me to get beer; their light, as they phrased it, being out. I watch'd the pay-table on Saturday night, and collected what I stood engag'd for them, having to pay sometimes near thirty shillings a week on their account. This, and my being esteem'd a pretty good riggite, that is, a jocular verbal satirist, supported my consequence in the society. My constant attendance (I never making a St. Monday) recommended me to the master; and my uncommon quickness at composing occasioned my being put upon all work of dispatch, which was generally better paid. So I went on now very agreeably.
paras.z: 这下我同他们关系融洽了，不久就有了相当大的影响。我对他们的“教堂”[4]规矩提出了几项合理的修改，不顾一切反对让它们通过了。在我的榜样带动下，他们中有很大一部分人不再吃那种啤酒加面包干酪的糊涂早饭，因为他们发现，可以同我一样，从邻近的一家铺子里买到一大碗热腾腾的稀粥，撒上胡椒，掰进面包屑，再加一小块黄油，价钱只抵一品脱啤酒，就是一个半便士。这顿早饭又舒服又便宜，还让他们头脑更清醒。那些仍旧整天泡在啤酒里的人，常常因为付不出钱，在酒店里赊不到账，就来求我替他们担保买酒；用他们的话说，他们的“灯灭了”。星期六晚上我守在发工钱的桌子旁边，把我替他们担保的钱收回来；有时一个星期要替他们垫付将近三十先令。这件事，加上大家认为我是个相当不错的“嘲弄家”，也就是善于用俏皮话挖苦人，使我在这个团体里保住了地位。我从不缺勤（我从来不过“圣星期一”），老板因此看重我；我排字又异常地快，所以凡是急件都派给我，这类活的工钱通常也高些。这样我日子过得很顺心。

paras.e: [4] "A printing-house is always called a chapel by the workmen, the origin of which appears to have been that printing was first carried on in England in an ancient chapel converted into a printing-house, and the title has been preserved by tradition. The bien venu among the printers answers to the terms entrance and footing among mechanics; thus a journeyman, on entering a printing-house, was accustomed to pay one or more gallons of beer for the good of the chapel; this custom was falling into disuse thirty years ago; it is very properly rejected entirely in the United States."--W. T. F.
paras.z: [4] “工人们总是把印刷所称为‘教堂’，其来历似乎是：英国最早的印刷是在一座改作印刷所的古老教堂里进行的，这个名称就沿袭了下来。印刷工人所说的‘入伙钱’相当于其他工匠所说的‘进门钱’；一个熟练工进了一家印刷所，照例要出一加仑或几加仑啤酒的钱，以飨‘教堂’同人。三十年前这个习俗已渐渐废弛，在美国则完全被摒弃了，这是很恰当的。”——威廉·坦普尔·富兰克林注

paras.e: My lodging in Little Britain being too remote, I found another in Duke-street, opposite to the Romish Chapel. It was two pair of stairs backwards, at an Italian warehouse. A widow lady kept the house; she had a daughter, and a maid servant, and a journeyman who attended the warehouse, but lodg'd abroad. After sending to inquire my character at the house where I last lodg'd she agreed to take me in at the same rate, 3s. 6d. per week; cheaper, as she said, from the protection she expected in having a man lodge in the house. She was a widow, an elderly woman; had been bred a Protestant, being a clergyman's daughter, but was converted to the Catholic religion by her husband, whose memory she much revered; had lived much among people of distinction, and knew a thousand anecdotes of them as far back as the times of Charles the Second. She was lame in her knees with the gout, and, therefore, seldom stirred out of her room, so sometimes wanted company; and hers was so highly amusing to me, that I was sure to spend an evening with her whenever she desired it. Our supper was only half an anchovy each, on a very little strip of bread and butter, and half a pint of ale between us; but the entertainment was in her conversation. My always keeping good hours, and giving little trouble in the family, made her unwilling to part with me; so that, when I talk'd of a lodging I had heard of, nearer my business, for two shillings a week, which, intent as I now was on saving money, made some difference, she bid me not think of it, for she would abate me two shillings a week for the future; so I remained with her at one shilling and sixpence as long as I staid in London.
paras.z: 我在小不列颠街的住处太远，就在公爵街另找了一处，对面是天主教的礼拜堂。那是一家意大利货栈的三层楼后间。管房子的是一位寡妇，她有一个女儿和一个女仆，还有一个照看货栈的伙计，但不住在这里。她派人到我原先的住处打听了我的品行，就同意照原来的价钱，每星期三先令六便士，让我住进来；她说，价钱所以便宜，是因为指望家里住一个男人可以有个照应。她是寡妇，上了年纪；她是牧师的女儿，从小受的是新教的教育，后来被丈夫劝得改信了天主教，她对亡夫十分敬重。她在上流人物中间生活过多年，知道他们的许许多多逸事，远的可以讲到查理二世的时代。她因为痛风，两膝不便，很少出房门，所以有时需要人作伴；而同她作伴对我是极大的乐事，只要她愿意，我一定陪她过一个晚上。我们的晚饭不过是每人半条鳀鱼，放在一小条抹了黄油的面包上，两人合喝半品脱麦酒；乐趣全在她的谈话里。我一向早睡早起，很少给这家人添麻烦，所以她舍不得我走。有一回我说起，我听说有一处住所离我做工的地方更近，每星期只要两先令——我那时一心攒钱，这点差别也不算小——她叫我不要动这个念头，说以后每星期给我减去两先令。这样，我在伦敦期间一直住在她那里，每星期一先令六便士。

paras.e: In a garret of her house there lived a maiden lady of seventy, in the most retired manner, of whom my landlady gave me this account: that she was a Roman Catholic, had been sent abroad when young, and lodg'd in a nunnery with an intent of becoming a nun; but, the country not agreeing with her, she returned to England, where, there being no nunnery, she had vow'd to lead the life of a nun, as near as might be done in those circumstances. Accordingly, she had given all her estate to charitable uses, reserving only twelve pounds a year to live on, and out of this sum she still gave a great deal in charity, living herself on water-gruel only, and using no fire but to boil it. She had lived many years in that garret, being permitted to remain there gratis by successive Catholic tenants of the house below, as they deemed it a blessing to have her there. A priest visited her to confess her every day. "I have ask'd her," says my landlady, "how she, as she liv'd, could possibly find so much employment for a confessor?" "Oh," said she, "it is impossible to avoid vain thoughts." I was permitted once to visit her. She was chearful and polite, and convers'd pleasantly. The room was clean, but had no other furniture than a matras, a table with a crucifix and book, a stool which she gave me to sit on, and a picture over the chimney of Saint Veronica displaying her handkerchief, with the miraculous figure of Christ's bleeding face on it, which she explained to me with great seriousness. She look'd pale, but was never sick; and I give it as another instance on how small an income life and health may be supported.
paras.z: 她这所房子的顶楼上住着一位七十岁的老处女，过着极其隐居的生活。房东太太对我讲了她的情形：她是罗马天主教徒，年轻时被送到国外，住在一所女修道院里，打算当修女；可是那个国家的水土同她不合，她就回到英国。英国没有女修道院，她就发愿在这种环境里尽可能过一种修女的生活。为此她把全部财产都捐作慈善之用，只留下每年十二镑维持生活；就是这笔钱，她还拿出很多来施舍，自己只靠稀粥过活，除了煮粥从不生火。她在那间顶楼上住了许多年，楼下历任信天主教的房客都让她白住，认为有她住在那里是一种福气。一位神父每天来听她忏悔。房东太太说：“我问过她，照她那样过日子，怎么可能有那么多事情要劳动听忏悔的神父？”她说：“哦，虚妄的念头是免不了的。”我得到许可去看过她一次。她神情愉快，彬彬有礼，谈吐很讨人喜欢。房间很干净，但除了一张床垫，一张放着十字架和书的桌子，一张她让给我坐的凳子，就没有别的家具了；壁炉上方挂着一幅画，画的是圣维罗尼卡展开她的手帕，上面有基督流血的面容显出的神迹。她十分郑重地向我解释了这幅画。她脸色苍白，但从来不生病。我举这件事作为又一个例子，说明多么微薄的收入就可以维持生命和健康。

paras.e: At Watts's printing-house I contracted an acquaintance with an ingenious young man, one Wygate, who, having wealthy relations, had been better educated than most printers; was a tolerable Latinist, spoke French, and lov'd reading. I taught him and a friend of his to swim at twice going into the river, and they soon became good swimmers. They introduc'd me to some gentlemen from the country, who went to Chelsea by water to see the College and Don Saltero's curiosities. In our return, at the request of the company, whose curiosity Wygate had excited, I stripped and leaped into the river, and swam from near Chelsea to Blackfryar's, performing on the way many feats of activity, both upon and under water, that surpris'd and pleas'd those to whom they were novelties.
paras.z: 在瓦茨印刷所，我结识了一个聪明的青年，名叫怀盖特。他有阔亲戚，所以受的教育比大多数印刷工人好；拉丁文还过得去，会说法语，喜欢读书。我只同他和他的一个朋友下了两次河，就教会了他们游泳，他们很快都成了游泳好手。他们把我介绍给几位从乡下来的绅士，这几位坐船去切尔西参观学院和“萨尔特罗先生”的珍奇陈列。回来的路上，同船的人被怀盖特说得起了好奇心，要我表演，我就脱了衣服跳进河里，从切尔西附近一直游到黑衣修士桥，一路上在水面和水下表演了许多花样，使那些没见过的人又惊又喜。

paras.e: I had from a child been ever delighted with this exercise, had studied and practis'd all Thevenot's motions and positions, added some of my own, aiming at the graceful and easy as well as the useful. All these I took this occasion of exhibiting to the company, and was much flatter'd by their admiration; and Wygate, who was desirous of becoming a master, grew more and more attach'd to me on that account, as well as from the similarity of our studies. He at length proposed to me travelling all over Europe together, supporting ourselves everywhere by working at our business. I was once inclined to it; but, mentioning it to my good friend Mr. Denham, with whom I often spent an hour when I had leisure, he dissuaded me from it, advising me to think only of returning to Pennsilvania, which he was now about to do.
paras.z: 我从小就一直喜欢这项运动，研究并练习过泰弗诺书中的全部动作和姿势，自己又添了一些，力求既实用，又优美自如。这一回我借机把这些全都表演给同船的人看，他们的赞叹使我十分得意。怀盖特很想成为游泳的行家，为了这个缘故，也因为我们钻研的东西相近，同我越来越亲近。后来他向我提议一起周游欧洲，到处靠干本行的活计维持生活。我一度动了心；可是我把这件事对我的好朋友德纳姆先生说了——我有空常去同他待上一个钟头——他劝我打消这个念头，要我只想着回宾夕法尼亚，他自己这时正要回去。

paras.e: I must record one trait of this good man's character. He had formerly been in business at Bristol, but failed in debt to a number of people, compounded and went to America. There, by a close application to business as a merchant, he acquir'd a plentiful fortune in a few years. Returning to England in the ship with me, he invited his old creditors to an entertainment, at which he thank'd them for the easy composition they had favored him with, and, when they expected nothing but the treat, every man at the first remove found under his plate an order on a banker for the full amount of the unpaid remainder with interest.
paras.z: 我一定要记下这位好人品格上的一件事。他从前在布里斯托尔做生意，破了产，欠了许多人的债，同债主达成了折偿的协议，然后去了美洲。在那里，他专心致志地经商，几年工夫就挣了一份丰厚的家产。他同我乘一条船回到英国，请他的老债主们来赴宴；席间他感谢他们当初宽厚，肯同他折偿了事。债主们原以为不过是吃一顿饭，谁知头一道菜撤下去的时候，每个人都在自己的盘子底下发现了一张银行汇票，数目是当年没有还清的余款，外加利息。

paras.e: He now told me he was about to return to Philadelphia, and should carry over a great quantity of goods in order to open a store there. He propos'd to take me over as his clerk, to keep his books, in which he would instruct me, copy his letters, and attend the store. He added that, as soon as I should be acquainted with mercantile business, he would promote me by sending me with a cargo of flour and bread, etc., to the West Indies, and procure me commissions from others which would be profitable; and, if I manag'd well, would establish me handsomely. The thing pleas'd me; for I was grown tired of London, remembered with pleasure the happy months I had spent in Pennsylvania, and wish'd again to see it; therefore I immediately agreed on the terms of fifty pounds a year, Pennsylvania money; less, indeed, than my present gettings as a compositor, but affording a better prospect.
paras.z: 这时他告诉我，他就要回费城，要带大批货物过去，在那里开一家铺子。他提议带我过去当他的伙计，替他记账（这个他会教我）、抄写信件、照看铺子。他还说，等我一熟悉了商业上的事，他就要提拔我，派我押一船面粉、面包之类的货到西印度群岛去，并且替我向别人揽些有利可图的代办生意；如果我干得好，他会让我体体面面地自立门户。这件事我很中意；因为我对伦敦已经厌倦了，愉快地回想起在宾夕法尼亚度过的那几个月的好日子，很想再见到那个地方。所以我当即答应了，条件是年薪五十镑宾夕法尼亚币；这的确比我眼下当排字工挣的少，但前景更好。

paras.e: I now took leave of printing, as I thought, for ever, and was daily employed in my new business, going about with Mr. Denham among the tradesmen to purchase various articles, and seeing them pack'd up, doing errands, calling upon workmen to dispatch, etc.; and, when all was on board, I had a few days' leisure. On one of these days, I was, to my surprise, sent for by a great man I knew only by name, a Sir William Wyndham, and I waited upon him. He had heard by some means or other of my swimming from Chelsea to Blackfriar's, and of my teaching Wygate and another young man to swim in a few hours. He had two sons, about to set out on their travels; he wish'd to have them first taught swimming, and proposed to gratify me handsomely if I would teach them. They were not yet come to town, and my stay was uncertain, so I could not undertake it; but, from this incident, I thought it likely that, if I were to remain in England and open a swimming-school, I might get a good deal of money; and it struck me so strongly, that, had the overture been sooner made me, probably I should not so soon have returned to America. After many years, you and I had something of more importance to do with one of these sons of Sir William Wyndham, become Earl of Egremont, which I shall mention in its place.
paras.z: 于是我告别了印刷这一行——我当时以为是永远告别了——每天忙着我的新差事：跟着德纳姆先生到各个商人那里采购各种货物，看着装箱，跑腿办事，催工人赶活，等等。货物全部装上船以后，我有了几天空闲。就在这几天里，有一天，出乎我的意料，一位我只闻其名的大人物威廉·温德姆爵士派人来叫我，我就去拜见了他。他不知从哪里听说了我从切尔西游到黑衣修士桥的事，还听说我只用几个钟头就教会了怀盖特和另一个青年游泳。他有两个儿子，即将出门游历；他想让他们先学会游泳，提出如果我肯教他们，他会重重地酬谢我。可是他们还没有到伦敦，我又不知道还能待多久，所以无法应承。不过从这件事我想到，如果我留在英国开一所游泳学校，很可能赚到不少钱。这个念头给我的印象非常强烈，要是这个提议来得早一些，我大概就不会那么快回美洲了。许多年以后，你和我同威廉·温德姆爵士的这两个儿子之一，也就是后来的埃格雷蒙特伯爵，有过更为重要的交道，这我到时候再说。

paras.e: Thus I spent about eighteen months in London; most part of the time I work'd hard at my business, and spent but little upon myself except in seeing plays and in books. My friend Ralph had kept me poor; he owed me about twenty-seven pounds, which I was now never likely to receive; a great sum out of my small earnings! I lov'd him, notwithstanding, for he had many amiable qualities. I had by no means improv'd my fortune; but I had picked up some very ingenious acquaintance, whose conversation was of great advantage to me; and I had read considerably.
paras.z: 这样我在伦敦过了大约十八个月。大部分时间我都勤勤恳恳地干本行的活，除了看戏和买书，在自己身上花钱很少。我的朋友拉尔夫让我一直穷着；他欠我大约二十七镑，这笔钱现在看来是永远收不回来了。在我那点微薄的收入里，这是很大的一笔！尽管如此，我还是喜欢他，因为他有许多可爱的地方。我的境况一点也没有改善；可是我结识了几位很有才智的人，同他们谈话使我获益不浅；我也读了相当多的书。

paras.e: We sail'd from Gravesend on the 23d of July, 1726. For the incidents of the voyage, I refer you to my Journal, where you will find them all minutely related. Perhaps the most important part of that journal is the plan [5] to be found in it, which I formed at sea, for regulating my future conduct in life. It is the more remarkable, as being formed when I was so young, and yet being pretty faithfully adhered to quite thro' to old age.
paras.z: 1726 年 7 月 23 日，我们从格雷夫森德启航。航行中的种种经过，你可以去看我的《日记》，在那里都有详细的记载。那本日记里最重要的部分，也许是我在海上拟定的那份规范我今后一生行为的计划[5]。它是我在那样年轻的时候拟定的，而我直到老年都相当忠实地遵行了它，这就更值得一提了。

paras.e: [5] The "Journal" was printed by Sparks, from a copy made at Reading in 1787. But it does not contain the Plan.--Ed.
paras.z: [5] 这本《日记》由斯帕克斯根据 1787 年在雷丁抄录的一个副本印行，但其中并没有这份计划。——编者注

paras.e: We landed in Philadelphia on the 11th of October, where I found sundry alterations. Keith was no longer governor, being superseded by Major Gordon. I met him walking the streets as a common citizen. He seem'd a little asham'd at seeing me, but pass'd without saying anything. I should have been as much asham'd at seeing Miss Read, had not her friends, despairing with reason of my return after the receipt of my letter, persuaded her to marry another, one Rogers, a potter, which was done in my absence. With him, however, she was never happy, and soon parted from him, refusing to cohabit with him or bear his name, it being now said that he had another wife. He was a worthless fellow, tho' an excellent workman, which was the temptation to her friends. He got into debt, ran away in 1727 or 1728, went to the West Indies, and died there. Keimer had got a better house, a shop well supply'd with stationery, plenty of new types, a number of hands, tho' none good, and seem'd to have a great deal of business.
paras.z: 我们在 10 月 11 日在费城上岸，我发现那里有了种种变化。基思已经不是总督，由戈登少校接替了。我遇见他像个普通市民一样在街上走。他见了我似乎有点惭愧，但一句话也没说就走过去了。我见了里德小姐本来也该同样惭愧，可是她的亲友收到我的信以后，认为我不会回来了——这也难怪——就劝她嫁了别人，一个姓罗杰斯的陶工，婚事是在我不在的时候办的。可是她同他在一起从来没有幸福过，不久就离开了他，不肯同他同居，也不肯用他的姓，因为这时有人说他另有一个妻子。他是个一无是处的家伙，手艺却很出色，她的亲友看中的就是这一点。他欠了债，在 1727 年或 1728 年逃走了，去了西印度群岛，死在那里。凯默换了一所好些的房子，开了一间文具齐全的铺子，添了大量新铅字，雇了好些工人，虽然没有一个是好手；看样子他生意很多。

paras.e: Mr. Denham took a store in Water-street, where we open'd our goods; I attended the business diligently, studied accounts, and grew, in a little time, expert at selling. We lodg'd and boarded together; he counsell'd me as a father, having a sincere regard for me. I respected and lov'd him, and we might have gone on together very happy; but, in the beginning of February, 1726-7, when I had just pass'd my twenty-first year, we both were taken ill. My distemper was a pleurisy, which very nearly carried me off. I suffered a good deal, gave up the point in my own mind, and was rather disappointed when I found myself recovering, regretting, in some degree, that I must now, some time or other, have all that disagreeable work to do over again. I forget what his distemper was; it held him a long time, and at length carried him off. He left me a small legacy in a nuncupative will, as a token of his kindness for me, and he left me once more to the wide world; for the store was taken into the care of his executors, and my employment under him ended.
paras.z: 德纳姆先生在水街租了一间铺面，我们在那里摆出了货物。我兢兢业业地照看生意，学习记账，不多久就成了卖货的行家。我们同吃同住；他像父亲一样指点我，真心看重我。我敬他爱他，本来我们可以这样很快活地一起干下去。可是 1727 年 2 月初，我刚满二十一岁，我们两个都病倒了。我得的是胸膜炎，差一点送了命。我受了很多苦，心里已经放弃了；后来发觉自己在好起来，倒有点失望，多少有些遗憾：这桩不愉快的差事，我总有一天还得从头再来一遍。他得的是什么病我忘了；他病了很久，终于不起。他在口头遗嘱里留给我一笔小小的遗赠，以表示他对我的厚意；他也又一次把我抛给了茫茫人世，因为铺子由他的遗嘱执行人接管，我在他手下的差事就此结束了。

paras.e: My brother-in-law, Holmes, being now at Philadelphia, advised my return to my business; and Keimer tempted me, with an offer of large wages by the year, to come and take the management of his printing-house, that he might better attend his stationer's shop. I had heard a bad character of him in London from his wife and her friends, and was not fond of having any more to do with him. I tri'd for farther employment as a merchant's clerk; but, not readily meeting with any, I clos'd again with Keimer. I found in his house these hands: Hugh Meredith, a Welsh Pensilvanian, thirty years of age, bred to country work; honest, sensible, had a great deal of solid observation, was something of a reader, but given to drink. Stephen Potts, a young countryman of full age, bred to the same, of uncommon natural parts, and great wit and humor, but a little idle. These he had agreed with at extream low wages per week, to be rais'd a shilling every three months, as they would deserve by improving in their business; and the expectation of these high wages, to come on hereafter, was what he had drawn them in with. Meredith was to work at press, Potts at book-binding, which he, by agreement, was to teach them, though he knew neither one nor t'other. John ------, a wild Irishman, brought up to no business, whose service, for four years, Keimer had purchased from the captain of a ship; he, too, was to be made a pressman. George Webb, an Oxford scholar, whose time for four years he had likewise bought, intending him for a compositor, of whom more presently; and David Harry, a country boy, whom he had taken apprentice.
paras.z: 我的姐夫霍姆斯这时正在费城，劝我重操旧业；凯默也用一年一大笔工钱来引诱我，要我去替他管理印刷所，好让他腾出身来照看他的文具铺。我在伦敦曾从他的妻子和她的朋友那里听说他品行不好，不愿意再同他打交道。我想再找一个商号伙计的差事，可是一时找不到，就又同凯默讲定了。我在他那里见到这样几个人手：休·梅雷迪思，一个威尔士裔的宾夕法尼亚人，三十岁，原是干农活出身；为人诚实，明白事理，颇有实在的见识，也读过些书，就是好喝酒。斯蒂芬·波茨，一个刚成年的乡下青年，也是干农活出身，天资不凡，很有机智和幽默，就是有点懒。这两个人，他讲定每星期给极低的工钱，以后每三个月加一个先令，看他们本行的长进而定；他就是用将来才能拿到的高工钱把他们引来的。梅雷迪思要干印刷，波茨要干装订；照约定这两样都该由凯默来教，可是他哪一样也不会。约翰某某，一个野性的爱尔兰人，什么行当也没学过，凯默从一个船长手里买下了他四年的服务期；他也要被培养成印刷工。乔治·韦布，一个牛津的学生，凯默同样买下了他四年的时间，打算让他当排字工，关于他我下面就要讲到。还有戴维·哈里，一个乡下孩子，是他收的学徒。

paras.e: I soon perceiv'd that the intention of engaging me at wages so much higher than he had been us'd to give, was, to have these raw, cheap hands form'd thro' me; and, as soon as I had instructed them, then they being all articled to him, he should be able to do without me. I went on, however, very cheerfully, put his printing-house in order, which had been in great confusion, and brought his hands by degrees to mind their business and to do it better.
paras.z: 我很快看出，他肯出比平常高得多的工钱雇我，用意是要通过我把这些又生疏又便宜的人手训练出来；一旦我把他们教会了，他们又都同他订了契约，他就可以不要我了。不过我还是高高兴兴地干下去，把他那乱成一团的印刷所整顿得井井有条，让他的工人渐渐用心干活，而且干得更好。

paras.e: It was an odd thing to find an Oxford scholar in the situation of a bought servant. He was not more than eighteen years of age, and gave me this account of himself; that he was born in Gloucester, educated at a grammar-school there, had been distinguish'd among the scholars for some apparent superiority in performing his part, when they exhibited plays; belong'd to the Witty Club there, and had written some pieces in prose and verse, which were printed in the Gloucester newspapers; thence he was sent to Oxford; where he continued about a year, but not well satisfi'd, wishing of all things to see London, and become a player. At length, receiving his quarterly allowance of fifteen guineas, instead of discharging his debts he walk'd out of town, hid his gown in a furze bush, and footed it to London, where, having no friend to advise him, he fell into bad company, soon spent his guineas, found no means of being introduc'd among the players, grew necessitous, pawn'd his cloaths, and wanted bread. Walking the street very hungry, and not knowing what to do with himself, a crimp's bill was put into his hand, offering immediate entertainment and encouragement to such as would bind themselves to serve in America. He went directly, sign'd the indentures, was put into the ship, and came over, never writing a line to acquaint his friends what was become of him. He was lively, witty, good-natur'd, and a pleasant companion, but idle, thoughtless, and imprudent to the last degree.
paras.z: 一个牛津的学生竟落到卖身为仆的地步，是件稀奇事。他不过十八岁，对我讲了他的身世：他生在格洛斯特，在当地的一所文法学校读书，学生们演戏的时候，他演得明显比别人出色，因此出了名；他是当地“才子会”的成员，写过一些散文和诗，登在格洛斯特的报纸上。后来他被送到牛津，在那里待了大约一年，但是不大满意，一心只想去看看伦敦，当一名演员。终于有一回，他领到一个季度的津贴十五个几尼，没有拿去还债，却走出了城，把学袍藏在一丛荆豆里，步行去了伦敦。在那里没有朋友给他出主意，他结交了坏人，很快把钱花光了，又找不到门路进戏班子，日子越来越窘，把衣服也当了，连面包也吃不上。他饿着肚子在街上走，不知如何是好，这时有人把一张拐卖人口的贩子的传单塞到他手里，上面说，凡是愿意立契到美洲去服役的人，马上可以得到吃住和优待。他立刻去了，签了契约，被送上了船，就这样过了海，没有写过一个字告诉亲友他的下落。他活泼、机智、脾气好，是个讨人喜欢的伙伴，但是懒散，不动脑筋，轻率到了极点。

paras.e: John, the Irishman, soon ran away; with the rest I began to live very agreeably, for they all respected me the more, as they found Keimer incapable of instructing them, and that from me they learned something daily. We never worked on Saturday, that being Keimer's Sabbath, so I had two days for reading. My acquaintance with ingenious people in the town increased. Keimer himself treated me with great civility and apparent regard, and nothing now made me uneasy but my debt to Vernon, which I was yet unable to pay, being hitherto but a poor œconomist. He, however, kindly made no demand of it.
paras.z: 那个爱尔兰人约翰不久就逃跑了。我同其余的人开始相处得很愉快，因为他们发现凯默没有本事教他们，而从我这里每天都能学到点东西，就更加敬重我。我们星期六从不做工，因为那是凯默的安息日，所以我有两天可以读书。我在镇上结识的有才智的人越来越多。凯默本人待我也很客气，显得很看重我。这时没有什么事让我不安，只有欠弗农的那笔债；我一向不会理财，还没有能力还。不过他很宽厚，并没有来讨。

paras.e: Our printing-house often wanted sorts, and there was no letter-founder in America; I had seen types cast at James's in London, but without much attention to the manner; however, I now contrived a mould, made use of the letters we had as puncheons, struck the matrices in lead, And thus supply'd in a pretty tolerable way all deficiencies. I also engrav'd several things on occasion; I made the ink; I was warehouseman, and everything, and, in short, quite a factotum.
paras.z: 我们的印刷所常常缺某些铅字，而美洲没有铸字匠。我在伦敦的詹姆斯铸字所见过人家铸字，只是当时没有怎么留心方法。不过我现在想法子做了一个模子，拿我们现有的铅字当冲头，在铅上冲出字模，就这样勉强补足了所有短缺的字。我有时还雕刻些东西；油墨是我做的；我又是仓库管理员，什么都干，总之，完全是个万能的杂役。

paras.e: But, however serviceable I might be, I found that my services became every day of less importance, as the other hands improv'd in the business; and, when Keimer paid my second quarter's wages, he let me know that he felt them too heavy, and thought I should make an abatement. He grew by degrees less civil, put on more of the master, frequently found fault, was captious, and seem'd ready for an outbreaking. I went on, nevertheless, with a good deal of patience, thinking that his encumber'd circumstances were partly the cause. At length a trifle snapt our connections; for, a great noise happening near the court-house, I put my head out of the window to see what was the matter. Keimer, being in the street, look'd up and saw me, call'd out to me in a loud voice and angry tone to mind my business, adding some reproachful words, that nettled me the more for their publicity, all the neighbors who were looking out on the same occasion being witnesses how I was treated. He came up immediately into the printing-house, continu'd the quarrel, high words pass'd on both sides, he gave me the quarter's warning we had stipulated, expressing a wish that he had not been oblig'd to so long a warning. I told him his wish was unnecessary, for I would leave him that instant; and so, taking my hat, walk'd out of doors, desiring Meredith, whom I saw below, to take care of some things I left, and bring them to my lodgings.
paras.z: 可是，不管我多么有用，我发现，随着别的工人本事长进，我的作用一天比一天不重要了。凯默付我第二个季度的工钱的时候，让我知道他觉得这笔钱太重，认为我应该减一些。他渐渐地不那么客气了，越发摆出老板的架子，常常挑毛病，吹毛求疵，看样子随时都会发作。尽管如此，我还是相当耐心地干下去，心想他处境窘迫也是一部分原因。最后，一件小事断了我们的关系。有一回，法院附近传来很大的喧闹声，我把头伸出窗外，看看出了什么事。凯默正在街上，抬头看见了我，就用很响的嗓门、很生气的口吻冲我喊，叫我干自己的活去，还加了几句责骂的话。这些话因为是当众说的，更使我恼火；所有为了同一件事探出头来的邻居，都亲眼看到了我受的是什么待遇。他马上上楼进了印刷所，接着吵下去，双方都说了些很难听的话。他按我们的约定给了我提前一个季度的解雇通知，还说但愿他当初没有答应要提前这么久。我对他说，他用不着这样但愿，因为我立刻就走。说着我拿起帽子，走出了门，看见梅雷迪思在楼下，就请他照看我留下的几样东西，替我送到我的住处去。

paras.e: Meredith came accordingly in the evening, when we talked my affair over. He had conceiv'd a great regard for me, and was very unwilling that I should leave the house while he remain'd in it. He dissuaded me from returning to my native country, which I began to think of; he reminded me that Keimer was in debt for all he possess'd; that his creditors began to be uneasy; that he kept his shop miserably, sold often without profit for ready money, and often trusted without keeping accounts; that he must therefore fall, which would make a vacancy I might profit of. I objected my want of money. He then let me know that his father had a high opinion of me, and, from some discourse that had pass'd between them, he was sure would advance money to set us up, if I would enter into partnership with him. "My time," says he, "will be out with Keimer in the spring; by that time we may have our press and types in from London. I am sensible I am no workman; if you like it, your skill in the business shall be set against the stock I furnish, and we will share the profits equally."
paras.z: 梅雷迪思晚上果然来了，我们把我的事商量了一番。他对我已经十分敬重，很不愿意在他还留在那里的时候我离开那家印刷所。我那时开始想回故乡去，他劝我不要这样做。他提醒我，凯默的全部家当都是欠着债的；他的债主已经开始不安；他那间铺子经营得一塌糊涂，为了现钱常常不赚钱就卖，赊账又常常不记账；所以他非垮不可，那时就会留出一个空当，我正可以利用。我说我没有钱。他这才告诉我，他父亲对我评价很高，从他们父子之间谈过的一些话来看，他确信，只要我肯同他合伙，他父亲会垫钱让我们开业。他说：“到明年春天，我同凯默的契约就满期了；到那时候，我们的印刷机和铅字也可以从伦敦运到了。我知道自己不是个好工人；如果你愿意，就拿你在这一行的本事抵我出的本钱，利润我们平分。”

paras.e: The proposal was agreeable, and I consented; his father was in town and approv'd of it; the more as he saw I had great influence with his son, had prevail'd on him to abstain long from dram-drinking, and he hop'd might break him off that wretched habit entirely, when we came to be so closely connected. I gave an inventory to the father, who carry'd it to a merchant; the things were sent for, the secret was to be kept till they should arrive, and in the mean time I was to get work, if I could, at the other printing-house. But I found no vacancy there, and so remain'd idle a few days, when Keimer, on a prospect of being employ'd to print some paper money in New Jersey, which would require cuts and various types that I only could supply, and apprehending Bradford might engage me and get the jobb from him, sent me a very civil message, that old friends should not part for a few words, the effect of sudden passion, and wishing me to return. Meredith persuaded me to comply, as it would give more opportunity for his improvement under my daily instructions; so I return'd, and we went on more smoothly than for some time before. The New Jersey jobb was obtain'd, I contriv'd a copperplate press for it, the first that had been seen in the country; I cut several ornaments and checks for the bills. We went together to Burlington, where I executed the whole to satisfaction; and he received so large a sum for the work as to be enabled thereby to keep his head much longer above water.
paras.z: 这个提议很合我意，我就答应了。他父亲正在城里，也表示赞成；尤其因为他看到我对他儿子影响很大，已经劝得他很久不喝烈酒，他希望等我们关系这样密切以后，我能让他把那个糟糕的习惯彻底戒掉。我给他父亲开了一张清单，他拿去交给一个商人，货就这样订了。在货运到之前要保守秘密；这期间，如果可能，我就到另一家印刷所去找活干。可是那里没有空缺，我就闲了几天。这时凯默有望揽到替新泽西印纸币的差事，那需要刻版和各种铅字，只有我才办得了；他又怕布拉德福德雇了我，把这笔生意从他手里抢走，就捎了一个很客气的口信给我，说老朋友不该为了一时气头上的几句话就分手，希望我回去。梅雷迪思劝我答应，因为这样他在我每天的指点下可以有更多的机会长进。于是我回去了，我们相处得比前一阵子顺当多了。新泽西的那笔生意揽到了，我为它设计了一台铜版印刷机，这是当地见到的头一台；我还为钞票刻了几种花饰和防伪标记。我们一起去了伯灵顿，我在那里把全部工作做得令人满意；他从这件活上拿到很大一笔钱，因此又多撑了好些时候没有垮。

paras.e: At Burlington I made an acquaintance with many principal people of the province. Several of them had been appointed by the Assembly a committee to attend the press, and take care that no more bills were printed than the law directed. They were therefore, by turns, constantly with us, and generally he who attended, brought with him a friend or two for company. My mind having been much more improv'd by reading than Keimer's, I suppose it was for that reason my conversation seem'd to be more valu'd. They had me to their houses, introduced me to their friends, and show'd me much civility; while he, tho' the master, was a little neglected. In truth, he was an odd fish; ignorant of common life, fond of rudely opposing receiv'd opinions, slovenly to extream dirtiness, enthusiastic in some points of religion, and a little knavish withal.
paras.z: 在伯灵顿，我结识了这个殖民地的许多头面人物。其中有几位是议会指派的委员，负责监督印刷，留意所印的钞票不得超过法律规定的数目。因此他们轮流不断地同我们在一起，来值班的人通常还带一两个朋友作伴。我因为读书，头脑比凯默开通得多，我想就是为了这个缘故，他们似乎更看重同我谈话。他们请我到家里去，把我介绍给他们的朋友，对我十分客气；而他虽然是老板，却有点受冷落。说实在的，他是个怪人：不懂日常的人情世故，喜欢粗鲁地反对公认的见解，邋遢到了极其肮脏的地步，在宗教的某些问题上很狂热，而且还有点无赖。

paras.e: We continu'd there near three months; and by that time I could reckon among my acquired friends, Judge Allen, Samuel Bustill, the secretary of the Province, Isaac Pearson, Joseph Cooper, and several of the Smiths, members of Assembly, and Isaac Decow, the surveyor-general. The latter was a shrewd, sagacious old man, who told me that he began for himself, when young, by wheeling clay for the brick-makers, learned to write after he was of age, carri'd the chain for surveyors, who taught him surveying, and he had now by his industry, acquir'd a good estate; and says he, "I foresee that you will soon work this man out of business, and make a fortune in it at Philadelphia." He had not then the least intimation of my intention to set up there or anywhere. These friends were afterwards of great use to me, as I occasionally was to some of them. They all continued their regard for me as long as they lived.
paras.z: 我们在那里待了将近三个月。到那时候，我可以算作新交的朋友有：艾伦法官，殖民地秘书塞缪尔·巴斯蒂尔，艾萨克·皮尔逊，约瑟夫·库珀，史密斯家的好几位（都是议会议员），还有测量总监艾萨克·德科。最后这一位是个精明睿智的老人，他告诉我，他年轻时自己谋生，起初是替砖瓦匠推黏土，成年以后才学会写字，替测量员拉测链，他们教了他测量，如今他凭着勤劳挣下了一份不错的家产。他说：“我看得出来，你不久就会把这个人挤出这一行，在费城靠这一行发财。”那时他丝毫不知道我有在费城或别处开业的打算。这些朋友后来对我大有用处，我有时对他们中的几位也有用处。他们终其一生都一直看重我。

paras.e: Before I enter upon my public appearance in business, it may be well to let you know the then state of my mind with regard to my principles and morals, that you may see how far those influenc'd the future events of my life. My parents had early given me religious impressions, and brought me through my childhood piously in the Dissenting way. But I was scarce fifteen, when, after doubting by turns of several points, as I found them disputed in the different books I read, I began to doubt of Revelation itself. Some books against Deism fell into my hands; they were said to be the substance of sermons preached at Boyle's Lectures. It happened that they wrought an effect on me quite contrary to what was intended by them; for the arguments of the Deists, which were quoted to be refuted, appeared to me much stronger than the refutations; in short, I soon became a thorough Deist. My arguments perverted some others, particularly Collins and Ralph; but, each of them having afterwards wrong'd me greatly without the least compunction, and recollecting Keith's conduct towards me (who was another freethinker), and my own towards Vernon and Miss Read, which at times gave me great trouble, I began to suspect that this doctrine, tho' it might be true, was not very useful. My London pamphlet, which had for its motto these lines of Dryden:
paras.z: 在讲我公开出面经营事业之前，不妨先让你知道我那时在原则和道德方面的心境，好让你看出这些对我后来一生的经历有多大影响。我父母很早就给了我宗教上的熏陶，在整个童年时代按照不从国教者的方式虔诚地教养我。可是我还不到十五岁，因为在读过的各种书里看到好些教义受到争论，就先后对它们起了怀疑，后来竟开始怀疑“启示”本身。有几本反对自然神论的书落到了我手里，据说是波义耳讲座上所讲的布道的要旨。谁知它们对我起的作用同它们的本意恰恰相反；因为书中为了驳斥而引用的自然神论者的论点，在我看来比那些驳斥有力得多。总之，我不久就成了一个彻底的自然神论者。我的议论把另外几个人也引上了歧路，特别是柯林斯和拉尔夫；可是他们两个后来都大大地亏待了我，而且毫无愧疚。我又想起基思（他也是个自由思想者）对我的所作所为，以及我自己对弗农和里德小姐的所作所为——这两件事有时使我十分不安——于是开始怀疑，这种学说虽然也许是真的，却不大有用。我在伦敦写的那本小册子，用德莱顿的这几行诗作题词：

paras.e:
"Whatever is, is right. Though purblind man
    Sees but a part o' the chain, the nearest link:
    His eyes not carrying to the equal beam,
    That poises all above;"
paras.z:
“凡存在的，都是对的。虽然半盲的人
只看见锁链的一段，最近的那一环；
他的眼睛够不着那平衡的秤杆，
是它在上面权衡着一切；”

paras.e: and from the attributes of God, his infinite wisdom, goodness and power, concluded that nothing could possibly be wrong in the world, and that vice and virtue were empty distinctions, no such things existing, appear'd now not so clever a performance as I once thought it; and I doubted whether some error had not insinuated itself unperceiv'd into my argument, so as to infect all that follow'd, as is common in metaphysical reasonings.
paras.z: 并且从上帝的属性，即他无限的智慧、仁慈和权能，推断出世上不可能有什么事是错的，善与恶是空洞的区分，根本没有这样的东西。这本小册子现在看来并不像我当初以为的那样高明了；我怀疑有某种错误不知不觉地混进了我的论证，以致把后面的一切都带坏了，这在形而上学的推理里是常有的事。

paras.e: I grew convinc'd that truth, sincerity and integrity in dealings between man and man were of the utmost importance to the felicity of life; and I form'd written resolutions, which still remain in my journal book, to practice them ever while I lived. Revelation had indeed no weight with me, as such; but I entertain'd an opinion that, though certain actions might not be bad because they were forbidden by it, or good because it commanded them, yet probably these actions might be forbidden because they were bad for us, or commanded because they were beneficial to us, in their own natures, all the circumstances of things considered. And this persuasion, with the kind hand of Providence, or some guardian angel, or accidental favorable circumstances and situations, or all together, preserved me, thro' this dangerous time of youth, and the hazardous situations I was sometimes in among strangers, remote from the eye and advice of my father, without any willful gross immorality or injustice, that might have been expected from my want of religion. I say willful, because the instances I have mentioned had something of necessity in them, from my youth, inexperience, and the knavery of others. I had therefore a tolerable character to begin the world with; I valued it properly, and determin'd to preserve it.
paras.z: 我渐渐确信，人与人交往中的真实、诚恳和正直，对人生的幸福至关重要；我写下了决心，要终身实行，这些话至今还留在我的日记本里。“启示”本身对我确实没有什么分量；但我有这样一种看法：某些行为，也许并不因为“启示”禁止它们就是坏的，也不因为“启示”命令它们就是好的；可是，把事物的各种情形全都考虑进去，这些行为很可能是因为本质上对我们有害才被禁止，因为本质上对我们有益才被命令。这种信念，加上上天仁慈的援手，或者某位守护天使，或者偶然碰上的有利的环境和处境，或者这一切合在一起，保全了我，使我度过了青年时代那段危险的时期，度过了我有时身处陌生人中间、远离父亲的眼睛和劝告的那些冒险的境地，没有犯下任何故意的、重大的不道德或不公正的行为——而以我那样缺乏宗教信仰，本是很可能犯下的。我说“故意的”，是因为我前面提到的那几件事，由于我年轻、没有经验，又由于别人的奸诈，多少带着几分不得已。所以，我踏入社会的时候，名声还算过得去；我恰如其分地珍视它，决心把它保持下去。

paras.e: We had not been long return'd to Philadelphia before the new types arriv'd from London. We settled with Keimer, and left him by his consent before he heard of it. We found a house to hire near the market, and took it. To lessen the rent, which was then but twenty-four pounds a year, tho' I have since known it to let for seventy, we took in Thomas Godfrey, a glazier, and his family, who were to pay a considerable part of it to us, and we to board with them. We had scarce opened our letters and put our press in order, before George House, an acquaintance of mine, brought a countryman to us, whom he had met in the street inquiring for a printer. All our cash was now expended in the variety of particulars we had been obliged to procure, and this countryman's five shillings, being our first-fruits, and coming so seasonably, gave me more pleasure than any crown I have since earned; and the gratitude I felt toward House has made me often more ready than perhaps I should otherwise have been to assist young beginners.
paras.z: 我们回到费城不久，新铅字就从伦敦运到了。我们同凯默结清了账，在他还没有听说这件事之前，征得他的同意离开了他。我们在市场附近找到一所出租的房子，租了下来。那时租金每年只要二十四镑，后来我知道它租到过七十镑。为了减轻租金的负担，我们把一部分房子分租给玻璃匠托马斯·戈弗雷一家，由他们付给我们相当一部分租金，我们则在他们家搭伙。我们刚把铅字拆了包，把印刷机安顿好，我的一个熟人乔治·豪斯就带了一个乡下人来找我们，那人是他在街上碰见的，正在打听哪里有印刷铺。这时我们的现钱已经全花在不得不置办的各色东西上了，这个乡下人的五个先令是我们头一笔进项，来得又那么及时，给我的快乐超过了我后来挣到的任何一块克朗；我对豪斯的感激之情，使我后来常常更乐意帮助初出茅庐的年轻人，否则我也许不会那样乐意。

paras.e: There are croakers in every country, always boding its ruin. Such a one then lived in Philadelphia; a person of note, an elderly man, with a wise look and a very grave manner of speaking; his name was Samuel Mickle. This gentleman, a stranger to me, stopt one day at my door, and asked me if I was the young man who had lately opened a new printing-house. Being answered in the affirmative, he said he was sorry for me, because it was an expensive undertaking, and the expense would be lost; for Philadelphia was a sinking place, the people already half-bankrupts, or near being so; all appearances to the contrary, such as new buildings and the rise of rents, being to his certain knowledge fallacious; for they were, in fact, among the things that would soon ruin us. And he gave me such a detail of misfortunes now existing, or that were soon to exist, that he left me half melancholy. Had I known him before I engaged in this business, probably I never should have done it. This man continued to live in this decaying place, and to declaim in the same strain, refusing for many years to buy a house there, because all was going to destruction; and at last I had the pleasure of seeing him give five times as much for one as he might have bought it for when he first began his croaking.
