paras.z: “秩序”这一项给我的麻烦最多。我发现，如果一个人的工作能让他自己支配时间，比如一个印刷工人，这或许还行得通；可是一个当老板的人，必须同外界来往，常常得按人家方便的时间接待来谈生意的人，就不可能严格遵守了。至于东西、文件之类各有定位这种秩序，我也发现极难养成。我没有从小养成这个习惯，记性又特别好，所以不大感觉得到没有条理的不便。因此这一条费了我极大的心力，我在这方面的过失使我十分烦恼，改进又那么少，旧病复发又那么频繁，我几乎想放弃尝试，在这一点上甘心做一个有缺点的人了。这就像那个向我的邻居、一个铁匠买斧头的人：他要求斧头的整个表面都同斧刃一样亮。铁匠答应替他磨亮，只要他肯摇砂轮。他摇着，铁匠把斧头的宽面使劲重重地压在砂轮上，这使摇轮子变得非常吃力。那人不时离开轮子过来看看活干得怎样了，最后说就这样把斧头拿走，不用再磨了。铁匠说：“不，摇下去，摇下去；我们过一会儿就能把它磨亮了；眼下它还只是斑斑点点的。”那人说：“是的，可是我觉得我最喜欢有斑点的斧头。”我相信许多人大概也是这样：他们因为没有我用的这一类办法，在别的善恶问题上发现养成好习惯、打破坏习惯之难，就放弃了努力，断定“有斑点的斧头最好”。因为有某种冒充理性的东西时时在暗示我：我对自己要求的这种极端的精细，也许是道德上的一种矫揉造作，如果让人知道了会惹人笑话；一个完美的品格也许会带来受人嫉妒和憎恨的不便；一个仁厚的人应当容许自己有几样缺点，好让朋友们不至于难堪。

paras.e: In truth, I found myself incorrigible with respect to Order; and now I am grown old, and my memory bad, I feel very sensibly the want of it. But, on the whole, tho' I never arrived at the perfection I had been so ambitious of obtaining, but fell far short of it, yet I was, by the endeavour, a better and a happier man than I otherwise should have been if I had not attempted it; as those who aim at perfect writing by imitating the engraved copies, tho' they never reach the wish'd-for excellence of those copies, their hand is mended by the endeavor, and is tolerable while it continues fair and legible.
paras.z: 说实话，我发现自己在“秩序”方面是不可救药的；如今我老了，记性不好了，就痛切地感到缺少它的不便。但是总的说来，我虽然从未达到我曾经热切希望达到的那种完善，而且差得很远，但是由于这番努力，我比不作这种尝试时成了一个更好、更幸福的人；正像那些临摹字帖、想把字写得十全十美的人，虽然永远达不到字帖那种他们所期望的精妙，他们的书法却因这番努力而有了改进，只要保持工整清楚，也就过得去了。

paras.e: It may be well my posterity should be informed that to this little artifice, with the blessing of God, their ancestor ow'd the constant felicity of his life, down to his 79th year, in which this is written. What reverses may attend the remainder is in the hand of Providence; but, if they arrive, the reflection on past happiness enjoy'd ought to help his bearing them with more resignation. To Temperance he ascribes his long-continued health, and what is still left to him of a good constitution; to Industry and Frugality, the early easiness of his circumstances and acquisition of his fortune, with all that knowledge that enabled him to be a useful citizen, and obtained for him some degree of reputation among the learned; to Sincerity and Justice, the confidence of his country, and the honorable employs it conferred upon him; and to the joint influence of the whole mass of the virtues, even in the imperfect state he was able to acquire them, all that evenness of temper, and that cheerfulness in conversation, which makes his company still sought for, and agreeable even to his younger acquaintance. I hope, therefore, that some of my descendants may follow the example and reap the benefit.
paras.z: 也许应该让我的后人知道，他们的祖先直到写这段话的七十九岁这一年为止，一生持续的幸福，靠着上帝的保佑，都得自这个小小的办法。余下的岁月会有什么逆转，掌握在上天手里；但如果逆转来了，回想过去享受过的幸福，应当能帮助他更安然地承受。他把自己长久的健康，以及至今还留给他的一副好体格，归功于“节制”；把早年境况的宽裕和财产的获得，以及使他能成为一个有用的公民、并在学者中间得到一些名声的全部知识，归功于“勤勉”和“节俭”；把国家对他的信任以及授予他的光荣职务，归功于“诚恳”和“公正”；而他性情的平和，谈吐的愉快——这使人们至今仍然愿意同他相处，连年轻的相识也觉得同他在一起很愉快——则归功于全部这些美德合在一起的影响，尽管他能做到的还很不完善。所以我希望我的子孙中有人能效法这个榜样，并且得到好处。

paras.e: It will be remark'd that, tho' my scheme was not wholly without religion, there was in it no mark of any of the distinguishing tenets of any particular sect. I had purposely avoided them; for, being fully persuaded of the utility and excellency of my method, and that it might be serviceable to people in all religions, and intending some time or other to publish it, I would not have any thing in it that should prejudice any one, of any sect, against it. I purposed writing a little comment on each virtue, in which I would have shown the advantages of possessing it, and the mischiefs attending its opposite vice; and I should have called my book The Art of Virtue, [7] because it would have shown the means and manner of obtaining virtue, which would have distinguished it from the mere exhortation to be good, that does not instruct and indicate the means, but is like the apostle's man of verbal charity, who only without showing to the naked and hungry how or where they might get clothes or victuals, exhorted them to be fed and clothed.--James ii. 15, 16.
paras.z: 读者会注意到，我的计划虽然不是完全没有宗教，其中却没有任何特定教派的特有教义的痕迹。我是有意避开这些的；因为我完全相信我的方法有用而且出色，对一切宗教的人都可能有益，并且打算有朝一日把它发表，所以不愿意其中有任何东西使任何教派的任何人对它抱有成见。我曾打算给每一项美德写一小段评注，说明具备它的好处，以及与它相反的恶习带来的害处；我本想把这本书叫做《美德的艺术》[7]，因为它要指出获得美德的途径和方法，这使它有别于单纯劝人为善的说教。那种说教并不教人、也不指明途径，倒像使徒所说的那种口头上行善的人，他不指给赤身露体、饥饿的人看怎样或到哪里可以得到衣服和食物，只劝他们吃饱穿暖。——《雅各书》第二章第 15、16 节。

paras.e: [7] Nothing so likely to make a man's fortune as virtue.--[Marg. note.]
paras.z: [7] 没有什么比美德更能使人发家。——［页边注］

paras.e: But it so happened that my intention of writing and publishing this comment was never fulfilled. I did, indeed, from time to time, put down short hints of the sentiments, reasonings, etc., to be made use of in it, some of which I have still by me; but the necessary close attention to private business in the earlier part of my life, and public business since, have occasioned my postponing it; for, it being connected in my mind with a great and extensive project, that required the whole man to execute, and which an unforeseen succession of employs prevented my attending to, it has hitherto remain'd unfinish'd.
paras.z: 可是事有不巧，我写作并出版这篇评注的打算始终没有实现。我确实不时把准备用在里面的想法、推理等等写成简短的提示，其中一些至今还在我手边；但是我早年必须专心于私人的生意，后来又忙于公务，这就使我把它一再推迟。因为在我心里，它是同一个宏大而广泛的计划联系在一起的，那个计划要一个人全力以赴才能实行，而一连串意料不到的职务使我无暇顾及，所以它至今没有完成。

paras.e: In this piece it was my design to explain and enforce this doctrine, that vicious actions are not hurtful because they are forbidden, but forbidden because they are hurtful, the nature of man alone considered; that it was, therefore, every one's interest to be virtuous who wish'd to be happy even in this world; and I should, from this circumstance (there being always in the world a number of rich merchants, nobility, states, and princes, who have need of honest instruments for the management of their affairs, and such being so rare), have endeavored to convince young persons that no qualities were so likely to make a poor man's fortune as those of probity and integrity.
paras.z: 在这部书里，我的意图是阐明并强调这样一个道理：只就人的本性而论，恶行并不是因为被禁止才有害，而是因为有害才被禁止；所以，凡是希望即使在今生也得到幸福的人，做一个有德的人都是对他有利的。我还要根据这样一个情形——世上总有许多富商、贵族、国家和君主，需要诚实的人替他们办理事务，而这样的人又是那样稀少——设法使年轻人相信，没有什么品质比正直和诚实更能使一个穷人发家。

paras.e: My list of virtues contain'd at first but twelve; but a Quaker friend having kindly informed me that I was generally thought proud; that my pride show'd itself frequently in conversation; that I was not content with being in the right when discussing any point, but was overbearing, and rather insolent, of which he convinc'd me by mentioning several instances; I determined endeavouring to cure myself, if I could, of this vice or folly among the rest, and I added Humility to my list, giving an extensive meaning to the word.
paras.z: 我的美德表起初只有十二项；但是一位贵格会的朋友好意地告诉我，人们普遍认为我骄傲；我的骄傲常常在谈话中流露出来；讨论任何问题时，我不满足于自己有理，还要盛气凌人，颇有些傲慢无礼。他举了几个例子，使我信服了。于是我决心，如果可能，也要努力治好自己的这个恶习或者说愚蠢，就在我的表上加了“谦逊”一项，并给这个词以广泛的含义。

paras.e: I cannot boast of much success in acquiring the reality of this virtue, but I had a good deal with regard to the appearance of it. I made it a rule to forbear all direct contradiction to the sentiments of others, and all positive assertion of my own. I even forbid myself, agreeably to the old laws of our Junto, the use of every word or expression in the language that imported a fix'd opinion, such as certainly, undoubtedly, etc., and I adopted, instead of them, I conceive, I apprehend, or I imagine a thing to be so or so; or it so appears to me at present. When another asserted something that I thought an error, I deny'd myself the pleasure of contradicting him abruptly, and of showing immediately some absurdity in his proposition; and in answering I began by observing that in certain cases or circumstances his opinion would be right, but in the present case there appear'd or seem'd to me some difference, etc. I soon found the advantage of this change in my manner; the conversations I engag'd in went on more pleasantly. The modest way in which I propos'd my opinions procur'd them a readier reception and less contradiction; I had less mortification when I was found to be in the wrong, and I more easily prevail'd with others to give up their mistakes and join with me when I happened to be in the right.
paras.z: 我不敢夸口说在养成这项美德的实质上有多大成就，但在它的外表上却大有收获。我给自己定下规矩，决不直接反驳别人的意见，也决不武断地坚持自己的意见。我甚至照我们讲读社的老规矩，禁止自己使用语言中一切表示见解确定不移的字眼，诸如“肯定”“毫无疑问”等等，而代之以“我以为”“我觉得”或者“我想某事是如此这般”，或者“目前在我看来是这样”。别人说了什么我认为错误的话，我克制自己，不去享受当场反驳他、立刻指出他的话有何荒谬的那种痛快；回答的时候，我先说在某些场合或情形下他的意见是对的，但在眼下这件事上，在我看来似乎有些不同，等等。我很快就发现了这样改变态度的好处：我参加的谈话进行得更愉快了。我提出意见时态度谦逊，这些意见就更容易被人接受，更少招来反驳；别人发现我错了，我也不那么难堪；而我碰巧对了的时候，也更容易说服别人放弃他们的错误，站到我这边来。

paras.e: And this mode, which I at first put on with some violence to natural inclination, became at length so easy, and so habitual to me, that perhaps for these fifty years past no one has ever heard a dogmatical expression escape me. And to this habit (after my character of integrity) I think it principally owing that I had early so much weight with my fellow-citizens when I proposed new institutions, or alterations in the old, and so much influence in public councils when I became a member; for I was but a bad speaker, never eloquent, subject to much hesitation in my choice of words, hardly correct in language, and yet I generally carried my points.
paras.z: 这种态度，我起初是相当勉强地违反着天性装出来的，后来竟变得那样容易，那样习惯，也许近五十年来没有人听我说出过一句武断的话。我想，我早年向同胞们提议设立新的机构或者改革旧的机构时所以有那样大的分量，后来当了议员在公共议事机构里所以有那样大的影响，除了我为人正直的名声之外，主要应当归功于这个习惯；因为我只是个蹩脚的演说者，从来不善辞令，选词用字很是迟疑，语言也不大准确，可是我的主张一般都能通过。

paras.e: In reality, there is, perhaps, no one of our natural passions so hard to subdue as pride. Disguise it, struggle with it, beat it down, stifle it, mortify it as much as one pleases, it is still alive, and will every now and then peep out and show itself; you will see it, perhaps, often in this history; for, even if I could conceive that I had compleatly overcome it, I should probably be proud of my humility.
paras.z: 事实上，在我们天生的各种情感里，也许没有哪一种像骄傲那样难以克服。随你怎样掩饰它，同它搏斗，把它打倒，扼住它，压制它，它依然活着，时不时还要探出头来露一露脸；你在这部历史里也许会常常看到它；因为，即使我能设想自己已经完全克服了它，我大概又会为自己的谦逊而骄傲了。

paras.e: [Thus far written at Passy, 1784.]
paras.z: ［以上写于帕西，1784 年。］

paras.e: ["I am now about to write at home, August, 1788, but can not have the help expected from my papers, many of them being lost in the war. I have, however, found the following."] [8]
paras.z: ［“我现在要在家里动笔了，时为 1788 年 8 月，但是得不到原先指望从文件中得到的帮助，因为其中许多已经在战争中遗失。不过我找到了下面这些。”］[8]

paras.e: Having mentioned a great and extensive project which I had conceiv'd, it seems proper that some account should be here given of that project and its object. Its first rise in my mind appears in the following little paper, accidentally preserv'd, viz.:
paras.z: 我既然提到了我曾设想过的一个宏大而广泛的计划，似乎应当在这里讲一讲这个计划和它的目的。它最初在我心里萌生的情形，可以从下面这张偶然保存下来的小纸片上看出来：

paras.e: [8] This is a marginal memorandum.--B.
paras.z: [8] 这是一条页边备忘。——比奇洛注

paras.e: Observations on my reading history, in Library, May 19th, 1731.
paras.z: 1731 年 5 月 19 日，在图书馆读史的感想。

paras.e: "That the great affairs of the world, the wars, revolutions, etc., are carried on and affected by parties.
paras.z: “世界上的大事，战争、革命等等，都是由党派进行并且左右的。

paras.e: "That the view of these parties is their present general interest, or what they take to be such.
paras.z: “这些党派着眼的是他们当前的共同利益，或者他们以为的共同利益。

paras.e: "That the different views of these different parties occasion all confusion.
paras.z: “这些不同党派的不同着眼点，造成了一切混乱。

paras.e: "That while a party is carrying on a general design, each man has his particular private interest in view.
paras.z: “一个党派在推行总的计划的时候，其中每个人都着眼于自己特殊的私利。

paras.e: "That as soon as a party has gain'd its general point, each member becomes intent upon his particular interest; which, thwarting others, breaks that party into divisions, and occasions more confusion.
paras.z: “一个党派一达到它总的目的，每个成员就专心于自己特殊的利益；这种利益同别人的相冲突，就使那个党派四分五裂，造成更多的混乱。

paras.e: "That few in public affairs act from a meer view of the good of their country, whatever they may pretend; and, tho' their actings bring real good to their country, yet men primarily considered that their own and their country's interest was united, and did not act from a principle of benevolence.
paras.z: “在公共事务中，很少有人纯粹从国家的利益着眼而行事，不管他们怎样标榜；虽然他们的行为确实给国家带来了好处，但人们首先考虑的是自己的利益同国家的利益是一致的，并不是出于仁爱的原则而行事。

paras.e: "That fewer still, in public affairs, act with a view to the good of mankind.
paras.z: “在公共事务中，着眼于人类利益而行事的人就更少了。

paras.e: "There seems to me at present to be great occasion for raising a United Party for Virtue, by forming the virtuous and good men of all nations into a regular body, to be govern'd by suitable good and wise rules, which good and wise men may probably be more unanimous in their obedience to, than common people are to common laws.
paras.z: “在我看来，目前很有必要组织一个‘美德联合党’，把各国有德行的好人组成一个正规的团体，用适当的、良好而明智的规则来管理；善良而明智的人服从这些规则，大概会比普通人服从普通的法律更加一致。

paras.e: "I at present think that whoever attempts this aright, and is well qualified, can not fail of pleasing God, and of meeting with success.
paras.z: “我目前认为，凡是用正确的方法尝试这件事，而又很有资格的人，不会不使上帝喜悦，也不会不成功。

paras.e: B. F."
paras.z: 本·富”

paras.e: Revolving this project in my mind, as to be undertaken hereafter, when my circumstances should afford me the necessary leisure, I put down from time to time, on pieces of paper, such thoughts as occurr'd to me respecting it. Most of these are lost; but I find one purporting to be the substance of an intended creed, containing, as I thought, the essentials of every known religion, and being free of every thing that might shock the professors of any religion. It is express'd in these words, viz.:
paras.z: 我在心里反复考虑这个计划，准备等日后我的境况能给我必要的空闲时再着手，就不时把想到的有关念头写在一片片纸上。这些纸片大都遗失了；但我找到一张，据其内容看，是拟议中的一份信条的要旨。照我当时的想法，它包含了一切已知宗教的要义，而没有任何可能冒犯任何宗教信徒的东西。它是用这样几句话表述的：

paras.e: "That there is one God, who made all things.
paras.z: “只有一位上帝，他创造了万物。

paras.e: "That he governs the world by his providence.
paras.z: “他以他的旨意治理世界。

paras.e: "That he ought to be worshiped by adoration, prayer, and thanksgiving.
paras.z: “应当用崇敬、祈祷和感恩来敬拜他。

paras.e: "But that the most acceptable service of God is doing good to man.
paras.z: “但最为上帝所悦纳的侍奉，是对人行善。

paras.e: "That the soul is immortal.
paras.z: “灵魂是不朽的。

paras.e: "And that God will certainly reward virtue and punish vice, either here or hereafter." [9]
paras.z: “上帝必定奖赏美德，惩罚罪恶，不在今生，就在来世。”[9]

paras.e: [9] In the Middle Ages, Franklin, if such a phenomenon as Franklin were possible in the Middle Ages, would probably have been the founder of a monastic order.--B.
paras.z: [9] 在中世纪，富兰克林——假如中世纪可能出现富兰克林这样的人物的话——大概会成为一个修会的创始人。——比奇洛注

paras.e: My ideas at that time were, that the sect should be begun and spread at first among young and single men only; that each person to be initiated should not only declare his assent to such creed, but should have exercised himself with the thirteen weeks' examination and practice of the virtues, as in the before-mention'd model; that the existence of such a society should be kept a secret, till it was become considerable, to prevent solicitations for the admission of improper persons, but that the members should each of them search among his acquaintance for ingenuous, well-disposed youths, to whom, with prudent caution, the scheme should be gradually communicated; that the members should engage to afford their advice, assistance, and support to each other in promoting one another's interests, business, and advancement in life; that, for distinction, we should be call'd The Society of the Free and Easy: free, as being, by the general practice and habit of the virtues, free from the dominion of vice; and particularly by the practice of industry and frugality, free from debt, which exposes a man to confinement, and a species of slavery to his creditors.
paras.z: 我当时的想法是：这个教派起初只在年轻的单身男子中间创立和传播；每一个要入会的人不仅要声明赞同这样的信条，而且要照前面说的那个样式，做过十三个星期的美德自省和实践；这样一个团体的存在要保密，直到它有了相当的规模，以免有人来请求接纳不合适的人；但是每个成员都要在自己的熟人中间寻找天资聪颖、心地善良的青年，谨慎小心地把这个计划逐步透露给他们；成员们要保证彼此提供意见、帮助和支持，促进各人的利益、事业和一生的上进；为了有个名目，我们叫做“自由自在社”——所谓“自由”，是说靠着普遍实行各项美德并养成习惯，摆脱了恶习的统治；尤其是靠着实行勤勉和节俭，摆脱了债务，因为债务使人有被监禁之虞，使人成为债主的某种奴隶。

paras.e: This is as much as I can now recollect of the project, except that I communicated it in part to two young men, who adopted it with some enthusiasm; but my then narrow circumstances, and the necessity I was under of sticking close to my business, occasion'd my postponing the further prosecution of it at that time; and my multifarious occupations, public and private, induc'd me to continue postponing, so that it has been omitted till I have no longer strength or activity left sufficient for such an enterprise; tho' I am still of opinion that it was a practicable scheme, and might have been very useful, by forming a great number of good citizens; and I was not discourag'd by the seeming magnitude of the undertaking, as I have always thought that one man of tolerable abilities may work great changes, and accomplish great affairs among mankind, if he first forms a good plan, and, cutting off all amusements or other employments that would divert his attention, makes the execution of that same plan his sole study and business.
paras.z: 关于这个计划，我现在能记起的就是这些，此外只记得我曾把它的一部分告诉过两个年轻人，他们相当热心地接受了。但是我那时境况窄小，又必须埋头于自己的生意，所以当时就把进一步实行的事搁了下来；后来公私事务繁杂，我又一再拖延，以致一直搁到如今，我已经没有足够的精力和活力来办这样一桩事业了。不过我仍然认为，那是一个切实可行的计划，可以造就大批的好公民，会是很有益的。这桩事业看上去规模宏大，但这并没有使我气馁，因为我一向认为，一个才能尚可的人，只要先订出一个好计划，割舍一切会分散他注意力的娱乐或别的事务，把执行这个计划当作他唯一的研究和事业，就可以在人类中间造成巨大的变化，成就伟大的事业。

paras.e: In 1732 I first publish'd my Almanack, under the name of Richard Saunders; it was continu'd by me about twenty-five years, commonly call'd Poor Richard's Almanac. I endeavor'd to make it both entertaining and useful, and it accordingly came to be in such demand, that I reap'd considerable profit from it, vending annually near ten thousand. And observing that it was generally read, scarce any neighborhood in the province being without it, I consider'd it as a proper vehicle for conveying instruction among the common people, who bought scarcely any other books; I therefore filled all the little spaces that occurr'd between the remarkable days in the calendar with proverbial sentences, chiefly such as inculcated industry and frugality, as the means of procuring wealth, and thereby securing virtue; it being more difficult for a man in want, to act always honestly, as, to use here one of those proverbs, it is hard for an empty sack to stand upright.
paras.z: 1732 年，我第一次出版我的历书，用的是理查德·桑德斯的名字；我接着出了大约二十五年，一般叫做《穷理查年鉴》。我努力把它办得既有趣又有用，因此它变得十分畅销，每年卖出将近一万册，我从中获利颇丰。我看到它流传很广，本殖民地几乎没有哪个街坊没有它，就认为它是向普通百姓传播教益的一种合适的工具，因为他们几乎不买别的书。所以，我把日历上值得注意的日子之间留下的所有小空白都填上了格言式的句子，主要是劝人勤劳节俭的，因为这是致富的手段，从而也是保全美德的手段；一个穷困的人要始终诚实行事是比较难的，借用其中一句格言来说，就是：空口袋难以直立。

paras.e: These proverbs, which contained the wisdom of many ages and nations, I assembled and form'd into a connected discourse prefix'd to the Almanack of 1757, as the harangue of a wise old man to the people attending an auction. The bringing all these scatter'd counsels thus into a focus enabled them to make greater impression. The piece, being universally approved, was copied in all the newspapers of the Continent; reprinted in Britain on a broad side, to be stuck up in houses; two translations were made of it in French, and great numbers bought by the clergy and gentry, to distribute gratis among their poor parishioners and tenants. In Pennsylvania, as it discouraged useless expense in foreign superfluities, some thought it had its share of influence in producing that growing plenty of money which was observable for several years after its publication.
paras.z: 这些格言包含了许多时代、许多民族的智慧，我把它们汇集起来，编成一篇连贯的讲话，放在 1757 年的历书前面，算是一位聪明的老人对参加拍卖会的众人的演说。把所有这些零散的劝诫这样集中到一点上，就使它们能给人更深的印象。这篇东西受到普遍的赞许，北美大陆的所有报纸都转载了；在英国，它被印成单面的大张，供人贴在家里；在法国有了两种译本，教士和乡绅们大量购买，免费分发给他们穷苦的教区居民和佃户。在宾夕法尼亚，因为它劝人不要把钱无谓地花在外国的奢侈品上，有人认为，它出版以后好几年间人们看到的那种货币日见充裕的现象，也有它的一份功劳。

paras.e: I considered my newspaper, also, as another means of communicating instruction, and in that view frequently reprinted in it extracts from the Spectator, and other moral writers; and sometimes publish'd little pieces of my own, which had been first compos'd for reading in our Junto. Of these are a Socratic dialogue, tending to prove that, whatever might be his parts and abilities, a vicious man could not properly be called a man of sense; and a discourse on self-denial, showing that virtue was not secure till its practice became a habitude, and was free from the opposition of contrary inclinations. These may be found in the papers about the beginning of 1735.
paras.z: 我也把我的报纸看作传播教益的另一种手段，本着这个目的，常常在报上转载《旁观者》和别的道德作家的摘录；有时也发表我自己的小文章，这些文章起初是为了在讲读社里宣读而写的。其中有一篇苏格拉底式的对话，意在证明：一个品行恶劣的人，无论有多大的才干和能力，都不能恰当地称为明白事理的人；还有一篇论克己的文章，说明美德只有在它的实行成了习惯、不再受相反倾向的抵抗之后，才算稳固。这些可以在 1735 年初前后的报纸上找到。

paras.e: In the conduct of my newspaper, I carefully excluded all libelling and personal abuse, which is of late years become so disgraceful to our country. Whenever I was solicited to insert anything of that kind, and the writers pleaded, as they generally did, the liberty of the press, and that a newspaper was like a stage-coach, in which any one who would pay had a right to a place, my answer was, that I would print the piece separately if desired, and the author might have as many copies as he pleased to distribute himself, but that I would not take upon me to spread his detraction; and that, having contracted with my subscribers to furnish them with what might be either useful or entertaining, I could not fill their papers with private altercation, in which they had no concern, without doing them manifest injustice. Now, many of our printers make no scruple of gratifying the malice of individuals by false accusations of the fairest characters among ourselves, augmenting animosity even to the producing of duels; and are, moreover, so indiscreet as to print scurrilous reflections on the government of neighboring states, and even on the conduct of our best national allies, which may be attended with the most pernicious consequences. These things I mention as a caution to young printers, and that they may be encouraged not to pollute their presses and disgrace their profession by such infamous practices, but refuse steadily, as they may see by my example that such a course of conduct will not, on the whole, be injurious to their interests.
paras.z: 我办报的时候，小心地把一切诽谤和人身攻击排除在外，近年来这类东西已经成了我国的一大耻辱。每逢有人要求我刊登这类东西，而作者像通常那样拿出版自由来辩解，说报纸就像一辆公共马车，谁肯付钱谁就有权占一个座位，我的回答是：如果需要，我可以把那篇东西单独印出来，作者想要多少份就给他多少份，由他自己去散发，但是我不愿意承担替他传播诽谤的责任；而且，我同我的订户有约在先，要向他们提供有用或有趣的东西，如果我用同他们毫不相干的私人争吵来塞满他们的报纸，那显然是对他们不公道。如今，我们有许多印刷商毫无顾忌地去满足个别人的恶意，对我们当中品格最清白的人妄加指控，加深仇恨，甚至引出决斗；不但如此，他们还轻率到刊登文章，对邻近各州的政府，甚至对我国最好的盟友的行为加以下流的攻击，这可能招致极其有害的后果。我提这些事，是要告诫年轻的印刷商，鼓励他们不要用这种卑劣的行径玷污自己的印刷机、辱没自己的职业，而要坚决拒绝；因为他们从我的例子可以看到，这样做总的说来并不会损害他们的利益。

paras.e: In 1733 I sent one of my journeymen to Charleston, South Carolina, where a printer was wanting. I furnish'd him with a press and letters, on an agreement of partnership, by which I was to receive one-third of the profits of the business, paying one-third of the expense. He was a man of learning, and honest but ignorant in matters of account; and, tho' he sometimes made me remittances, I could get no account from him, nor any satisfactory state of our partnership while he lived. On his decease, the business was continued by his widow, who, being born and bred in Holland, where, as I have been inform'd, the knowledge of accounts makes a part of female education, she not only sent me as clear a state as she could find of the transactions past, but continued to account with the greatest regularity and exactness every quarter afterwards, and managed the business with such success, that she not only brought up reputably a family of children, but, at the expiration of the term, was able to purchase of me the printing-house, and establish her son in it.
paras.z: 1733 年，我把手下的一个工人派到南卡罗来纳的查尔斯顿去，那里正缺一个印刷商。我供给他一台印刷机和铅字，订了合伙的协议，按照协议，我得营业利润的三分之一，负担开支的三分之一。他是个有学问的人，也诚实，可是不懂账目；他虽然有时给我汇款，我在他生前却始终拿不到一份账目，也得不到任何关于我们合伙情况的令人满意的说明。他死后，生意由他的遗孀继续经营。她生长在荷兰，我听说在那里账目的知识是女子教育的一部分；她不但把她能找到的过去的往来账目尽可能清楚地整理了一份寄给我，而且此后每个季度都极其按时而准确地结账。她把生意经营得很成功，不但体面地把一家子女抚养成人，而且在合伙期满时还能从我手里买下印刷所，让她的儿子在那里立了业。

paras.e: I mention this affair chiefly for the sake of recommending that branch of education for our young females, as likely to be of more use to them and their children, in case of widowhood, than either music or dancing, by preserving them from losses by imposition of crafty men, and enabling them to continue, perhaps, a profitable mercantile house, with establish'd correspondence, till a son is grown up fit to undertake and go on with it, to the lasting advantage and enriching of the family.
paras.z: 我提这件事，主要是为了建议让我们年轻的女子受这一门教育，因为万一守了寡，这对她们和她们的子女大概比音乐或舞蹈都更有用：它可以使她们不致受狡猾之徒的欺骗而遭受损失，也许还能使她们把一家有固定往来关系的、赚钱的商号维持下去，直到儿子长大成人，能够接手经营，从而使全家长久受益，富裕起来。

paras.e: About the year 1734 there arrived among us from Ireland a young Presbyterian preacher, named Hemphill, who delivered with a good voice, and apparently extempore, most excellent discourses, which drew together considerable numbers of different persuasion, who join'd in admiring them. Among the rest, I became one of his constant hearers, his sermons pleasing me, as they had little of the dogmatical kind, but inculcated strongly the practice of virtue, or what in the religious stile are called good works. Those, however, of our congregation, who considered themselves as orthodox Presbyterians, disapprov'd his doctrine, and were join'd by most of the old clergy, who arraign'd him of heterodoxy before the synod, in order to have him silenc'd. I became his zealous partisan, and contributed all I could to raise a party in his favour, and we combated for him a while with some hopes of success. There was much scribbling pro and con upon the occasion; and finding that, tho' an elegant preacher, he was but a poor writer, I lent him my pen and wrote for him two or three pamphlets, and one piece in the Gazette of April, 1735. Those pamphlets, as is generally the case with controversial writings, tho' eagerly read at the time, were soon out of vogue, and I question whether a single copy of them now exists.
paras.z: 大约在 1734 年，从爱尔兰来了一位年轻的长老会牧师，名叫亨普希尔。他嗓音很好，讲起道来似乎是即席而谈，讲得极其出色，吸引了不同教派的许多人，大家同声赞赏。我也同别人一样成了他的固定听众；他的讲道我很喜欢，因为其中很少教条式的东西，而是极力劝人实行美德，也就是宗教用语里所谓的“善功”。可是，我们会众里那些自认为是正统长老会教徒的人不赞成他的教义，大多数老牧师也站在他们一边，在教区会议上控告他是异端，要使他不得再讲道。我成了他热心的拥护者，尽我所能组织了一派人支持他，我们为他奋战了一阵子，颇有几分成功的希望。为了这件事，赞成的和反对的写了许多文字；我发现他虽然是个优雅的讲道人，文章却写得很差，就把我的笔借给他，替他写了两三本小册子，还在 1735 年 4 月的《公报》上发表了一篇文章。那些小册子，正如论战文字通常的命运一样，当时虽然人人争读，不久就过时了，我怀疑现在是否还有一本存世。

paras.e: During the contest an unlucky occurrence hurt his cause exceedingly. One of our adversaries having heard him preach a sermon that was much admired, thought he had somewhere read the sermon before, or at least a part of it. On search he found that part quoted at length, in one of the British Reviews, from a discourse of Dr. Foster's. This detection gave many of our party disgust, who accordingly abandoned his cause, and occasion'd our more speedy discomfiture in the synod. I stuck by him, however, as I rather approv'd his giving us good sermons compos'd by others, than bad ones of his own manufacture, tho' the latter was the practice of our common teachers. He afterward acknowledg'd to me that none of those he preach'd were his own; adding, that his memory was such as enabled him to retain and repeat any sermon after one reading only. On our defeat, he left us in search elsewhere of better fortune, and I quitted the congregation, never joining it after, tho' I continu'd many years my subscription for the support of its ministers.
paras.z: 在这场争论中，出了一件倒霉的事，大大损害了他的事业。我们的一个对手听他讲了一次很受称赞的道，觉得自己以前在什么地方读到过这篇讲道，至少读到过其中的一部分。他一查，发现那一部分被一份英国评论刊物整段引用过，出自福斯特博士的一篇讲道。这一揭发使我们这一派的许多人大为反感，他们于是抛弃了他的事业，这使我们在教区会议上败得更快。不过我还是支持他到底，因为我宁愿他给我们讲别人写的好讲道，也不愿他讲自己造出来的坏讲道，虽然后者是我们一般牧师的做法。他后来向我承认，他讲的那些没有一篇是他自己的；还说他的记性好到任何一篇讲道只读一遍就能记住并背出来。我们失败以后，他离开了我们，到别处去另寻出路；我也退出了那个会众，以后再没有加入，虽然我多年来一直交纳供养牧师的捐款。

paras.e: I had begun in 1733 to study languages; I soon made myself so much a master of the French as to be able to read the books with ease. I then undertook the Italian. An acquaintance, who was also learning it, us'd often to tempt me to play chess with him. Finding this took up too much of the time I had to spare for study, I at length refus'd to play any more, unless on this condition, that the victor in every game should have a right to impose a task, either in parts of the grammar to be got by heart, or in translations, etc., which tasks the vanquish'd was to perform upon honour, before our next meeting. As we play'd pretty equally, we thus beat one another into that language. I afterwards with a little painstaking, acquir'd as much of the Spanish as to read their books also.
paras.z: 我在 1733 年开始学习外语。我不久就把法语掌握到能够轻松读书的程度。然后我着手学意大利语。有一个熟人也在学，常常引诱我同他下棋。我发现这占去了我留给学习的时间太多，最后就拒绝再下，除非答应这个条件：每一盘的胜者有权规定一项作业，或者是要背熟的若干文法，或者是翻译之类，输的人要凭信用在我们下次见面之前完成。我们棋力相当，就这样你赢我一盘、我赢你一盘地把彼此打进了那门语言里。后来我稍稍下了点功夫，又把西班牙语学到了也能读他们的书的程度。

paras.e: I have already mention'd that I had only one year's instruction in a Latin school, and that when very young, after which I neglected that language entirely. But, when I had attained an acquaintance with the French, Italian, and Spanish, I was surpriz'd to find, on looking over a Latin Testament, that I understood so much more of that language than I had imagined, which encouraged me to apply myself again to the study of it, and I met with more success, as those preceding languages had greatly smooth'd my way.
paras.z: 我已经说过，我只在拉丁文学校受过一年的教育，而且是在很小的时候，此后就把那门语言完全丢开了。可是，等我熟悉了法语、意大利语和西班牙语以后，有一回翻阅一本拉丁文的《新约》，惊讶地发现我懂得的拉丁文比我想象的多得多。这鼓励我重新用功学它，而且学得更顺利了，因为前面那几种语言已经大大铺平了我的道路。

paras.e: From these circumstances, I have thought that there is some inconsistency in our common mode of teaching languages. We are told that it is proper to begin first with the Latin, and, having acquir'd that, it will be more easy to attain those modern languages which are deriv'd from it; and yet we do not begin with the Greek, in order more easily to acquire the Latin. It is true that, if you can clamber and get to the top of a staircase without using the steps, you will more easily gain them in descending; but certainly, if you begin with the lowest you will with more ease ascend to the top; and I would therefore offer it to the consideration of those who superintend the education of our youth, whether, since many of those who begin with the Latin quit the same after spending some years without having made any great proficiency, and what they have learnt becomes almost useless, so that their time has been lost, it would not have been better to have begun with the French, proceeding to the Italian, etc.; for, tho', after spending the same time, they should quit the study of languages and never arrive at the Latin, they would, however, have acquired another tongue or two, that, being in modern use, might be serviceable to them in common life.
paras.z: 从这些情形我想到，我们通常教语言的方式有些不合理。人家告诉我们，应当先从拉丁文学起，学会了拉丁文，再学由它派生出来的那些现代语言就比较容易；可是我们并不为了更容易学会拉丁文而先学希腊文。不错，如果你不用台阶就能攀爬到楼梯的顶上，那么你往下走的时候会更容易踏上那些台阶；可是毫无疑问，如果你从最低的一级开始，你会更省力地登上顶端。所以我想提请主管我国青年教育的人们考虑：既然许多从拉丁文学起的人花了几年工夫，没有多大长进就放弃了，他们学到的东西几乎毫无用处，时间也就白费了，那么，从法语学起，再进到意大利语等等，是不是更好些？因为，即使他们花了同样的时间之后放弃了语言的学习，始终没有学到拉丁文，他们毕竟已经学会了另外一两种语言，这些语言是现代通用的，在日常生活中也许对他们有用处。

paras.e: After ten years' absence from Boston, and having become easy in my circumstances, I made a journey thither to visit my relations, which I could not sooner well afford. In returning, I call'd at Newport to see my brother, then settled there with his printing-house. Our former differences were forgotten, and our meeting was very cordial and affectionate. He was fast declining in his health, and requested of me that, in case of his death, which he apprehended not far distant, I would take home his son, then but ten years of age, and bring him up to the printing business. This I accordingly perform'd, sending him a few years to school before I took him into the office. His mother carried on the business till he was grown up, when I assisted him with an assortment of new types, those of his father being in a manner worn out. Thus it was that I made my brother ample amends for the service I had depriv'd him of by leaving him so early.
paras.z: 我离开波士顿十年以后，境况宽裕了，就回去了一趟探望亲属，在这之前我是负担不起这趟路费的。回来的路上，我到纽波特去看我哥哥，那时他带着他的印刷所在那里定居。我们从前的不和都已忘却，见面时非常亲热友爱。他的健康迅速衰退，他请求我，万一他死了——他担心那已为期不远——我把他那个才十岁的儿子带回家，培养他学印刷这一行。这件事我照办了，先送他上了几年学，然后才让他进印刷所。他母亲把生意维持下去，直到他长大成人；那时我资助了他一套新铅字，因为他父亲的铅字差不多已经磨损完了。就这样，我当年过早离开我哥哥，使他失去了我本应提供的服务，如今算是充分补偿了他。

paras.e: In 1736 I lost one of my sons, a fine boy of four years old, by the small-pox, taken in the common way. I long regretted bitterly, and still regret that I had not given it to him by inoculation. This I mention for the sake of parents who omit that operation, on the supposition that they should never forgive themselves if a child died under it; my example showing that the regret may be the same either way, and that, therefore, the safer should be chosen.
paras.z: 1736 年，我失去了一个儿子，一个四岁的好孩子，他是照通常的途径染上天花死的。我长久地痛悔，至今仍在痛悔，没有给他种痘。我提这件事，是为了那些不给孩子种痘的父母——他们以为，如果孩子因种痘而死，他们永远不会原谅自己；我的例子表明，无论哪种情形，悔恨也许是一样的，所以应当选择那条比较安全的路。

paras.e: Our club, the Junto, was found so useful, and afforded such satisfaction to the members, that several were desirous of introducing their friends, which could not well be done without exceeding what we had settled as a convenient number, viz., twelve. We had from the beginning made it a rule to keep our institution a secret, which was pretty well observ'd; the intention was to avoid applications of improper persons for admittance, some of whom, perhaps, we might find it difficult to refuse. I was one of those who were against any addition to our number, but, instead of it, made in writing a proposal, that every member separately should endeavor to form a subordinate club, with the same rules respecting queries, etc., and without informing them of the connection with the Junto. The advantages proposed were, the improvement of so many more young citizens by the use of our institutions; our better acquaintance with the general sentiments of the inhabitants on any occasion, as the Junto member might propose what queries we should desire, and was to report to the Junto what pass'd in his separate club; the promotion of our particular interests in business by more extensive recommendation, and the increase of our influence in public affairs, and our power of doing good by spreading thro' the several clubs the sentiments of the Junto.
paras.z: 我们的社团讲读社，大家发现它十分有益，社员们都很满意，有几位就想介绍自己的朋友加入；可是这样做，就不免超过我们定下的合适人数，就是十二个人。我们从一开始就立下规矩，对我们的组织保守秘密，这条规矩大家遵守得相当好；用意是避免不合适的人申请加入，其中有些人我们也许难以拒绝。我是反对增加人数的人之一，但我没有只是反对，而是写了一份书面建议：每个社员各自设法组织一个附属的社团，采用同样的关于提问等等的规则，但不告诉他们同讲读社的关系。预期的好处是：有更多的年轻公民可以利用我们的办法而得到提高；我们可以更好地了解居民在任何场合的普遍意见，因为讲读社的社员可以在各自的社团里提出我们希望提出的问题，并且要向讲读社报告他那个社团里的讨论情况；通过更广泛的推荐，可以促进我们各自生意上的利益；通过各个社团传播讲读社的意见，可以增加我们在公共事务中的影响和我们行善的力量。

paras.e: The project was approv'd, and every member undertook to form his club, but they did not all succeed. Five or six only were compleated, which were called by different names, as the Vine, the Union, the Band, etc. They were useful to themselves, and afforded us a good deal of amusement, information, and instruction, besides answering, in some considerable degree, our views of influencing the public opinion on particular occasions, of which I shall give some instances in course of time as they happened.
paras.z: 这个计划得到了赞同，每个社员都着手组织自己的社团，但并不是人人都成功。只有五六个办成了，各有不同的名称，如“藤社”“联合社”“同盟社”等等。它们对自己有益，也给了我们不少乐趣、见闻和教益，此外还在相当程度上实现了我们在特定场合影响舆论的意图；这方面的事例，我以后会按照发生的先后讲几个。

paras.e: My first promotion was my being chosen, in 1736, clerk of the General Assembly. The choice was made that year without opposition; but the year following, when I was again propos'd (the choice, like that of the members, being annual), a new member made a long speech against me, in order to favour some other candidate. I was, however, chosen, which was the more agreeable to me, as, besides the pay for the immediate service as clerk, the place gave me a better opportunity of keeping up an interest among the members, which secur'd to me the business of printing the votes, laws, paper money, and other occasional jobbs for the public, that, on the whole, were very profitable.
paras.z: 我的第一次升迁，是 1736 年被选为州议会的书记。那一年选举时没有人反对；可是第二年我再次被提名的时候（这个职位同议员一样，是一年一选的），一位新议员发表了一篇长篇演说反对我，为的是支持另一个候选人。不过我还是当选了。这使我格外高兴，因为除了当书记本身的薪水之外，这个职位还使我有更好的机会同议员们保持交情，从而保证我得到印刷表决记录、法律、纸币以及其他不时会有的公家零活的生意，这些加在一起是很有利可图的。

paras.e: I therefore did not like the opposition of this new member, who was a gentleman of fortune and education, with talents that were likely to give him, in time, great influence in the House, which, indeed, afterwards happened. I did not, however, aim at gaining his favour by paying any servile respect to him, but, after some time, took this other method. Having heard that he had in his library a certain very scarce and curious book, I wrote a note to him, expressing my desire of perusing that book, and requesting he would do me the favour of lending it to me for a few days. He sent it immediately, and I return'd it in about a week with another note, expressing strongly my sense of the favour. When we next met in the House, he spoke to me (which he had never done before), and with great civility; and he ever after manifested a readiness to serve me on all occasions, so that we became great friends, and our friendship continued to his death. This is another instance of the truth of an old maxim I had learned, which says, "He that has once done you a kindness will be more ready to do you another, than he whom you yourself have obliged." And it shows how much more profitable it is prudently to remove, than to resent, return, and continue inimical proceedings.
paras.z: 所以我不喜欢这位新议员同我作对。他是一位有财产、有教养的绅士，凭他的才干，日后很可能在议院里有很大的影响，后来果然如此。不过我并不打算用卑躬屈膝的办法去讨他的欢心，而是过了一段时间，用了另一个办法。我听说他的藏书里有一本非常稀罕而珍奇的书，就给他写了一张便条，表示我很想读一读那本书，请他赏脸借给我几天。他马上派人送来了；大约一个星期后我把书还给他，又附了一张便条，热烈地表示我对这一厚意的感激。我们下次在议院里见面时，他同我说话了（以前他从没有这样做过），而且十分客气；此后他在一切场合都表现出乐意为我效劳，于是我们成了很好的朋友，我们的友谊一直延续到他去世。这又是一个例子，证明我学到的一句老格言是对的，那句话说：“曾经帮过你一次忙的人，比你自己帮过忙的人，更乐意再帮你一次。”这也表明，审慎地消除敌意，比怨恨它、回敬它、把它继续下去，要有利得多。

paras.e: In 1737, Colonel Spotswood, late governor of Virginia, and then postmaster-general, being dissatisfied with the conduct of his deputy at Philadelphia, respecting some negligence in rendering, and inexactitude of his accounts, took from him the commission and offered it to me. I accepted it readily, and found it of great advantage; for, tho' the salary was small, it facilitated the correspondence that improv'd my newspaper, increas'd the number demanded, as well as the advertisements to be inserted, so that it came to afford me a considerable income. My old competitor's newspaper declin'd proportionably, and I was satisfy'd without retaliating his refusal, while postmaster, to permit my papers being carried by the riders. Thus he suffer'd greatly from his neglect in due accounting; and I mention it as a lesson to those young men who may be employ'd in managing affairs for others, that they should always render accounts, and make remittances, with great clearness and punctuality. The character of observing such a conduct is the most powerful of all recommendations to new employments and increase of business.
paras.z: 1737 年，斯波茨伍德上校——他原任弗吉尼亚总督，当时是邮政总长——不满意他在费城的代理人的所作所为，因为那人交账疏忽，账目又不准确，就撤了他的委任，把这个职位给了我。我欣然接受，发现它大有好处；因为薪水虽然少，它却方便了通信往来，使我的报纸办得更好，订数增加了，要登的广告也多了，结果它给我带来了相当可观的收入。我那位老对手的报纸相应地衰落下去；他当邮政局长的时候不许邮差捎带我的报纸，我却没有用同样的办法报复他，这样我已经心满意足了。他就是这样因为不按时交账而大受损失的；我提这件事，是给那些可能受雇替别人经管事务的年轻人一个教训：他们交账和汇款，都要十分清楚、十分准时。有了这样行事的名声，就是谋求新差事、扩大生意的最有力的推荐。

paras.e: I began now to turn my thoughts a little to public affairs, beginning, however, with small matters. The city watch was one of the first things that I conceiv'd to want regulation. It was managed by the constables of the respective wards in turn; the constable warned a number of housekeepers to attend him for the night. Those who chose never to attend paid him six shillings a year to be excus'd, which was suppos'd to be for hiring substitutes, but was, in reality, much more than was necessary for that purpose, and made the constableship a place of profit; and the constable, for a little drink, often got such ragamuffins about him as a watch, that respectable housekeepers did not choose to mix with. Walking the rounds, too, was often neglected, and most of the nights spent in tippling. I thereupon wrote a paper to be read in Junto, representing these irregularities, but insisting more particularly on the inequality of this six-shilling tax of the constables, respecting the circumstances of those who paid it, since a poor widow housekeeper, all whose property to be guarded by the watch did not perhaps exceed the value of fifty pounds, paid as much as the wealthiest merchant, who had thousands of pounds' worth of goods in his stores.
paras.z: 这时我开始把心思稍稍转向公共事务，不过是从小事做起。城里的巡夜是我最先认为需要整顿的事情之一。它由各区的警官轮流管理；警官通知若干户主当夜跟他一起值班。那些情愿永远不去值班的人每年付给他六先令以求免役，这笔钱据说是用来雇人顶替的，其实远远超过了这个用途的需要，使警官成了一个有油水的职位；而警官只要给一点酒喝，常常招来一帮叫花子似的人当巡夜的，体面的户主都不愿意同他们混在一起。巡逻也常常被忽略，大半夜都花在喝酒上。于是我写了一篇文章在讲读社里宣读，陈述这些不正常的情形，但特别强调警官收的这六先令的捐税，就交钱人的境况来说是不公平的；因为一个穷寡妇户主，她需要巡夜人保护的全部财产也许不超过五十镑，交的钱却同铺子里存着成千镑货物的最富有的商人一样多。

paras.e: On the whole, I proposed as a more effectual watch, the hiring of proper men to serve constantly in that business; and as a more equitable way of supporting the charge the levying a tax that should be proportion'd to the property. This idea, being approv'd by the Junto, was communicated to the other clubs, but as arising in each of them; and though the plan was not immediately carried into execution, yet, by preparing the minds of people for the change, it paved the way for the law obtained a few years after, when the members of our clubs were grown into more influence.
paras.z: 总之，我提议雇用合适的人长期专门担任这项工作，作为更有效的巡夜办法；并且征收一种同财产成比例的税，作为负担这笔费用的更公平的办法。这个主意得到讲读社的赞同，就传达给其他各个社团，不过说成是各社自己提出来的。这个计划虽然没有立刻付诸实行，但它使人们的思想对这种变革有了准备，为几年后通过的那项法律铺平了道路，那时我们各个社团的成员已经更有影响了。

paras.e: About this time I wrote a paper (first to be read in Junto, but it was afterward publish'd) on the different accidents and carelessnesses by which houses were set on fire, with cautions against them, and means proposed of avoiding them. This was much spoken of as a useful piece, and gave rise to a project, which soon followed it, of forming a company for the more ready extinguishing of fires, and mutual assistance in removing and securing the goods when in danger. Associates in this scheme were presently found, amounting to thirty. Our articles of agreement oblig'd every member to keep always in good order, and fit for use, a certain number of leather buckets, with strong bags and baskets (for packing and transporting of goods), which were to be brought to every fire; and we agreed to meet once a month and spend a social evening together, in discoursing and communicating such ideas as occurred to us upon the subject of fires, as might be useful in our conduct on such occasions.
paras.z: 大约在这个时候，我写了一篇文章（先是在讲读社里宣读的，后来发表了），论述引起房屋失火的各种意外和疏忽，提出防范的告诫和避免的办法。大家都说这是一篇有用的文章，由此产生了一个计划，不久就实行了，就是组织一个消防队，以便更迅速地扑灭火灾，并且在财物有危险时互相帮助搬运和保护。很快就找到了三十个愿意参加这个计划的人。我们的协议条款规定，每个成员必须经常备有一定数目的皮水桶，保持完好可用，还要有结实的袋子和篮子（用来装运财物），每逢火灾都要带到现场；我们还约定每月聚会一次，共度一个联欢的晚上，交谈并交流我们想到的有关火灾的意见，这些意见在救火时可能对我们有用。

paras.e: The utility of this institution soon appeared, and many more desiring to be admitted than we thought convenient for one company, they were advised to form another, which was accordingly done; and this went on, one new company being formed after another, till they became so numerous as to include most of the inhabitants who were men of property; and now, at the time of my writing this, tho' upward of fifty years since its establishment, that which I first formed, called the Union Fire Company, still subsists and flourishes, tho' the first members are all deceas'd but myself and one, who is older by a year than I am. The small fines that have been paid by members for absence at the monthly meetings have been apply'd to the purchase of fire-engines, ladders, fire-hooks, and other useful implements for each company, so that I question whether there is a city in the world better provided with the means of putting a stop to beginning conflagrations; and, in fact, since these institutions, the city has never lost by fire more than one or two houses at a time, and the flames have often been extinguished before the house in which they began has been half consumed.
paras.z: 这个组织的效用不久就显示出来了，想参加的人比我们认为一个队适宜容纳的多得多，我们就劝他们另组一队，他们照办了。这样一个接一个地组织新的消防队，后来数目多到把大多数有产业的居民都包括进去了。如今，在我写这些话的时候，离它成立虽然已有五十多年，我最先组织的那一队，叫做“联合消防队”，仍然存在，而且很兴旺，尽管最初的队员除了我和一位比我大一岁的人以外都已去世了。队员因缺席每月的聚会而交纳的小额罚金，被用来为每个队购买救火机、梯子、火钩和其他有用的器械，所以我怀疑世界上是否有哪个城市在扑灭初起的火灾方面比这里装备得更好。事实上，自从有了这些组织，这个城市每次失火从没有烧掉过一两所以上的房子，而且火焰常常在起火的那所房子烧掉一半之前就被扑灭了。

paras.e: In 1739 arrived among us from Ireland the Reverend Mr. Whitefield, who had made himself remarkable there as an itinerant preacher. He was at first permitted to preach in some of our churches; but the clergy, taking a dislike to him, soon refus'd him their pulpits, and he was oblig'd to preach in the fields. The multitudes of all sects and denominations that attended his sermons were enormous, and it was matter of speculation to me, who was one of the number, to observe the extraordinary influence of his oratory on his hearers, and how much they admir'd and respected him, notwithstanding his common abuse of them, by assuring them that they were naturally half beasts and half devils. It was wonderful to see the change soon made in the manners of our inhabitants. From being thoughtless or indifferent about religion, it seem'd as if all the world were growing religious, so that one could not walk thro' the town in an evening without hearing psalms sung in different families of every street.
paras.z: 1739 年，怀特菲尔德牧师先生从爱尔兰来到我们这里，他在那里已经以巡回传道而出了名。起初他获准在我们的几座教堂里讲道；但牧师们讨厌他，不久就不让他用他们的讲坛，他只好在野外讲道。来听他讲道的各教各派的群众多得惊人。我也是听众之一，观察他的口才对听众有多么不同寻常的影响，观察他们多么钦佩他、敬重他——尽管他常常辱骂他们，向他们断言他们天生一半是野兽、一半是魔鬼——这对我成了一个值得琢磨的问题。看到我们居民的风气不久就起的变化，真是奇妙。人们原先对宗教漫不经心或者漠不关心，这时却好像全世界都变得虔诚起来，以致傍晚在城里走一趟，每条街上都能听到不同的人家在唱赞美诗。

paras.e: And it being found inconvenient to assemble in the open air, subject to its inclemencies, the building of a house to meet in was no sooner propos'd, and persons appointed to receive contributions, but sufficient sums were soon receiv'd to procure the ground and erect the building, which was one hundred feet long and seventy broad, about the size of Westminster Hall; and the work was carried on with such spirit as to be finished in a much shorter time than could have been expected. Both house and ground were vested in trustees, expressly for the use of any preacher of any religious persuasion who might desire to say something to the people at Philadelphia; the design in building not being to accommodate any particular sect, but the inhabitants in general; so that even if the Mufti of Constantinople were to send a missionary to preach Mohammedanism to us, he would find a pulpit at his service.
paras.z: 人们发现在露天集会要受天气不好之苦，很不方便，于是刚一提议盖一所聚会用的房子，并指定了收捐款的人，很快就收到了足够的款项来买地盖房。那所房子长一百英尺，宽七十英尺，大小同威斯敏斯特大厅差不多；工程进行得十分带劲，完工的时间比预料的短得多。房子和地皮都交给了受托人，明文规定供任何宗教派别的任何讲道人使用，只要他想对费城人讲点什么；盖这所房子的宗旨不是为了某一个教派的方便，而是为了全体居民；所以，即使君士坦丁堡的穆夫提派一个传教士来向我们宣讲伊斯兰教，他也会发现有一个讲坛供他使用。

paras.e: Mr. Whitefield, in leaving us, went preaching all the way thro' the colonies to Georgia. The settlement of that province had lately been begun, but, instead of being made with hardy, industrious husbandmen, accustomed to labor, the only people fit for such an enterprise, it was with families of broken shop-keepers and other insolvent debtors, many of indolent and idle habits, taken out of the jails, who, being set down in the woods, unqualified for clearing land, and unable to endure the hardships of a new settlement, perished in numbers, leaving many helpless children unprovided for. The sight of their miserable situation inspir'd the benevolent heart of Mr. Whitefield with the idea of building an Orphan House there, in which they might be supported and educated. Returning northward, he preach'd up this charity, and made large collections, for his eloquence had a wonderful power over the hearts and purses of his hearers, of which I myself was an instance.
paras.z: 怀特菲尔德先生离开我们以后，一路讲道穿过各殖民地，到了佐治亚。那个殖民地不久前才开始拓殖，可是去拓殖的不是吃苦耐劳、勤恳、惯于劳作的农夫——只有这样的人才适合这种事业——而是破产的店主和其他还不起债的债务人的家庭，许多人习性懒散，是从监狱里放出来的。这些人被安置在森林里，不会开垦土地，又受不了新垦地的艰苦，成批地死去，留下许多无依无靠、无人抚养的孩子。看到他们悲惨的处境，怀特菲尔德先生仁慈的心里产生了在那里建一所孤儿院的想法，让他们在里面得到抚养和教育。他回到北方，为这项慈善事业讲道劝募，募到了大笔的捐款，因为他的口才对听众的心和钱袋都有奇妙的力量，我自己就是一个例子。

paras.e: I did not disapprove of the design, but, as Georgia was then destitute of materials and workmen, and it was proposed to send them from Philadelphia at a great expense, I thought it would have been better to have built the house here, and brought the children to it. This I advis'd; but he was resolute in his first project, rejected my counsel, and I therefore refus'd to contribute. I happened soon after to attend one of his sermons, in the course of which I perceived he intended to finish with a collection, and I silently resolved he should get nothing from me. I had in my pocket a handful of copper money, three or four silver dollars, and five pistoles in gold. As he proceeded I began to soften, and concluded to give the coppers. Another stroke of his oratory made me asham'd of that, and determin'd me to give the silver; and he finish'd so admirably, that I empty'd my pocket wholly into the collector's dish, gold and all. At this sermon there was also one of our club, who, being of my sentiments respecting the building in Georgia, and suspecting a collection might be intended, had, by precaution, emptied his pockets before he came from home. Towards the conclusion of the discourse, however, he felt a strong desire to give, and apply'd to a neighbour, who stood near him, to borrow some money for the purpose. The application was unfortunately [made] to perhaps the only man in the company who had the firmness not to be affected by the preacher. His answer was, "At any other time, Friend Hopkinson, I would lend to thee freely; but not now, for thee seems to be out of thy right senses."
paras.z: 我并不反对这个计划，但是佐治亚当时既缺材料又缺工匠，有人提议花很大的费用从费城运去，我想不如把孤儿院建在这里，把孩子们接来。我这样劝过他；可是他坚持他最初的计划，拒绝了我的意见，我因此不肯捐款。不久以后，我碰巧去听他的一次讲道，听着听着，我看出他打算在结束时募捐，就暗自下了决心，他别想从我这里得到一文钱。我口袋里有一把铜币，三四块银元，五个皮斯托尔金币。他讲下去，我开始心软了，决定把铜币捐出去。他的口才又是一击，使我为此感到惭愧，决定把银元也捐了；而他结束得那样精彩，我把口袋里的钱全部倒进了募捐人的盘子里，连金币一起。听这次讲道的还有我们社团的一个人，他对在佐治亚建院的看法同我一样，又疑心可能要募捐，为防万一，出门前把口袋掏空了。可是讲道快结束的时候，他很想捐钱，就向站在旁边的一个邻居借钱。不巧的是，他求借的这个人，也许是全场唯一有定力不为讲道人所动的人。那人回答说：“朋友霍普金森，要是在别的任何时候，我都乐意借给你；可是现在不行，因为你好像神志不大正常。”

paras.e: Some of Mr. Whitefield's enemies affected to suppose that he would apply these collections to his own private emolument; but I who was intimately acquainted with him (being employed in printing his Sermons and Journals, etc.), never had the least suspicion of his integrity, but am to this day decidedly of opinion that he was in all his conduct a perfectly honest man, and methinks my testimony in his favour ought to have the more weight, as we had no religious connection. He us'd, indeed, sometimes to pray for my conversion, but never had the satisfaction of believing that his prayers were heard. Ours was a mere civil friendship, sincere on both sides, and lasted to his death.
paras.z: 怀特菲尔德先生的一些仇人故意假定他会把这些捐款挪作私用；但是我同他很熟（因为我受雇印刷他的讲道集和日记等等），对他的正直从没有过丝毫的怀疑，至今仍然坚决认为他在一切行为上都是一个完全诚实的人。我想，我替他作的这个见证应当更有分量，因为我们在宗教上并没有关系。他确实有时为我的归信而祈祷，但始终没有得到那种满足，相信他的祈祷已蒙垂听。我们之间纯粹是世俗的友谊，双方都很真诚，一直维持到他去世。

paras.e: The following instance will show something of the terms on which we stood. Upon one of his arrivals from England at Boston, he wrote to me that he should come soon to Philadelphia, but knew not where he could lodge when there, as he understood his old friend and host, Mr. Benezet, was removed to Germantown. My answer was, "You know my house; if you can make shift with its scanty accommodations, you will be most heartily welcome." He reply'd, that if I made that kind offer for Christ's sake, I should not miss of a reward. And I returned, "Don't let me be mistaken; it was not for Christ's sake, but for your sake." One of our common acquaintance jocosely remark'd, that, knowing it to be the custom of the saints, when they received any favour, to shift the burden of the obligation from off their own shoulders, and place it in heaven, I had contriv'd to fix it on earth.
paras.z: 下面这件事多少可以说明我们之间的关系。有一回他从英国到了波士顿，写信给我说，他不久要来费城，但不知道到了以后可以住在哪里，因为听说他的老朋友、老房东贝内泽特先生搬到日耳曼敦去了。我回信说：“你知道我的家；如果你能将就那里简陋的条件，我将十分衷心地欢迎你。”他回信说，如果我是为了基督的缘故提出这样好意的邀请，我是不会得不到报偿的。我又回信说：“别让人误会了；那不是为了基督的缘故，是为了你的缘故。”我们的一个共同的熟人开玩笑说，他知道圣徒们有个习惯，受了别人的恩惠，总要把这份情的负担从自己肩上卸下来，放到天上去，而我却设法把它固定在了地上。

paras.e: The last time I saw Mr. Whitefield was in London, when he consulted me about his Orphan House concern, and his purpose of appropriating it to the establishment of a college.
paras.z: 我最后一次见到怀特菲尔德先生是在伦敦，那时他同我商量他那所孤儿院的事，以及他想把它拨作创办一所学院之用的打算。

paras.e: He had a loud and clear voice, and articulated his words and sentences so perfectly, that he might be heard and understood at a great distance, especially as his auditories, however numerous, observ'd the most exact silence. He preach'd one evening from the top of the Court-house steps, which are in the middle of Market-street, and on the west side of Second-street, which crosses it at right angles. Both streets were fill'd with his hearers to a considerable distance. Being among the hindmost in Market-street, I had the curiosity to learn how far he could be heard, by retiring backwards down the street towards the river; and I found his voice distinct till I came near Front-street, when some noise in that street obscur'd it. Imagining then a semi-circle, of which my distance should be the radius, and that it were fill'd with auditors, to each of whom I allow'd two square feet, I computed that he might well be heard by more than thirty thousand. This reconcil'd me to the newspaper accounts of his having preach'd to twenty-five thousand people in the fields, and to the ancient histories of generals haranguing whole armies, of which I had sometimes doubted.
paras.z: 他的嗓音洪亮而清晰，字句的发音完美无缺，在很远的地方都能听见、听懂，尤其是他的听众不管有多少，总是保持着绝对的肃静。有一天傍晚，他站在法院台阶的顶上讲道，那台阶在市场街的中间，在同它直角相交的第二街的西侧。两条街上都挤满了他的听众，延伸到相当远的地方。我站在市场街最后面的人群里，出于好奇，想知道他的声音能传多远，就沿着街朝河边倒退着走；我发现他的声音一直很清楚，直到我快到前街的时候，那条街上的一些嘈杂声才把它盖住。于是我设想一个半圆，以我所在的距离为半径，里面站满了听众，每人占两平方英尺，算下来能够听清他讲话的人远不止三万。这使我相信了报纸上关于他曾在野外向两万五千人讲道的报道，也相信了古代史书上关于将军们向全军训话的记载，对这些我以前有时是怀疑的。

paras.e: By hearing him often, I came to distinguish easily between sermons newly compos'd, and those which he had often preach'd in the course of his travels. His delivery of the latter was so improv'd by frequent repetitions that every accent, every emphasis, every modulation of voice, was so perfectly well turn'd and well plac'd, that, without being interested in the subject, one could not help being pleas'd with the discourse; a pleasure of much the same kind with that receiv'd from an excellent piece of musick. This is an advantage itinerant preachers have over those who are stationary, as the latter can not well improve their delivery of a sermon by so many rehearsals.
paras.z: 听他讲得多了，我就能很容易地分辨出哪些是新写的讲道，哪些是他在旅途中讲过多次的。后一种讲道因为经常重复，讲得大有改进，每一个重音，每一处强调，每一次声调的抑扬，都处理得那样完美，安排得那样恰当，即使对题目不感兴趣，也不能不为这篇讲话感到愉快；这种愉快同听一支绝妙的乐曲所得到的愉快大致是同一类的。这是巡回传道的人胜过固定在一处的人的一个长处，因为后者不大可能通过这么多次的排练来改进一篇讲道的讲法。

paras.e: His writing and printing from time to time gave great advantage to his enemies; unguarded expressions, and even erroneous opinions, delivered in preaching, might have been afterwards explain'd or qualifi'd by supposing others that might have accompani'd them, or they might have been deny'd; but litera scripta manet. Critics attack'd his writings violently, and with so much appearance of reason as to diminish the number of his votaries and prevent their encrease; so that I am of opinion if he had never written any thing, he would have left behind him a much more numerous and important sect, and his reputation might in that case have been still growing, even after his death, as there being nothing of his writing on which to found a censure and give him a lower character, his proselytes would be left at liberty to feign for him as great a variety of excellence as their enthusiastic admiration might wish him to have possessed.
paras.z: 他不时写作和付印的东西，给了他的仇人很大的便宜。讲道时说出口的不谨慎的词句，甚至错误的见解，事后还可以解释或者加以限定，说当时还有别的话相伴，或者干脆否认；但是“写下来的字是留存的”。批评家们猛烈地攻击他的著作，而且看上去很有道理，以致减少了他的信徒的数目，阻止了他们的增加。所以我认为，如果他从来没有写过任何东西，他身后会留下一个人数多得多、也重要得多的教派，他的名声在那种情况下甚至在他死后也许还会不断增长；因为没有他写的东西可以作为指责的根据而降低他的声望，他的皈依者就可以随意替他虚构出各种各样的优点，他们狂热的崇拜希望他有多少，就有多少。

paras.e: My business was now continually augmenting, and my circumstances growing daily easier, my newspaper having become very profitable, as being for a time almost the only one in this and the neighbouring provinces. I experienced, too, the truth of the observation, "that after getting the first hundred pound, it is more easy to get the second," money itself being of a prolific nature.
paras.z: 这时我的生意不断扩大，我的境况一天比一天宽裕，我的报纸已经非常赚钱，因为有一段时间它几乎是本殖民地和邻近各殖民地唯一的报纸。我也体会到了这句话的道理：“挣到头一百镑以后，再挣第二个一百镑就容易些了。”钱这种东西本身是能生钱的。

paras.e: The partnership at Carolina having succeeded, I was encourag'd to engage in others, and to promote several of my workmen, who had behaved well, by establishing them with printing-houses in different colonies, on the same terms with that in Carolina. Most of them did well, being enabled at the end of our term, six years, to purchase the types of me and go on working for themselves, by which means several families were raised. Partnerships often finish in quarrels; but I was happy in this, that mine were all carried on and ended amicably, owing, I think, a good deal to the precaution of having very explicitly settled, in our articles, every thing to be done by or expected from each partner, so that there was nothing to dispute, which precaution I would therefore recommend to all who enter into partnerships; for, whatever esteem partners may have for, and confidence in each other at the time of the contract, little jealousies and disgusts may arise, with ideas of inequality in the care and burden of the business, etc., which are attended often with breach of friendship and of the connection, perhaps with lawsuits and other disagreeable consequences.
paras.z: 卡罗来纳的合伙生意成功了，这鼓励我再办几处，提拔了几个表现好的工人，按照同卡罗来纳那一处相同的条件，让他们在不同的殖民地开办印刷所。他们大多数都干得不错，在我们六年的合伙期满时，能够从我手里买下铅字，继续为自己干下去，好几个家庭就这样兴旺起来。合伙往往以争吵告终；但我在这方面很幸运，我的合伙生意全都是在友好中进行、在友好中结束的。我想这在很大程度上要归功于一种预防措施：我们在条款里把每个合伙人该做的事、该得的东西都规定得十分明确，因此没有什么可争的。所以我愿意把这种预防措施推荐给一切合伙的人；因为，不管合伙人在订约的时候彼此多么敬重、多么信任，日后也可能生出小小的猜忌和不快，觉得在照管生意和承担责任上不平等，等等，这往往导致友谊破裂、关系断绝，也许还会打官司，带来别的不愉快的后果。

paras.e: I had, on the whole, abundant reason to be satisfied with my being established in Pennsylvania. There were, however, two things that I regretted, there being no provision for defense, nor for a compleat education of youth; no militia, nor any college. I therefore, in 1743, drew up a proposal for establishing an academy; and at that time, thinking the Reverend Mr. Peters, who was out of employ, a fit person to superintend such an institution, I communicated the project to him; but he, having more profitable views in the service of the proprietaries, which succeeded, declin'd the undertaking; and, not knowing another at that time suitable for such a trust, I let the scheme lie a while dormant. I succeeded better the next year, 1744, in proposing and establishing a Philosophical Society. The paper I wrote for that purpose will be found among my writings, when collected.
paras.z: 总的说来，我有充分的理由对自己在宾夕法尼亚立业感到满意。不过有两件事使我遗憾：这里既没有防务方面的设施，也没有完整的青年教育的设施；没有民兵，也没有任何学院。所以我在 1743 年起草了一份创办一所学校的建议；那时我想，彼得斯牧师先生正赋闲在家，是主持这样一个机构的合适人选，就把计划告诉了他。可是他另有替业主们效力的更有利可图的打算（后来实现了），就谢绝了这件事；我当时又不知道还有谁适合担当这样的重托，就让这个计划暂时搁了下来。第二年，1744 年，我提议并创办了一个哲学学会，这件事倒比较成功。我为此写的那篇文章，将来我的著作汇集起来的时候，可以在里面找到。

paras.e: With respect to defense, Spain having been several years at war against Great Britain, and being at length join'd by France, which brought us into great danger; and the laboured and long-continued endeavour of our governor, Thomas, to prevail with our Quaker Assembly to pass a militia law, and make other provisions for the security of the province, having proved abortive, I determined to try what might be done by a voluntary association of the people. To promote this, I first wrote and published a pamphlet, entitled Plain Truth, in which I stated our defenceless situation in strong lights, with the necessity of union and discipline for our defense, and promis'd to propose in a few days an association, to be generally signed for that purpose. The pamphlet had a sudden and surprising effect. I was call'd upon for the instrument of association, and having settled the draft of it with a few friends, I appointed a meeting of the citizens in the large building before mentioned. The house was pretty full; I had prepared a number of printed copies, and provided pens and ink dispers'd all over the room. I harangued them a little on the subject, read the paper, and explained it, and then distributed the copies, which were eagerly signed, not the least objection being made.
paras.z: 关于防务，西班牙同英国交战已有几年，最后法国也加入了西班牙一方，这使我们处在很大的危险之中；而我们的总督托马斯长期费力地劝说我们那个由贵格会教徒把持的议会通过一项民兵法，并为本殖民地的安全采取其他措施，结果毫无成效。于是我决心试一试，看看靠民众自愿结社能做成什么。为了推动这件事，我先写了一本小册子发表，题为《明白的真相》，其中用强烈的笔调陈述了我们毫无防御的处境，以及为了自卫必须联合起来、加以训练，并且许诺几天之内就提出一份结社公约，供大家为此普遍签署。这本小册子产生了突然而惊人的效果。人们来向我要那份结社公约；我同几位朋友商定了草稿，就约定在前面提到的那座大建筑里召开一次市民大会。屋子里坐得相当满；我事先印好了许多份公约，又在屋子里各处摆好了笔和墨水。我就这个题目对他们稍稍讲了几句，把公约念了一遍，作了解释，然后把印好的公约分发下去，大家踊跃地签了名，没有人提出一点异议。

paras.e: When the company separated, and the papers were collected, we found above twelve hundred hands; and, other copies being dispersed in the country, the subscribers amounted at length to upward of ten thousand. These all furnished themselves as soon as they could with arms, formed themselves into companies and regiments, chose their own officers, and met every week to be instructed in the manual exercise, and other parts of military discipline. The women, by subscriptions among themselves, provided silk colors, which they presented to the companies, painted with different devices and mottos, which I supplied.
paras.z: 散会以后，把公约收上来，我们发现签名的有一千二百多人；别的副本又散发到乡下，最后签名的人达到一万以上。这些人都尽快自备了武器，自己编成连和团，选出了自己的军官，每星期集合一次，接受持枪操练和其他军事训练。妇女们自己募捐，置办了丝质的旗帜送给各连，上面画着不同的图案和题词，这些都是我提供的。

paras.e: The officers of the companies composing the Philadelphia regiment, being met, chose me for their colonel; but, conceiving myself unfit, I declin'd that station, and recommended Mr. Lawrence, a fine person, and man of influence, who was accordingly appointed. I then propos'd a lottery to defray the expense of building a battery below the town, and furnishing it with cannon. It filled expeditiously, and the battery was soon erected, the merlons being fram'd of logs and fill'd with earth. We bought some old cannon from Boston, but, these not being sufficient, we wrote to England for more, soliciting, at the same time, our proprietaries for some assistance, tho' without much expectation of obtaining it.
paras.z: 组成费城团的各连军官开了会，推选我当他们的上校；但我自认为不合适，谢绝了这个职位，推荐了劳伦斯先生，他仪表堂堂，又是个有影响的人，于是他被任命了。然后我提议发行一次彩票，用来支付在城下游修筑一座炮台并配备大炮的费用。彩票很快就认购一空，炮台不久就修起来了，炮台的胸墙是用原木搭成框架、里面填土筑成的。我们从波士顿买了几门旧炮，但这些还不够，我们就写信到英国去再要，同时请求我们的业主们给些帮助，虽然并不怎么指望能得到。

paras.e: Meanwhile, Colonel Lawrence, William Allen, Abram Taylor, Esqr., and myself were sent to New York by the associators, commission'd to borrow some cannon of Governor Clinton. He at first refus'd us peremptorily; but at dinner with his council, where there was great drinking of Madeira wine, as the custom of that place then was, he softened by degrees, and said he would lend us six. After a few more bumpers he advanc'd to ten; and at length he very good-naturedly conceded eighteen. They were fine cannon, eighteen-pounders, with their carriages, which we soon transported and mounted on our battery, where the associators kept a nightly guard while the war lasted, and among the rest I regularly took my turn of duty there as a common soldier.
paras.z: 同时，劳伦斯上校、威廉·艾伦、艾布拉姆·泰勒先生和我受结社成员的委派去纽约，向克林顿总督借几门大炮。他起初断然拒绝了我们；但是同他的参事会一起吃饭的时候，照当时那里的风俗，大家痛饮马德拉酒，他渐渐软了下来，说可以借给我们六门。又干了几大杯之后，他加到十门；最后他十分和气地让步到十八门。那都是上好的大炮，十八磅炮，还带着炮架；我们不久就把它们运来安放在我们的炮台上。战争期间，结社成员每夜在那里守卫，我也同其他人一样，作为一名普通士兵按时轮班值勤。

paras.e: My activity in these operations was agreeable to the governor and council; they took me into confidence, and I was consulted by them in every measure wherein their concurrence was thought useful to the association. Calling in the aid of religion, I propos'd to them the proclaiming a fast, to promote reformation, and implore the blessing of Heaven on our undertaking. They embrac'd the motion; but, as it was the first fast ever thought of in the province, the secretary had no precedent from which to draw the proclamation. My education in New England, where a fast is proclaimed every year, was here of some advantage: I drew it in the accustomed stile, it was translated into German, printed in both languages, and divulg'd thro' the province. This gave the clergy of the different sects an opportunity of influencing their congregations to join in the association, and it would probably have been general among all but Quakers if the peace had not soon interven'd.
paras.z: 我在这些活动中的积极表现，很合总督和参事会的心意；他们把我当作心腹，凡是认为他们的赞同对结社有用的每一项措施，他们都同我商量。为了借助宗教的力量，我向他们提议宣布举行一次斋戒，以促进风气的改良，并祈求上天保佑我们的事业。他们欣然接受了这个动议；但因为这是本殖民地破天荒头一次想到斋戒，秘书找不到可以依据来起草文告的先例。我在新英格兰受的教育在这里派上了一点用场，那里每年都要宣布斋戒：我照惯用的格式起草了文告，把它译成德文，用两种文字印出来，在全殖民地公布。这给了各教派的牧师一个机会，去影响他们的会众参加结社；要不是和平不久就来临，除了贵格会教徒，大概所有的人都会普遍参加。

paras.e: It was thought by some of my friends that, by my activity in these affairs, I should offend that sect, and thereby lose my interest in the Assembly of the province, where they formed a great majority. A young gentleman who had likewise some friends in the House, and wished to succeed me as their clerk, acquainted me that it was decided to displace me at the next election; and he, therefore, in good will, advis'd me to resign, as more consistent with my honour than being turn'd out. My answer to him was, that I had read or heard of some public man who made it a rule never to ask for an office, and never to refuse one when offer'd to him. "I approve," says I, "of his rule, and will practice it with a small addition; I shall never ask, never refuse, nor ever resign an office. If they will have my office of clerk to dispose of to another, they shall take it from me. I will not, by giving it up, lose my right of some time or other making reprisals on my adversaries." I heard, however, no more of this; I was chosen again unanimously as usual at the next election. Possibly, as they dislik'd my late intimacy with the members of council, who had join'd the governors in all the disputes about military preparations, with which the House had long been harass'd, they might have been pleas'd if I would voluntarily have left them; but they did not care to displace me on account merely of my zeal for the association, and they could not well give another reason.
paras.z: 我的一些朋友认为，我在这些事情上这样积极，会得罪那个教派，从而失去我在本殖民地议会里的地位，因为他们在议会里占了大多数。有一位年轻的绅士，在议院里也有几个朋友，想接替我当书记，他告诉我，已经决定在下次选举时把我撤换；因此他好意劝我辞职，说这比被人撵走更合我的体面。我回答他说，我曾经读到或者听说过某一位公众人物，他立下一条规矩：从不谋求职位，职位送上门来也从不拒绝。我说：“我赞成他的规矩，并且要稍加补充来实行它：我决不谋求，决不拒绝，也决不辞去一个职位。如果他们要把我的书记职位拿去给别人，那就让他们从我手里拿走。我不会主动放弃它，从而失去有朝一日向我的对手报复的权利。”不过这件事后来就没有下文了；下一次选举时，我照常又被一致选上了。也许，他们不喜欢我近来同参事会成员过从甚密——在关于军备的一切争论中，这些参事都站在总督一边，议院长期以来为这些争论所苦——如果我自愿离开他们，他们可能会高兴；但他们不愿仅仅因为我热心结社而撤换我，又找不出别的像样的理由。

paras.e: Indeed I had some cause to believe that the defense of the country was not disagreeable to any of them, provided they were not requir'd to assist in it. And I found that a much greater number of them than I could have imagined, tho' against offensive war, were clearly for the defensive. Many pamphlets pro and con were publish'd on the subject, and some by good Quakers, in favour of defense, which I believe convinc'd most of their younger people.
paras.z: 说实在的，我有理由相信，保卫这块地方并不是他们任何人所不乐见的，只要不要求他们出力就行。我还发现，他们中间有比我想象的多得多的人，虽然反对进攻性的战争，却明确赞成防御性的战争。关于这个问题，发表了许多赞成和反对的小册子，其中有几本是虔诚的贵格会教徒写的，赞成自卫，我相信这使他们的大多数年轻人信服了。

paras.e: A transaction in our fire company gave me some insight into their prevailing sentiments. It had been propos'd that we should encourage the scheme for building a battery by laying out the present stock, then about sixty pounds, in tickets of the lottery. By our rules, no money could be dispos'd of till the next meeting after the proposal. The company consisted of thirty members, of which twenty-two were Quakers, and eight only of other persuasions. We eight punctually attended the meeting; but, tho' we thought that some of the Quakers would join us, we were by no means sure of a majority. Only one Quaker, Mr. James Morris, appear'd to oppose the measure. He expressed much sorrow that it had ever been propos'd, as he said Friends were all against it, and it would create such discord as might break up the company. We told him that we saw no reason for that; we were the minority, and if Friends were against the measure, and outvoted us, we must and should, agreeably to the usage of all societies, submit. When the hour for business arriv'd it was mov'd to put the vote; he allow'd we might then do it by the rules, but, as he could assure us that a number of members intended to be present for the purpose of opposing it, it would be but candid to allow a little time for their appearing.
paras.z: 我们消防队里的一件事，使我对他们中间占上风的想法有了几分了解。有人提议，我们应当把队里现有的款子——当时大约六十镑——用来买彩票，以支持修筑炮台的计划。照我们的规章，任何款项都要到提议之后的下一次会议才能动用。全队三十个队员，其中二十二个是贵格会教徒，只有八个属于别的教派。我们这八个人准时到会；虽然我们以为会有几个贵格会教徒站在我们一边，却一点也没有把握得到多数。只有一位贵格会教徒詹姆斯·莫里斯先生到场反对这项措施。他对竟有人提出这种建议深表遗憾，因为他说教友们全都反对，这会造成不和，说不定会使消防队解散。我们对他说，我们看不出有什么理由会这样；我们是少数，如果教友们反对这项措施，票数压倒我们，那么按照一切团体的惯例，我们必须服从，也一定服从。到了议事的时间，有人动议付表决；他承认照规章那时可以表决，但是他可以向我们保证，有好些队员打算到会来反对，所以稍等一会儿让他们到场，才算光明正大。

paras.e: While we were disputing this, a waiter came to tell me two gentlemen below desir'd to speak with me. I went down, and found they were two of our Quaker members. They told me there were eight of them assembled at a tavern just by; that they were determin'd to come and vote with us if there should be occasion, which they hop'd would not be the case, and desir'd we would not call for their assistance if we could do without it, as their voting for such a measure might embroil them with their elders and friends. Being thus secure of a majority, I went up, and after a little seeming hesitation, agreed to a delay of another hour. This Mr. Morris allow'd to be extreamly fair. Not one of his opposing friends appear'd, at which he express'd great surprize; and, at the expiration of the hour, we carry'd the resolution eight to one; and as, of the twenty-two Quakers, eight were ready to vote with us, and thirteen, by their absence, manifested that they were not inclin'd to oppose the measure, I afterward estimated the proportion of Quakers sincerely against defense as one to twenty-one only; for these were all regular members of that society, and in good reputation among them, and had due notice of what was propos'd at that meeting.
paras.z: 我们正在为此争论，一个侍者来告诉我，楼下有两位先生想同我说话。我下了楼，发现是我们队里的两位贵格会教徒。他们告诉我，他们有八个人聚在附近的一家酒馆里；如果有必要，他们决心过来同我们投一样的票，但希望不至于如此，并且要求我们，如果没有他们也行，就不要叫他们来帮忙，因为投票赞成这样一项措施，可能使他们同长老和教友们闹得不愉快。这样我有了多数的把握，就上楼去，装作稍稍犹豫了一下，同意再推迟一个小时。莫里斯先生承认这是极其公道的。他那些反对的朋友一个也没有来，他对此大表惊讶；一小时过后，我们以八票对一票通过了决议。二十二个贵格会教徒中，有八个准备同我们投一样的票，另有十三个用缺席表明他们无意反对这项措施，所以我后来估计，真心反对防卫的贵格会教徒的比例只是二十一分之一；因为这些人都是那个教派的正式成员，在他们中间名声很好，而且事先都接到了通知，知道那次会上要提议什么。

paras.e: The honorable and learned Mr. Logan, who had always been of that sect, was one who wrote an address to them, declaring his approbation of defensive war, and supporting his opinion by many strong arguments. He put into my hands sixty pounds to be laid out in lottery tickets for the battery, with directions to apply what prizes might be drawn wholly to that service. He told me the following anecdote of his old master, William Penn, respecting defense. He came over from England, when a young man, with that proprietary, and as his secretary. It was war-time, and their ship was chas'd by an armed vessel, suppos'd to be an enemy. Their captain prepar'd for defense; but told William Penn, and his company of Quakers, that he did not expect their assistance, and they might retire into the cabin, which they did, except James Logan, who chose to stay upon deck, and was quarter'd to a gun. The suppos'd enemy prov'd a friend, so there was no fighting; but when the secretary went down to communicate the intelligence, William Penn rebuk'd him severely for staying upon deck, and undertaking to assist in defending the vessel, contrary to the principles of Friends, especially as it had not been required by the captain. This reproof, being before all the company, piqu'd the secretary, who answer'd, "I being thy servant, why did thee not order me to come down? But thee was willing enough that I should stay and help to fight the ship when thee thought there was danger."
paras.z: 可敬而博学的洛根先生一向是那个教派的人，他就是写过文章向他们呼吁的人之一，声明他赞成防御性的战争，并且用许多有力的论据支持自己的意见。他交给我六十镑，让我替炮台买彩票，并嘱咐说，如果中了奖，奖金全部用于同一用途。他给我讲了下面这件关于他的老主人威廉·佩恩对防卫的态度的逸事。他年轻时作为那位业主的秘书，同他一起从英国渡海而来。当时正值战争，他们的船被一艘武装船只追赶，以为是敌船。船长准备抵抗，但对威廉·佩恩和他那一群贵格会教徒说，他并不指望他们帮忙，他们可以退到舱里去。他们都去了，只有詹姆斯·洛根宁愿留在甲板上，被分派去守一门炮。那艘被当作敌船的船原来是友船，所以没有打起来；可是这位秘书下去报告消息的时候，威廉·佩恩严厉地责备他，说他留在甲板上、承担起协助保卫船只的任务，违背了教友的原则，何况船长并没有这样要求。这番当众的责备惹恼了秘书，他回答说：“我既是你的仆人，你为什么不命令我下来？可是你以为有危险的时候，倒很愿意我留在上面帮着打仗保船。”

paras.e: My being many years in the Assembly, the majority of which were constantly Quakers, gave me frequent opportunities of seeing the embarrassment given them by their principle against war, whenever application was made to them, by order of the crown, to grant aids for military purposes. They were unwilling to offend government, on the one hand, by a direct refusal; and their friends, the body of the Quakers, on the other, by a compliance contrary to their principles; hence a variety of evasions to avoid complying, and modes of disguising the compliance when it became unavoidable. The common mode at last was, to grant money under the phrase of its being "for the king's use," and never to inquire how it was applied.
paras.z: 我在议会里多年，议会的多数一直是贵格会教徒，这使我常常有机会看到，每逢奉国王之命要求他们拨款用于军事目的时，他们那条反对战争的原则给他们带来的窘迫。一方面，他们不愿意直截了当地拒绝而得罪政府；另一方面，又不愿意违背自己的原则去答应，而得罪他们的朋友，也就是贵格会的全体教友。于是就有了各种各样避免照办的遁词，以及在无法避免时把照办掩饰起来的方式。最后，通常的方式是拨一笔款，名目是“供国王之用”，而且从不过问它是怎样用的。

paras.e: But, if the demand was not directly from the crown, that phrase was found not so proper, and some other was to be invented. As, when powder was wanting (I think it was for the garrison at Louisburg), and the government of New England solicited a grant of some from Pennsilvania, which was much urg'd on the House by Governor Thomas, they could not grant money to buy powder, because that was an ingredient of war; but they voted an aid to New England of three thousand pounds, to be put into the hands of the governor, and appropriated it for the purchasing of bread, flour, wheat, or other grain. Some of the council, desirous of giving the House still further embarrassment, advis'd the governor not to accept provision, as not being the thing he had demanded; but be reply'd, "I shall take the money, for I understand very well their meaning; other grain is gunpowder," which he accordingly bought, and they never objected to it. [10]
paras.z: 但是，如果要求不是直接来自国王，这个名目就不大合适，必须另想一个。比如，有一回缺火药（我想是为了路易斯堡的驻军），新英格兰政府请求宾夕法尼亚拨给一些，托马斯总督极力敦促议院答应。他们不能拨款买火药，因为那是战争的要素；但是他们投票通过拨给新英格兰三千镑的援助，交到总督手里，指定用来购买面包、面粉、小麦或“其他谷物”。参事会里有些人想让议院更加难堪，劝总督不要接受粮食，因为那不是他所要求的东西；但他回答说：“我要收下这笔钱，因为我很明白他们的意思；‘其他谷物’就是火药。”他于是买了火药，他们也从没有提出过异议。[10]

paras.e: [10] See the votes.--[Marg. note.]
paras.z: [10] 参看表决记录。——［页边注］

paras.e: It was in allusion to this fact that, when in our fire company we feared the success of our proposal in favour of the lottery, and I had said to my friend Mr. Syng, one of our members, "If we fail, let us move the purchase of a fire-engine with the money; the Quakers can have no objection to that; and then, if you nominate me and I you as a committee for that purpose, we will buy a great gun, which is certainly a fire-engine." "I see," says he, "you have improv'd by being so long in the Assembly; your equivocal project would be just a match for their wheat or other grain."
paras.z: 我就是暗指这件事。当时在我们的消防队里，我们担心支持彩票的提议通不过，我对我的朋友、队员之一辛格先生说：“如果我们失败了，我们就动议用这笔钱买一台救火机；贵格会教徒不可能反对这个。然后，你提名我、我提名你组成一个办这件事的委员会，我们就去买一尊大炮，那肯定是一台‘火机’。”他说：“我看得出来，你在议会里待了这么久，大有长进了；你这个模棱两可的计划，正好同他们的‘小麦或其他谷物’旗鼓相当。”

paras.e: These embarrassments that the Quakers suffer'd from having establish'd and published it as one of their principles that no kind of war was lawful, and which, being once published, they could not afterwards, however they might change their minds, easily get rid of, reminds me of what I think a more prudent conduct in another sect among us, that of the Dunkers. I was acquainted with one of its founders, Michael Welfare, soon after it appear'd. He complain'd to me that they were grievously calumniated by the zealots of other persuasions, and charg'd with abominable principles and practices, to which they were utter strangers. I told him this had always been the case with new sects, and that, to put a stop to such abuse, I imagin'd it might be well to publish the articles of their belief, and the rules of their discipline. He said that it had been propos'd among them, but not agreed to, for this reason: "When we were first drawn together as a society," says he, "it had pleased God to enlighten our minds so far as to see that some doctrines, which we once esteemed truths, were errors; and that others, which we had esteemed errors, were real truths. From time to time He has been pleased to afford us farther light, and our principles have been improving, and our errors diminishing. Now we are not sure that we are arrived at the end of this progression, and at the perfection of spiritual or theological knowledge; and we fear that, if we should once print our confession of faith, we should feel ourselves as if bound and confin'd by it, and perhaps be unwilling to receive farther improvement, and our successors still more so, as conceiving what we their elders and founders had done, to be something sacred, never to be departed from."
paras.z: 贵格会教徒把“任何战争都不合法”定为他们的原则之一并且公之于世，一经公布，以后不管他们的想法怎样改变，也不容易摆脱了，由此吃了这些苦头。这使我想起我们这里另一个教派——邓克派——的做法，我认为要审慎得多。那个教派出现不久，我就认识了它的创始人之一迈克尔·韦尔费尔。他向我诉苦说，别的教派的狂热分子恶毒地诽谤他们，指控他们有种种可憎的原则和行为，而那些他们其实毫不相干。我对他说，新教派向来都是这样的；我想，要制止这种诽谤，不妨把他们的信条和纪律规章公布出来。他说，他们中间有人提议过，但没有得到同意，理由是这样的。他说：“我们最初聚到一起成为一个团体的时候，上帝乐意启迪我们的心智，使我们看到，有些我们曾经认为是真理的教义其实是谬误，另一些我们曾经认为是谬误的却是真正的真理。他不时乐意给我们进一步的光照，我们的原则一直在改进，我们的错误一直在减少。现在我们没有把握说我们已经走到了这个进程的尽头，达到了属灵的或神学的知识的完善；我们担心，一旦把我们的信仰告白印了出来，我们会觉得自己好像被它束缚住、限制住了，也许不愿再接受进一步的改进，而我们的后继者更会如此，因为他们会把我们这些长辈和创始人所做的事看成神圣的东西，永远不可背离。”

paras.e: This modesty in a sect is perhaps a singular instance in the history of mankind, every other sect supposing itself in possession of all truth, and that those who differ are so far in the wrong; like a man traveling in foggy weather, those at some distance before him on the road he sees wrapped up in the fog, as well as those behind him, and also the people in the fields on each side, but near him all appears clear, tho' in truth he is as much in the fog as any of them. To avoid this kind of embarrassment, the Quakers have of late years been gradually declining the public service in the Assembly and in the magistracy, choosing rather to quit their power than their principle.
paras.z: 一个教派有这样的谦虚，在人类历史上也许是绝无仅有的例子。别的每一个教派都以为自己掌握了全部真理，凡是持不同意见的人，在那不同之处就是错的；这就像一个人在雾天赶路，他看见路上前面稍远的人裹在雾里，后面的人也是，两旁田野里的人也是，可是他身边看来却一片清朗，其实他同他们任何一个人一样身在雾中。为了避免这一类窘境，贵格会教徒近年来逐渐辞去议会和地方官的公职，宁愿放弃权力，也不放弃原则。

paras.e: In order of time, I should have mentioned before, that having, in 1742, invented an open stove for the better warming of rooms, and at the same time saving fuel, as the fresh air admitted was warmed in entering, I made a present of the model to Mr. Robert Grace, one of my early friends, who, having an iron-furnace, found the casting of the plates for these stoves a profitable thing, as they were growing in demand.
