To promote that demand, I wrote and published a pamphlet, entitled "An Account of the new-invented Pennsylvania Fireplaces; wherein their Construction and Manner of Operation is particularly explained; their Advantages above every other Method of warming Rooms demonstrated; and all Objections that have been raised against the Use of them answered and obviated," etc. This pamphlet had a good effect. Gov'r. Thomas was so pleas'd with the construction of this stove, as described in it, that he offered to give me a patent for the sole vending of them for a term of years; but I declin'd it from a principle which has ever weighed with me on such occasions, viz., That, as we enjoy great advantages from the inventions of others, we should be glad of an opportunity to serve others by any invention of ours; and this we should do freely and generously.
paras.z: 按时间的先后，我本该早些提到，1742 年我发明了一种敞开式的火炉，既能更好地取暖，同时又节省燃料，因为进入室内的新鲜空气在进来时就被烘暖了。我把模型送给了我早年的朋友之一罗伯特·格雷斯先生；他有一座炼铁炉，发现铸造这种火炉的铁板是有利可图的事，因为需求在不断增加。为了推广这种需求，我写了一本小册子发表，题为《新发明的宾夕法尼亚壁炉说明：其中详细解释其构造和使用方法，证明其优于其他一切室内取暖方法之处，并对反对使用它的一切意见加以答复和排除》，等等。这本小册子效果很好。托马斯总督对其中所描述的这种火炉的构造非常满意，提出要给我一项专利，让我在若干年内独家销售；但我谢绝了，这是出于一条原则，每逢这种场合，这条原则在我心里总是很有分量，那就是：既然我们从别人的发明中享受到很大的好处，我们就应当乐于有机会用自己的任何发明为别人服务；而且应当无偿地、慷慨地这样做。

paras.e: An ironmonger in London however, assuming a good deal of my pamphlet, and working it up into his own, and making some small changes in the machine, which rather hurt its operation, got a patent for it there, and made, as I was told, a little fortune by it. And this is not the only instance of patents taken out for my inventions by others, tho' not always with the same success, which I never contested, as having no desire of profiting by patents myself, and hating disputes. The use of these fireplaces in very many houses, both of this and the neighbouring colonies, has been, and is, a great saving of wood to the inhabitants.
paras.z: 可是伦敦有一个铁器商，把我那本小册子的许多内容拿去，改头换面写成他自己的，又对那个装置作了一些小小的改动，这些改动反而有损它的功效，然后在那里取得了专利，据说还因此发了一笔小财。别人拿我的发明去申请专利，这并不是唯一的一回，虽然并不总是同样成功；我从不同他们争，因为我自己无意靠专利获利，又讨厌争执。这种壁炉在本殖民地和邻近各殖民地的许许多多人家里使用，过去和现在都为居民节省了大量的木柴。

paras.e: Peace being concluded, and the association business therefore at an end, I turn'd my thoughts again to the affair of establishing an academy. The first step I took was to associate in the design a number of active friends, of whom the Junto furnished a good part; the next was to write and publish a pamphlet, entitled Proposals Relating to the Education of Youth in Pennsylvania. This I distributed among the principal inhabitants gratis; and as soon as I could suppose their minds a little prepared by the perusal of it, I set on foot a subscription for opening and supporting an academy; it was to be paid in quotas yearly for five years; by so dividing it, I judg'd the subscription might be larger, and I believe it was so, amounting to no less, if I remember right, than five thousand pounds.
paras.z: 和约缔结了，结社的事因此告一段落，我的心思又转到创办一所学校的事情上来。我走的第一步，是邀集一批积极的朋友参加这个计划，其中很大一部分是讲读社的人；第二步，是写了一本小册子发表，题为《有关宾夕法尼亚青年教育的建议》。我把它免费分送给有地位的居民；一到我估计他们读过以后思想上有了一点准备，就发起募捐，用来开办并维持一所学校。捐款分五年按年交纳；我判断，这样分开来交，认捐的数目会大一些，我相信确实如此，如果我没有记错，总数不下五千镑。

paras.e: In the introduction to these proposals, I stated their publication, not as an act of mine, but of some publick-spirited gentlemen, avoiding as much as I could, according to my usual rule, the presenting myself to the publick as the author of any scheme for their benefit.
paras.z: 在这些建议的引言里，我把它们的发表说成不是我个人的举动，而是几位热心公益的绅士的举动；我照自己一贯的规矩，尽量避免以任何为公众谋利益的计划的发起人的面目出现在公众面前。

paras.e: The subscribers, to carry the project into immediate execution, chose out of their number twenty-four trustees, and appointed Mr. Francis, then attorney-general, and myself to draw up constitutions for the government of the academy; which being done and signed, a house was hired, masters engag'd, and the schools opened, I think, in the same year, 1749.
paras.z: 为了把计划立即付诸实行，捐款人从自己中间选出了二十四位董事，并指定当时的检察长弗朗西斯先生和我起草管理学校的章程。章程写好并签署之后，就租了一所房子，聘了教师，学校开了学，我想是在同一年，1749 年。

paras.e: The scholars increasing fast, the house was soon found too small, and we were looking out for a piece of ground, properly situated, with intention to build, when Providence threw into our way a large house ready built, which, with a few alterations, might well serve our purpose. This was the building before mentioned, erected by the hearers of Mr. Whitefield, and was obtained for us in the following manner.
paras.z: 学生增加得很快，不久就发现房子太小了。我们正在物色一块位置合适的地皮，打算盖房子，这时上天把一所现成的大房子送到了我们面前，稍加改造就很合我们的用场。这就是前面提到的、由怀特菲尔德先生的听众们盖的那座建筑，我们是这样把它弄到手的。

paras.e: It is to be noted that the contributions to this building being made by people of different sects, care was taken in the nomination of trustees, in whom the building and ground was to be vested, that a predominancy should not be given to any sect, lest in time that predominancy might be a means of appropriating the whole to the use of such sect, contrary to the original intention. It was therefore that one of each sect was appointed, viz., one Church-of-England man, one Presbyterian, one Baptist, one Moravian, etc., those, in case of vacancy by death, were to fill it by election from among the contributors. The Moravian happen'd not to please his colleagues, and on his death they resolved to have no other of that sect. The difficulty then was, how to avoid having two of some other sect, by means of the new choice.
paras.z: 要说明的是，这座建筑的捐款来自不同教派的人，所以在提名受托人——房子和地皮是交给他们掌管的——的时候，特别留意不让任何一个教派占优势，以免日久之后这种优势成了手段，违背原意把全部房产拨给那个教派使用。因此每个教派指定了一个人，就是：一个英国国教徒，一个长老会教徒，一个浸礼会教徒，一个摩拉维亚教徒，等等；遇有人去世出缺，由其余的人从捐款人当中选举补上。那位摩拉维亚教徒碰巧不讨同事们的喜欢，他死后，他们决定不再要那个教派的人。这时的难题是，新选一个人，怎样才能避免某个别的教派有两个人。

paras.e: Several persons were named, and for that reason not agreed to. At length one mention'd me, with the observation that I was merely an honest man, and of no sect at all, which prevail'd with them to chuse me. The enthusiasm which existed when the house was built had long since abated, and its trustees had not been able to procure fresh contributions for paying the ground-rent, and discharging some other debts the building had occasion'd, which embarrass'd them greatly. Being now a member of both setts of trustees, that for the building and that for the Academy, I had a good opportunity of negotiating with both, and brought them finally to an agreement, by which the trustees for the building were to cede it to those of the academy, the latter undertaking to discharge the debt, to keep for ever open in the building a large hall for occasional preachers, according to the original intention, and maintain a free-school for the instruction of poor children. Writings were accordingly drawn, and on paying the debts the trustees of the academy were put in possession of the premises; and by dividing the great and lofty hall into stories, and different rooms above and below for the several schools, and purchasing some additional ground, the whole was soon made fit for our purpose, and the scholars remov'd into the building. The care and trouble of agreeing with the workmen, purchasing materials, and superintending the work, fell upon me; and I went thro' it the more cheerfully, as it did not then interfere with my private business, having the year before taken a very able, industrious, and honest partner, Mr. David Hall, with whose character I was well acquainted, as he had work'd for me four years. He took off my hands all care of the printing-office, paying me punctually my share of the profits. This partnership continued eighteen years, successfully for us both.
paras.z: 提了好几个人的名，都因为这个缘故没有通过。最后有人提到我，说我只是一个诚实的人，根本不属于任何教派，这就说动了他们选了我。盖房子时的那股热情早已消退，受托人一直募不到新的捐款来付地租、偿还这座建筑引起的另外一些债务，这使他们十分为难。这时我既是这座建筑的受托人，又是学校的董事，两个班子我都是成员，就有了同双方磋商的好机会，最后促成他们达成了协议：建筑的受托人把房子让给学校的董事，后者承担清偿债务，按照原来的宗旨在房子里永远保留一个大厅供偶尔来的讲道人使用，并且办一所免费学校教育贫苦儿童。于是立了文书，学校的董事们付清了债务，接管了房产。我们把那个又大又高的大厅隔成几层，上上下下分出不同的房间给各个班级使用，又添购了一些地皮，不久就把整座房子改造得合乎我们的用途，学生们搬了进去。同工匠讲价钱、采购材料、监督工程，这些操心费力的事都落在我身上；我干得很起劲，因为那时这并不妨碍我自己的生意——前一年我已经找了一位非常能干、勤勉而诚实的合伙人戴维·霍尔先生，他的为人我很了解，因为他替我干过四年。他把印刷所的一切操心事都从我手里接了过去，按时把我应得的利润付给我。这次合伙持续了十八年，对我们双方都很成功。

paras.e: The trustees of the academy, after a while, were incorporated by a charter from the governor; their funds were increas'd by contributions in Britain and grants of land from the proprietaries, to which the Assembly has since made considerable addition; and thus was established the present University of Philadelphia. I have been continued one of its trustees from the beginning, now near forty years, and have had the very great pleasure of seeing a number of the youth who have receiv'd their education in it, distinguish'd by their improv'd abilities, serviceable in public stations, and ornaments to their country.
paras.z: 过了一段时间，学校的董事们由总督颁发特许状，成了法人；靠着在英国募到的捐款和业主们拨赠的土地，他们的基金增加了，后来议会又作了相当可观的补充；这样就建立了现在的费城大学。我从一开始就一直是它的董事之一，至今将近四十年了；我十分高兴地看到，许多在那里受过教育的青年以他们增进了的才能而出众，在公职上有所贡献，为他们的国家增了光。

paras.e: When I disengaged myself, as above mentioned, from private business, I flatter'd myself that, by the sufficient tho' moderate fortune I had acquir'd, I had secured leisure during the rest of my life for philosophical studies and amusements. I purchased all Dr. Spence's apparatus, who had come from England to lecture here, and I proceeded in my electrical experiments with great alacrity; but the publick, now considering me as a man of leisure, laid hold of me for their purposes, every part of our civil government, and almost at the same time, imposing some duty upon me. The governor put me into the commission of the peace; the corporation of the city chose me of the common council, and soon after an alderman; and the citizens at large chose me a burgess to represent them in Assembly. This latter station was the more agreeable to me, as I was at length tired with sitting there to hear debates, in which, as clerk, I could take no part, and which were often so unentertaining that I was induc'd to amuse myself with making magic squares or circles, or any thing to avoid weariness; and I conceiv'd my becoming a member would enlarge my power of doing good. I would not, however, insinuate that my ambition was not flatter'd by all these promotions; it certainly was; for, considering my low beginning, they were great things to me; and they were still more pleasing, as being so many spontaneous testimonies of the public good opinion, and by me entirely unsolicited.
paras.z: 我像上面说的那样从私人生意中脱身的时候，自以为凭着已经挣得的那份虽不算多却也够用的家产，余生可以有闲暇从事哲学研究和消遣了。斯彭斯博士从英国到这里来讲学，我买下了他的全套仪器，兴致勃勃地进行我的电学实验。可是公众这时把我看成一个有闲的人，就抓住我来为他们办事；我们民政的各个部门几乎同时都把某种职责加到我身上。总督把我列入治安法官的名单；市政当局选我做市议会议员，不久又选我做市参议员；全体市民选我做议员，在州议会里代表他们。最后这个职位更合我的心意，因为我坐在那里听辩论已经听腻了——作为书记，我不能参加辩论，而这些辩论又常常那么乏味，我只好编些幻方、幻圆之类的东西来解闷——而且我想，当了议员会扩大我行善的力量。不过我并不想暗示，这一连串的升迁没有满足我的抱负；肯定是满足了的；因为，想到我低微的出身，这些对我都是了不起的事；而且它们更使我高兴，是因为这都是公众对我的好评的自发的表示，完全不是我自己求来的。

paras.e: The office of justice of the peace I try'd a little, by attending a few courts, and sitting on the bench to hear causes; but finding that more knowledge of the common law than I possess'd was necessary to act in that station with credit, I gradually withdrew from it, excusing myself by my being oblig'd to attend the higher duties of a legislator in the Assembly. My election to this trust was repeated every year for ten years, without my ever asking any elector for his vote, or signifying, either directly or indirectly, any desire of being chosen. On taking my seat in the House, my son was appointed their clerk.
paras.z: 治安法官这个职位我稍稍试了一下，出过几次庭，坐在法官席上听审案件；但我发现，要体面地担任这个职位，需要的普通法知识比我所有的要多，就渐渐退了出来，借口说我必须去履行议会里立法者的更高的职责。我连续十年每年都被选担任这一重任，从没有请任何一个选民投我的票，也没有直接或间接地表示过任何想当选的愿望。我在议院里就座的时候，我的儿子被任命为他们的书记。

paras.e: The year following, a treaty being to be held with the Indians at Carlisle, the governor sent a message to the House, proposing that they should nominate some of their members, to be join'd with some members of council, as commissioners for that purpose. [11] The House named the speaker (Mr. Norris) and myself; and, being commission'd, we went to Carlisle, and met the Indians accordingly.
paras.z: 第二年，要在卡莱尔同印第安人订立一项条约，总督向议院送了一份咨文，提议由议院提名几位议员，同参事会的几位成员一起担任办理这件事的专员。[11]议院提名了议长（诺里斯先生）和我；我们受了委任，就去了卡莱尔，如约会见了印第安人。

paras.e: [11] See the votes to have this more correctly.--[Marg. note.]
paras.z: [11] 参看表决记录，以求更准确。——［页边注］

paras.e: As those people are extreamly apt to get drunk, and, when so, are very quarrelsome and disorderly, we strictly forbad the selling any liquor to them; and when they complain'd of this restriction, we told them that if they would continue sober during the treaty, we would give them plenty of rum when business was over. They promis'd this, and they kept their promise, because they could get no liquor, and the treaty was conducted very orderly, and concluded to mutual satisfaction. They then claim'd and receiv'd the rum; this was in the afternoon; they were near one hundred men, women, and children, and were lodg'd in temporary cabins, built in the form of a square, just without the town. In the evening, hearing a great noise among them, the commissioners walk'd out to see what was the matter. We found they had made a great bonfire in the middle of the square; they were all drunk, men and women, quarreling and fighting. Their dark-colour'd bodies, half naked, seen only by the gloomy light of the bonfire, running after and beating one another with firebrands, accompanied by their horrid yellings, form'd a scene the most resembling our ideas of hell that could well be imagin'd; there was no appeasing the tumult, and we retired to our lodging. At midnight a number of them came thundering at our door, demanding more rum, of which we took no notice.
paras.z: 这些人极容易喝醉，一醉就非常好斗、不守秩序，所以我们严禁卖任何酒给他们；他们抱怨这项限制的时候，我们对他们说，如果他们在谈判期间保持清醒，事情办完以后我们会给他们大量的朗姆酒。他们答应了，也守了诺言，因为他们弄不到酒；谈判进行得很有秩序，结果双方都满意。然后他们来要朗姆酒，也拿到了；那是在下午。他们男女老少将近一百人，住在城外临时搭的小屋里，小屋围成一个方场。傍晚，我们听到他们那里一片喧闹，专员们就走出去看看出了什么事。我们发现他们在方场中央点了一堆大篝火；他们男男女女全都喝醉了，在争吵打架。他们深色的、半裸的身体，只在篝火昏暗的光里才看得见，互相追逐，用燃烧的木柴打来打去，伴着可怕的嚎叫，这幅景象同我们想象中的地狱再相像不过了。这场骚乱无法平息，我们就回到了住处。半夜里，他们有好几个人来把我们的门擂得山响，要更多的朗姆酒，我们没有理睬。

paras.e: The next day, sensible they had misbehav'd in giving us that disturbance, they sent three of their old counselors to make their apology. The orator acknowledg'd the fault, but laid it upon the rum; and then endeavored to excuse the rum by saying, "The Great Spirit, who made all things, made every thing for some use, and whatever use he design'd any thing for, that use it should always be put to. Now, when he made rum, he said 'Let this be for the Indians to get drunk with,' and it must be so." And, indeed, if it be the design of Providence to extirpate these savages in order to make room for cultivators of the earth, it seems not improbable that rum may be the appointed means. It has already annihilated all the tribes who formerly inhabited the sea-coast.
paras.z: 第二天，他们意识到那样打扰我们是失礼的，就派了三位年老的顾问来道歉。发言的人承认了过错，但把它归咎于朗姆酒；然后又设法替朗姆酒开脱，说：“创造万物的伟大神灵，创造每样东西都有某种用处；他打算让一样东西派什么用处，那样东西就应当永远派那个用处。他造朗姆酒的时候说：‘让这东西给印第安人喝醉用。’所以一定得这样。”说实在的，如果上天的旨意是要灭绝这些野蛮人，好给耕种土地的人腾出地方，那么朗姆酒也许就是指定的手段，这并非不可能。它已经消灭了所有从前居住在海岸一带的部落。

paras.e: In 1751, Dr. Thomas Bond, a particular friend of mine, conceived the idea of establishing a hospital in Philadelphia (a very beneficent design, which has been ascrib'd to me, but was originally his), for the reception and cure of poor sick persons, whether inhabitants of the province or strangers. He was zealous and active in endeavouring to procure subscriptions for it, but the proposal being a novelty in America, and at first not well understood, he met but with small success.
paras.z: 1751 年，我的一位特别要好的朋友托马斯·邦德医生想到要在费城创办一所医院（这是一个十分仁慈的计划，人们把它归功于我，其实最初是他的主意），用来收容和医治贫苦的病人，不论是本殖民地的居民还是外来的人。他热心而积极地设法为它募捐，但是这个建议在美洲是件新鲜事，起初人们不大理解，所以他成效甚微。

paras.e: At length he came to me with the compliment that he found there was no such thing as carrying a public-spirited project through without my being concern'd in it. "For," says he, "I am often ask'd by those to whom I propose subscribing, Have you consulted Franklin upon this business? And what does he think of it? And when I tell them that I have not (supposing it rather out of your line), they do not subscribe, but say they will consider of it." I enquired into the nature and probable utility of his scheme, and receiving from him a very satisfactory explanation, I not only subscrib'd to it myself, but engag'd heartily in the design of procuring subscriptions from others. Previously, however, to the solicitation, I endeavoured to prepare the minds of the people by writing on the subject in the newspapers, which was my usual custom in such cases, but which he had omitted.
paras.z: 最后他来找我，恭维我说，他发现不管什么热心公益的计划，要是没有我参与，就办不成。他说：“因为我向人提议认捐的时候，人家常常问我：这件事你同富兰克林商量过没有？他怎么看？我告诉他们没有（我原以为这不大是你的本行），他们就不认捐，只说要考虑考虑。”我询问了他这个计划的性质和可能有的用处，他作了非常令人满意的解释，我不但自己认了捐，而且全心全意地投入了向别人募捐的工作。不过，在募捐之前，我先在报纸上就这个题目写文章，设法让人们思想上有所准备，这是我在这类事情上一贯的做法，而他却忽略了。

paras.e: The subscriptions afterwards were more free and generous; but, beginning to flag, I saw they would be insufficient without some assistance from the Assembly, and therefore propos'd to petition for it, which was done. The country members did not at first relish the project; they objected that it could only be serviceable to the city, and therefore the citizens alone should be at the expense of it; and they doubted whether the citizens themselves generally approv'd of it. My allegation on the contrary, that it met with such approbation as to leave no doubt of our being able to raise two thousand pounds by voluntary donations, they considered as a most extravagant supposition, and utterly impossible.
paras.z: 此后捐款来得比较踊跃、比较慷慨了；但是势头开始减弱，我看出没有议会的一些资助是不够的，就提议向议会请愿求助，这件事办了。乡村的议员起初不喜欢这个计划；他们反对说，它只能对城市有用，所以应当只由市民负担费用；他们还怀疑市民自己是否普遍赞成。我提出相反的说法，说它得到的赞同足以使我们毫无疑问能靠自愿捐款筹到两千镑；他们认为这是极其夸大的设想，完全不可能。

paras.e: On this I form'd my plan; and asking leave to bring in a bill for incorporating the contributors according to the prayer of their petition, and granting them a blank sum of money, which leave was obtained chiefly on the consideration that the House could throw the bill out if they did not like it, I drew it so as to make the important clause a conditional one, viz., "And be it enacted, by the authority aforesaid, that when the said contributors shall have met and chosen their managers and treasurer, and shall have raised by their contributions a capital stock of ------ value (the yearly interest of which is to be applied to the accommodating of the sick poor in the said hospital, free of charge for diet, attendance, advice, and medicines), and shall make the same appear to the satisfaction of the speaker of the Assembly for the time being, that then it shall and may be lawful for the said speaker, and he is hereby required, to sign an order on the provincial treasurer for the payment of two thousand pounds, in two yearly payments, to the treasurer of the said hospital, to be applied to the founding, building, and finishing of the same."
paras.z: 我就根据这一点拟定了我的方案。我请求准许提出一项法案，照捐款人请愿书的请求让他们组成法人，并拨给他们一笔数目待填的款项；这项请求得到了准许，主要是考虑到议院如果不喜欢这个法案可以把它否决。我起草的时候，把那个重要的条款写成了有条件的，就是：“兹由上述权力机关规定：上述捐款人集会选出理事和司库，并以其捐款筹得价值若干之基金（其每年利息须用于在该医院内收容贫病之人，免收饮食、护理、诊治及药品之费），且使时任议会议长确信其属实之后，该议长即可依法、并在此被责成，签署一纸命令，由殖民地司库分两年拨付两千镑予该医院之司库，用于该医院之创办、建筑及落成。”

paras.e: This condition carried the bill through; for the members, who had oppos'd the grant, and now conceiv'd they might have the credit of being charitable without the expence, agreed to its passage; and then, in soliciting subscriptions among the people, we urg'd the conditional promise of the law as an additional motive to give, since every man's donation would be doubled; thus the clause work'd both ways. The subscriptions accordingly soon exceeded the requisite sum, and we claim'd and receiv'd the public gift, which enabled us to carry the design into execution. A convenient and handsome building was soon erected; the institution has by constant experience been found useful, and flourishes to this day; and I do not remember any of my political manœuvres, the success of which gave me at the time more pleasure, or wherein, after thinking of it, I more easily excus'd myself for having made some use of cunning.
paras.z: 这个条件使法案得以通过；因为那些原先反对拨款的议员，这时以为可以不花钱而落个乐善好施的名声，就同意让它通过了。然后，我们在民众中间募捐的时候，又强调法律上这项有条件的承诺，作为多一条捐款的理由，因为每个人的捐款都会翻一倍；这样，那个条款两头都起了作用。于是捐款不久就超过了规定的数目，我们提出申请，领到了公家的拨款，这使我们能够把计划付诸实行。一座方便而美观的建筑不久就落成了；经验不断证明这个机构是有用的，它至今兴旺；我记得，在我所有的政治手腕中，没有哪一次的成功在当时给我更多的快乐，也没有哪一次在我事后想来，更容易原谅自己用了一点狡计。

paras.e: It was about this time that another projector, the Rev. Gilbert Tennent, came to me with a request that I would assist him in procuring a subscription for erecting a new meeting-house. It was to be for the use of a congregation he had gathered among the Presbyterians, who were originally disciples of Mr. Whitefield. Unwilling to make myself disagreeable to my fellow-citizens by too frequently soliciting their contributions, I absolutely refus'd. He then desired I would furnish him with a list of the names of persons I knew by experience to be generous and public-spirited. I thought it would be unbecoming in me, after their kind compliance with my solicitations, to mark them out to be worried by other beggars, and therefore refus'd also to give such a list. He then desir'd I would at least give him my advice. "That I will readily do," said I; "and, in the first place, I advise you to apply to all those whom you know will give something; next, to those whom you are uncertain whether they will give any thing or not, and show them the list of those who have given; and, lastly, do not neglect those who you are sure will give nothing, for in some of them you may be mistaken." He laugh'd and thank'd me, and said he would take my advice. He did so, for he ask'd of everybody, and he obtained a much larger sum than he expected, with which he erected the capacious and very elegant meeting-house that stands in Arch-street.
paras.z: 大约在这个时候，另一位爱筹划的人吉尔伯特·坦南特牧师来找我，请我帮他募捐建一座新的聚会所。那是给他在长老会教徒中间聚集起来的一批会众用的，他们原是怀特菲尔德先生的门徒。我不愿意因为过于频繁地向同胞们募捐而招人讨厌，就一口回绝了。于是他要我给他开一张名单，列出我凭经验知道是慷慨而热心公益的人。我想，人家好意答应了我的请求，我反倒把他们指给别的募捐人去纠缠，这是不像话的，所以也拒绝开这样的名单。他又要我至少给他出个主意。我说：“这我很乐意。第一，我劝你去找所有你知道会捐一点的人；其次，去找那些你拿不准会不会捐的人，把已经捐了的人的名单给他们看；最后，也别漏掉那些你确信一文不捐的人，因为其中有些人你也许看错了。”他笑了，谢了我，说要照我的主意办。他果然照办了，因为他向每个人都开了口，结果募到的钱比他预期的多得多，他用这笔钱盖起了那座宽敞而十分雅致的聚会所，现在还立在拱门街上。

paras.e: Our city, tho' laid out with a beautiful regularity, the streets large, strait, and crossing each other at right angles, had the disgrace of suffering those streets to remain long unpav'd, and in wet weather the wheels of heavy carriages plough'd them into a quagmire, so that it was difficult to cross them; and in dry weather the dust was offensive. I had liv'd near what was call'd the Jersey Market, and saw with pain the inhabitants wading in mud while purchasing their provisions. A strip of ground down the middle of that market was at length pav'd with brick, so that, being once in the market, they had firm footing, but were often over shoes in dirt to get there. By talking and writing on the subject, I was at length instrumental in getting the street pav'd with stone between the market and the brick'd foot-pavement, that was on each side next the houses. This, for some time, gave an easy access to the market dry-shod; but, the rest of the street not being pav'd, whenever a carriage came out of the mud upon this pavement, it shook off and left its dirt upon it, and it was soon cover'd with mire, which was not remov'd, the city as yet having no scavengers.
paras.z: 我们这座城市虽然布局美观整齐，街道宽阔笔直，彼此直角相交，却有一件丢脸的事：这些街道长期没有铺砌，雨天里重车的轮子把它们犁成一片泥沼，很难穿过；天干的时候，尘土又叫人受不了。我曾住在所谓“泽西市场”附近，看着居民们买食品时在泥里跋涉，心里很难受。后来市场中间的一长条地面终于用砖铺上了，这样他们一进市场就有了结实的落脚处，可是走到那里，泥常常没过鞋面。我又是说又是写地谈这个问题，终于促成了把市场同两旁靠房子的砖砌人行道之间的那段街用石头铺了起来。有一段时间，这使人可以不湿鞋轻松地走到市场；可是街的其余部分没有铺，每逢有车子从泥里驶上这段路面，就把泥抖落留在上面，不久路面就盖满了烂泥，而且没有人清除，因为那时城里还没有清道夫。

paras.e: After some inquiry I found a poor industrious man, who was willing to undertake keeping the pavement clean, by sweeping it twice a week, carrying off the dirt from before all the neighbours' doors, for the sum of sixpence per month, to be paid by each house. I then wrote and printed a paper setting forth the advantages to the neighbourhood that might be obtain'd by this small expense; the greater ease in keeping our houses clean, so much dirt not being brought in by people's feet; the benefit to the shops by more custom, etc., etc., as buyers could more easily get at them; and by not having, in windy weather, the dust blown in upon their goods, etc., etc. I sent one of these papers to each house, and in a day or two went round to see who would subscribe an agreement to pay these sixpences; it was unanimously sign'd, and for a time well executed. All the inhabitants of the city were delighted with the cleanliness of the pavement that surrounded the market, it being a convenience to all, and this rais'd a general desire to have all the streets paved, and made the people more willing to submit to a tax for that purpose.
paras.z: 我打听了一番，找到一个勤快的穷人，他愿意承担保持路面清洁的工作，每星期扫两次，把所有邻居门前的脏土运走，每户每月付六便士。然后我写了一篇文章印出来，陈述花这一点小钱可以给街坊带来的种种好处：人们脚上不会带进那么多泥土，我们的屋子更容易保持干净；买主更容易走到铺子跟前，铺子的顾客会更多；刮风的时候，尘土不会吹到他们的货物上，等等，等等。我给每户送了一份，过了一两天挨家去看谁愿意签一份协议来付这六便士；大家一致签了，有一段时间执行得很好。全城的居民看到市场四周的路面那样干净，都很高兴，因为这对大家都方便；这就引起了普遍的愿望，要把所有的街道都铺起来，也使人们更愿意为此负担一项捐税。

paras.e: After some time I drew a bill for paving the city, and brought it into the Assembly. It was just before I went to England, in 1757, and did not pass till I was gone, [12] and then with an alteration in the mode of assessment, which I thought not for the better, but with an additional provision for lighting as well as paving the streets, which was a great improvement. It was by a private person, the late Mr. John Clifton, his giving a sample of the utility of lamps, by placing one at his door, that the people were first impress'd with the idea of enlighting all the city. The honour of this public benefit has also been ascrib'd to me, but it belongs truly to that gentleman. I did but follow his example, and have only some merit to claim respecting the form of our lamps, as differing from the globe lamps we were at first supply'd with from London. Those we found inconvenient in these respects: they admitted no air below; the smoke, therefore, did not readily go out above, but circulated in the globe, lodg'd on its inside, and soon obstructed the light they were intended to afford; giving, besides, the daily trouble of wiping them clean; and an accidental stroke on one of them would demolish it, and render it totally useless. I therefore suggested the composing them of four flat panes, with a long funnel above to draw up the smoke, and crevices admitting air below, to facilitate the ascent of the smoke; by this means they were kept clean, and did not grow dark in a few hours, as the London lamps do, but continu'd bright till morning, and an accidental stroke would generally break but a single pane, easily repair'd.
paras.z: 过了一段时间，我起草了一项铺砌全城街道的法案，提交给议会。那正是我 1757 年去英国之前，法案到我走后才通过[12]，而且在摊派捐税的方式上作了改动，我认为并没有改得更好；但是增加了一项规定，除了铺路还要给街道照明，这是一大改进。最初使人们想到要给全城照明的，是一位平民，已故的约翰·克利夫顿先生，他在自己门口装了一盏灯，以此示范了路灯的用处。这项公益的荣誉也被人归到我头上，其实它真正属于那位先生。我不过是学了他的样，只在我们路灯的式样上有一点功劳可言，这种式样不同于最初从伦敦运来给我们用的球形灯。我们发现那种灯有这些不便：下面不进空气，所以烟不容易从上面出去，而是在球里打转，积在球的内壁上，不久就挡住了它们本该发出的光；此外每天都要费事把它们擦干净；而且偶然碰一下就会把它打碎，完全不能用了。所以我建议用四块平板玻璃拼成，上面装一个长烟筒把烟抽上去，下面留缝隙进空气，好帮助烟上升。这样灯就保持干净，不像伦敦的灯那样几个小时就变暗，而是一直亮到早晨；偶然碰一下，通常也只打碎一块玻璃，很容易修理。

paras.e: [12] See votes.
paras.z: [12] 参看表决记录。

paras.e: I have sometimes wonder'd that the Londoners did not, from the effect holes in the bottom of the globe lamps us'd at Vauxhall have in keeping them clean, learn to have such holes in their street lamps. But, these holes being made for another purpose, viz., to communicate flame more suddenly to the wick by a little flax hanging down thro' them, the other use, of letting in air, seems not to have been thought of; and therefore, after the lamps have been lit a few hours, the streets of London are very poorly illuminated.
paras.z: 我有时感到奇怪，沃克斯豪尔游乐园用的球形灯底部有孔，这些孔对保持灯的清洁有那样的效果，伦敦人怎么没有从中学到在路灯上也开这样的孔。不过那些孔是为另一个目的开的，就是让一小束亚麻从孔里垂下来，好更快地把火引到灯芯上；至于让空气进来的另一个用处，似乎没有人想到过。所以，灯点了几个钟头以后，伦敦的街道就照得很暗了。

paras.e: The mention of these improvements puts me in mind of one I propos'd, when in London, to Dr. Fothergill, who was among the best men I have known, and a great promoter of useful projects. I had observ'd that the streets, when dry, were never swept, and the light dust carried away; but it was suffer'd to accumulate till wet weather reduc'd it to mud, and then, after lying some days so deep on the pavement that there was no crossing but in paths kept clean by poor people with brooms, it was with great labour rak'd together and thrown up into carts open above, the sides of which suffer'd some of the slush at every jolt on the pavement to shake out and fall, sometimes to the annoyance of foot-passengers. The reason given for not sweeping the dusty streets was, that the dust would fly into the windows of shops and houses.
paras.z: 提到这些改进，我想起我在伦敦时向福瑟吉尔医生提过的一项建议。他是我认识的最好的人之一，也是有益事业的热心推动者。我注意到，街道干燥的时候从来没有人扫，把浮土运走；而是听任尘土积聚，直到雨天把它变成泥浆。泥浆在路面上积得很深，一连好几天，除了穷人用扫帚扫出来的小路，无处可以过街；然后才费很大的力气把它耙到一起，铲进敞口的大车里，车子在路面上每颠一下，就有一些泥浆从车帮里晃出来掉下去，有时溅到行人身上。不扫干燥街道的理由，据说是尘土会飞进铺子和住宅的窗户。

paras.e: An accidental occurrence had instructed me how much sweeping might be done in a little time. I found at my door in Craven-street, one morning, a poor woman sweeping my pavement with a birch broom; she appeared very pale and feeble, as just come out of a fit of sickness. I ask'd who employ'd her to sweep there; she said, "Nobody, but I am very poor and in distress, and I sweeps before gentlefolkses doors, and hopes they will give me something." I bid her sweep the whole street clean, and I would give her a shilling; this was at nine o'clock; at 12 she came for the shilling. From the slowness I saw at first in her working, I could scarce believe that the work was done so soon, and sent my servant to examine it, who reported that the whole street was swept perfectly clean, and all the dust plac'd in the gutter, which was in the middle; and the next rain wash'd it quite away, so that the pavement and even the kennel were perfectly clean.
paras.z: 一件偶然的事使我知道了在很短的时间里可以扫多少地方。有一天早晨，我在克雷文街的寓所门口看到一个穷苦的妇人用桦树枝扫帚在扫我门前的路面；她脸色苍白，身体虚弱，像是刚生过一场病。我问是谁雇她在那里扫地的；她说：“没有谁，可是我很穷，日子难过，我在上等人家的门口扫地，指望他们给我一点什么。”我叫她把整条街扫干净，我给她一个先令。那是九点钟；十二点她就来领那个先令了。我起初看她干活那样慢，简直不能相信活这么快就干完了，就派仆人去察看；他回来报告说，整条街扫得干干净净，尘土都堆到了街中央的排水沟里。下一场雨把它冲得一干二净，路面甚至水沟都十分清洁了。

paras.e: I then judg'd that, if that feeble woman could sweep such a street in three hours, a strong, active man might have done it in half the time. And here let me remark the convenience of having but one gutter in such a narrow street, running down its middle, instead of two, one on each side, near the footway; for where all the rain that falls on a street runs from the sides and meets in the middle, it forms there a current strong enough to wash away all the mud it meets with; but when divided into two channels, it is often too weak to cleanse either, and only makes the mud it finds more fluid, so that the wheels of carriages and feet of horses throw and dash it upon the foot-pavement, which is thereby rendered foul and slippery, and sometimes splash it upon those who are walking. My proposal, communicated to the good doctor, was as follows:
paras.z: 于是我判断，如果那个虚弱的妇人三个小时能扫完这样一条街，一个强壮利落的男人用一半的时间就够了。这里让我顺便说说，这样窄的街道只在中间有一条排水沟，而不是两边靠人行道各有一条，有什么便利。落在街上的雨水全都从两边流向中间汇合，在那里形成的水流强得足以冲走它遇到的全部泥浆；可是分成两条沟，水流往往太弱，哪一条也冲不干净，只是把泥浆搅得更稀，车轮和马蹄就把它甩到、溅到人行道上，弄得又脏又滑，有时还溅到行人身上。我告诉那位好医生的建议如下：

paras.e: "For the more effectual cleaning and keeping clean the streets of London and Westminster, it is proposed that the several watchmen be contracted with to have the dust swept up in dry seasons, and the mud rak'd up at other times, each in the several streets and lanes of his round; that they be furnish'd with brooms and other proper instruments for these purposes, to be kept at their respective stands, ready to furnish the poor people they may employ in the service.
paras.z: “为了更有效地清扫伦敦和威斯敏斯特的街道并保持清洁，建议同各个巡夜人订约，由他们各自负责在自己巡逻的街巷里，旱季扫除尘土，其他时候耙起泥浆；给他们配备扫帚和其他适用的工具，放在各自的岗亭里，随时可以发给他们雇来干这件事的穷人。

paras.e: "That in the dry summer months the dust be all swept up into heaps at proper distances, before the shops and windows of houses are usually opened, when the scavengers, with close-covered carts, shall also carry it all away.
paras.z: “在干燥的夏季月份，要在铺子和住宅的窗户照例打开之前，把尘土全部扫成堆，每隔适当的距离一堆，这时清道夫也要用盖得严实的大车把它全部运走。

paras.e: "That the mud, when rak'd up, be not left in heaps to be spread abroad again by the wheels of carriages and trampling of horses, but that the scavengers be provided with bodies of carts, not plac'd high upon wheels, but low upon sliders, with lattice bottoms, which, being cover'd with straw, will retain the mud thrown into them, and permit the water to drain from it, whereby it will become much lighter, water making the greatest part of its weight; these bodies of carts to be plac'd at convenient distances, and the mud brought to them in wheel-barrows; they remaining where plac'd till the mud is drain'd, and then horses brought to draw them away."
paras.z: “耙起来的泥浆不要成堆留在那里，让车轮和马蹄再把它散开；而要给清道夫配备一种车厢，不是高高地装在轮子上，而是低低地装在滑橇上，车底是格栅，铺上稻草，可以留住倒进去的泥浆，让水从中沥出，这样泥浆就会轻得多，因为水占了它重量的最大部分。这些车厢每隔适当的距离放一个，泥浆用手推车运到那里；车厢留在原地，等泥浆沥干了，再牵马来把它们拉走。”

paras.e: I have since had doubts of the practicability of the latter part of this proposal, on account of the narrowness of some streets, and the difficulty of placing the draining-sleds so as not to encumber too much the passage; but I am still of opinion that the former, requiring the dust to be swept up and carry'd away before the shops are open, is very practicable in the summer, when the days are long; for, in walking thro' the Strand and Fleet-street one morning at seven o'clock, I observ'd there was not one shop open, tho' it had been daylight and the sun up above three hours; the inhabitants of London chusing voluntarily to live much by candle-light, and sleep by sunshine, and yet often complain, a little absurdly, of the duty on candles and the high price of tallow.
paras.z: 后来我对这项建议的后一部分是否可行有了怀疑，因为有些街道很窄，沥水的橇车很难放得不太妨碍通行；但我仍然认为，前一部分——要求在铺子开门之前把尘土扫起运走——在夏天白昼长的时候是很可行的。因为有一天早晨七点钟我走过河滨街和舰队街，注意到没有一家铺子开门，虽然天已经亮了三个多小时，太阳也出来了三个多小时；伦敦的居民自愿多在烛光下生活，在阳光下睡觉，却又常常抱怨蜡烛税和牛脂价高，这多少有点荒唐。

paras.e: Some may think these trifling matters not worth minding or relating; but when they consider that tho' dust blown into the eyes of a single person, or into a single shop on a windy day, is but of small importance, yet the great number of the instances in a populous city, and its frequent repetitions give it weight and consequence, perhaps they will not censure very severely those who bestow some attention to affairs of this seemingly low nature. Human felicity is produc'd not so much by great pieces of good fortune that seldom happen, as by little advantages that occur every day. Thus, if you teach a poor young man to shave himself, and keep his razor in order, you may contribute more to the happiness of his life than in giving him a thousand guineas. The money may be soon spent, the regret only remaining of having foolishly consumed it; but in the other case, he escapes the frequent vexation of waiting for barbers, and of their sometimes dirty fingers, offensive breaths, and dull razors; he shaves when most convenient to him, and enjoys daily the pleasure of its being done with a good instrument. With these sentiments I have hazarded the few preceding pages, hoping they may afford hints which some time or other may be useful to a city I love, having lived many years in it very happily, and perhaps to some of our towns in America.
paras.z: 有人也许认为这些琐碎的事不值得留意，也不值得讲述；但是请他们想一想：在刮风的日子里，尘土吹进一个人的眼睛或者一家铺子，固然无关紧要，可是在一个人口稠密的城市里，这样的事例数目很大，又常常重复，就有了分量和重要性；那么，他们也许就不会十分严厉地责备那些对这类看似低微的事务稍加留意的人了。人的幸福，与其说来自难得一遇的大好运，不如说来自每天都有的小便利。比方说，你教会一个贫穷的年轻人自己刮脸，把剃刀保养好，你对他一生幸福的贡献，也许比给他一千个几尼还大。钱可能很快就花光，只留下愚蠢地把它挥霍掉的懊悔；而在另一种情形下，他免去了常常等候理发匠的烦恼，免去了他们有时肮脏的手指、难闻的口气和钝了的剃刀；他在自己最方便的时候刮脸，每天都享受用一件好工具把这件事做好的快乐。抱着这样的想法，我冒昧写了前面这几页，希望它们提供的一些意见，有朝一日对我所爱的一座城市有用——我在那里十分愉快地住过许多年——或许对我们美洲的某些城镇也有用。

paras.e: Having been for some time employed by the postmaster-general of America as his comptroller in regulating several offices, and bringing the officers to account, I was, upon his death in 1753, appointed, jointly with Mr. William Hunter, to succeed him, by a commission from the postmaster-general in England. The American office never had hitherto paid any thing to that of Britain. We were to have six hundred pounds a year between us, if we could make that sum out of the profits of the office. To do this, a variety of improvements were necessary; some of these were inevitably at first expensive, so that in the first four years the office became above nine hundred pounds in debt to us. But it soon after began to repay us; and before I was displac'd by a freak of the ministers, of which I shall speak hereafter, we had brought it to yield three times as much clear revenue to the crown as the postoffice of Ireland. Since that imprudent transaction, they have receiv'd from it--not one farthing!
paras.z: 我曾有一段时间受美洲邮政总长的委派，担任他的稽核，整顿几处邮局，督促邮政人员结账。1753 年他去世后，英国的邮政总长颁发委任状，任命我同威廉·亨特先生共同接替他。在此之前，美洲邮政局从没有向英国邮政局上缴过一文钱。我们两人合得的年薪是六百镑，但要从邮局的盈利里挣得出这笔钱才行。为了做到这一点，需要进行各种改进；其中有些起初不可避免地要花钱，所以头四年邮局反而欠了我们九百多镑。可是此后不久它就开始偿还我们了；在我因为大臣们的一时任性而被免职之前（这件事我以后还要讲到），我们已经使它上缴给国王的纯收入达到爱尔兰邮政局的三倍。自从那次不明智的举动以后，他们从它那里得到的是——一个铜板也没有！

paras.e: The business of the postoffice occasion'd my taking a journey this year to New England, where the College of Cambridge, of their own motion, presented me with the degree of Master of Arts. Yale College, in Connecticut, had before made me a similar compliment. Thus, without studying in any college, I came to partake of their honours. They were conferr'd in consideration of my improvements and discoveries in the electric branch of natural philosophy.
paras.z: 为了邮政局的公务，我这一年去了一趟新英格兰，在那里，剑桥的学院（哈佛）主动授予我文学硕士学位。康涅狄格的耶鲁学院在此之前也曾给过我同样的荣誉。这样，我没有在任何学院读过书，却分享了它们的荣誉。这些学位是鉴于我在自然哲学的电学分支中的改进和发现而授予的。

paras.e: In 1754, war with France being again apprehended, a congress of commissioners from the different colonies was, by an order of the Lords of Trade, to be assembled at Albany, there to confer with the chiefs of the Six Nations concerning the means of defending both their country and ours. Governor Hamilton, having receiv'd this order, acquainted the House with it, requesting they would furnish proper presents for the Indians, to be given on this occasion; and naming the speaker (Mr. Norris) and myself to join Mr. Thomas Penn and Mr. Secretary Peters as commissioners to act for Pennsylvania. The House approv'd the nomination, and provided the goods for the present, and tho' they did not much like treating out of the provinces; and we met the other commissioners at Albany about the middle of June.
paras.z: 1754 年，同法国的战争眼看又要发生，根据贸易大臣们的命令，各殖民地的专员要在奥尔巴尼集会，同六族联盟的酋长们商讨保卫他们的地方和我们的地方的办法。汉密尔顿总督接到这道命令，通知了议院，请他们准备适当的礼物，在这个场合送给印第安人；并提名议长（诺里斯先生）和我，会同托马斯·佩恩先生和秘书彼得斯先生，作为代表宾夕法尼亚的专员。议院批准了这项提名，并置办了作礼物的货物，虽然他们不大喜欢到本殖民地以外去谈判；我们大约在六月中旬在奥尔巴尼同其他专员会合。

paras.e: In our way thither, I projected and drew a plan for the union of all the colonies under one government, so far as might be necessary for defense, and other important general purposes. As we pass'd thro' New York, I had there shown my project to Mr. James Alexander and Mr. Kennedy, two gentlemen of great knowledge in public affairs, and, being fortified by their approbation, I ventur'd to lay it before the Congress. It then appeared that several of the commissioners had form'd plans of the same kind. A previous question was first taken, whether a union should be established, which pass'd in the affirmative unanimously. A committee was then appointed, one member from each colony, to consider the several plans and report. Mine happen'd to be preferr'd, and, with a few amendments, was accordingly reported.
paras.z: 在去那里的路上，我构思并起草了一个方案，把所有殖民地联合在一个政府之下，范围以防务和其他重要的共同目的所必需者为限。我们路过纽约的时候，我把方案拿给詹姆斯·亚历山大先生和肯尼迪先生看过，这两位绅士对公共事务极有见识；得到他们的赞许，我更有了信心，就大胆地把它提交给了会议。这时才知道，有好几位专员都拟了同类的方案。会议先就一个先决问题进行表决：是否应当建立一个联盟，结果一致通过。然后指定了一个委员会，每个殖民地出一人，审议各个方案并提出报告。我的方案恰好被选中，稍加修改后，就作为报告提了出来。

paras.e: By this plan the general government was to be administered by a president-general, appointed and supported by the crown, and a grand council was to be chosen by the representatives of the people of the several colonies, met in their respective assemblies. The debates upon it in Congress went on daily, hand in hand with the Indian business. Many objections and difficulties were started, but at length they were all overcome, and the plan was unanimously agreed to, and copies ordered to be transmitted to the Board of Trade and to the assemblies of the several provinces. Its fate was singular: the assemblies did not adopt it, as they all thought there was too much prerogative in it, and in England it was judg'd to have too much of the democratic.
paras.z: 按照这个方案，总的政府由一位总统领（President-General）主持，由国王任命并由国王供给薪俸；另设一个大议会，由各殖民地的人民代表在各自的议会里选举产生。会议上每天就这个方案进行辩论，同印第安人事务齐头并进。有人提出了许多异议和困难，但最后都一一克服了，方案得到一致同意，并下令把抄本送交贸易委员会和各殖民地的议会。它的命运很奇特：各殖民地的议会没有采纳，因为它们都认为其中君主的特权太多；而在英国，人们却断定它的民主成分太多。

paras.e: The Board of Trade therefore did not approve of it, nor recommend it for the approbation of his majesty; but another scheme was form'd, supposed to answer the same purpose better, whereby the governors of the provinces, with some members of their respective councils, were to meet and order the raising of troops, building of forts, etc., and to draw on the treasury of Great Britain for the expense, which was afterwards to be refunded by an act of Parliament laying a tax on America. My plan, with my reasons in support of it, is to be found among my political papers that are printed.
paras.z: 所以贸易委员会没有批准它，也没有把它呈请国王陛下批准；而是另拟了一个方案，据认为能更好地达到同样的目的：由各殖民地的总督同各自参事会的若干成员集会，下令招募军队、修筑堡垒等等，费用向英国国库支取，日后由国会通过一项向美洲征税的法令来偿还。我的方案，连同我支持它的理由，可以在我已刊印的政治文件中找到。

paras.e: Being the winter following in Boston, I had much conversation with Governor Shirley upon both the plans. Part of what passed between us on the occasion may also be seen among those papers. The different and contrary reasons of dislike to my plan makes me suspect that it was really the true medium; and I am still of opinion it would have been happy for both sides the water if it had been adopted. The colonies, so united, would have been sufficiently strong to have defended themselves; there would then have been no need of troops from England; of course, the subsequent pretence for taxing America, and the bloody contest it occasioned, would have been avoided. But such mistakes are not new; history is full of the errors of states and princes.
paras.z: 那年冬天我在波士顿，同雪利总督就这两个方案谈了很多。我们当时交谈的一部分内容，也可以在那些文件里看到。人们出于不同的、相反的理由不喜欢我的方案，这使我猜想它其实正是真正的中道；我至今仍然认为，如果它被采纳了，对大洋两岸都是幸事。各殖民地这样联合起来，就足以自卫；那就不需要英国派兵来；后来向美洲征税的借口，以及由此引起的流血冲突，当然也就可以避免了。但是这样的错误并不新鲜；历史上充满了国家和君主的过失。

paras.e: Look round the habitable world, how few
paras.z: 环顾这有人居住的世界，有几人

paras.e: Know their own good, or, knowing it, pursue!
paras.z: 知道自己的利益，或者知道了，肯去追求！

paras.e: Those who govern, having much business on their hands, do not generally like to take the trouble of considering and carrying into execution new projects. The best public measures are therefore seldom adopted from previous wisdom, but forc'd by the occasion.
paras.z: 执政的人手头事务繁多，一般不愿意费神去考虑并实行新的计划。所以，最好的公共措施很少是出于事先的智慧而被采纳的，而是被时势逼出来的。

paras.e: The Governor of Pennsylvania, in sending it down to the Assembly, express'd his approbation of the plan, "as appearing to him to be drawn up with great clearness and strength of judgment, and therefore recommended it as well worthy of their closest and most serious attention." The House, however, by the management of a certain member, took it up when I happen'd to be absent, which I thought not very fair, and reprobated it without paying any attention to it at all, to my no small mortification.
paras.z: 宾夕法尼亚总督把这个方案送交议会的时候，表示了赞同，说“在他看来，它拟得十分清楚，判断有力，所以推荐给议会，认为很值得他们最仔细、最认真地加以注意”。可是议院在某一位议员的操纵下，趁我碰巧不在的时候把它提了出来——我认为这不大光明正大——根本没有加以注意就把它否决了，这使我很是懊丧。

paras.e: In my journey to Boston this year, I met at New York with our new governor, Mr. Morris, just arriv'd there from England, with whom I had been before intimately acquainted. He brought a commission to supersede Mr. Hamilton, who, tir'd with the disputes his proprietary instructions subjected him to, had resign'd. Mr. Morris ask'd me if I thought he must expect as uncomfortable an administration. I said, "No; you may, on the contrary, have a very comfortable one, if you will only take care not to enter into any dispute with the Assembly." "My dear friend," says he, pleasantly, "how can you advise my avoiding disputes? You know I love disputing; it is one of my greatest pleasures; however, to show the regard I have for your counsel, I promise you I will, if possible, avoid them." He had some reason for loving to dispute, being eloquent, an acute sophister, and, therefore, generally successful in argumentative conversation. He had been brought up to it from a boy, his father, as I have heard, accustoming his children to dispute with one another for his diversion, while sitting at table after dinner; but I think the practice was not wise; for, in the course of my observation, these disputing, contradicting, and confuting people are generally unfortunate in their affairs. They get victory sometimes, but they never get good will, which would be of more use to them. We parted, he going to Philadelphia, and I to Boston.
paras.z: 这一年我去波士顿的途中，在纽约遇见了我们的新总督莫里斯先生，他刚从英国到那里，我以前同他很熟。他带来了接替汉密尔顿先生的委任状；汉密尔顿先生因为业主的训令使他陷入无穷的争执，感到厌倦，已经辞职了。莫里斯先生问我，他是否也得预料任内会同样不舒服。我说：“不；相反，你可以过得很舒服，只要你留心不同议会发生任何争执。”他愉快地说：“我亲爱的朋友，你怎么能劝我避免争执呢？你知道我是爱争辩的；这是我最大的乐趣之一。不过，为了表示我尊重你的劝告，我答应你，只要可能，我就避免。”他爱争辩是有几分道理的，因为他口才好，是个机敏的诡辩家，所以在辩论式的谈话中通常都能取胜。他从小就受这种训练；我听说，他父亲饭后坐在桌旁，习惯让孩子们互相争辩，以此取乐。但我认为这种做法并不明智；因为据我的观察，这些爱争辩、爱反驳、爱驳倒别人的人，一般在自己的事务上都不走运。他们有时赢得胜利，却从来赢不到好感，而好感对他们会更有用。我们分了手，他去费城，我去波士顿。

paras.e: In returning, I met at New York with the votes of the Assembly, by which it appear'd that, notwithstanding his promise to me, he and the House were already in high contention; and it was a continual battle between them as long as he retain'd the government. I had my share of it; for, as soon as I got back to my seat in the Assembly, I was put on every committee for answering his speeches and messages, and by the committees always desired to make the drafts. Our answers, as well as his messages, were often tart, and sometimes indecently abusive; and, as he knew I wrote for the Assembly, one might have imagined that, when we met, we could hardly avoid cutting throats; but he was so good-natur'd a man that no personal difference between him and me was occasion'd by the contest, and we often din'd together.
paras.z: 回来的路上，我在纽约看到了议会的表决记录，从中可以看出，尽管他对我有过承诺，他同议院已经吵得不可开交；在他任总督期间，他们之间一直争战不休。我也有份；因为我一回到议会的席位上，就被编进了每一个答复他的演说和咨文的委员会，各委员会又总是要我起草。我们的答复同他的咨文一样，常常很尖刻，有时还谩骂得不成体统；他知道议会的文字是我写的，人家或许以为我们见了面免不了要拼个你死我活。可是他是个脾气那样好的人，这场争执并没有在他和我之间造成任何个人的隔阂，我们还常常一起吃饭。

paras.e: One afternoon, in the height of this public quarrel, we met in the street. "Franklin," says he, "you must go home with me and spend the evening; I am to have some company that you will like;" and, taking me by the arm, he led me to his house. In gay conversation over our wine, after supper, he told us, jokingly, that he much admir'd the idea of Sancho Panza, who, when it was proposed to give him a government, requested it might be a government of blacks, as then, if he could not agree with his people, he might sell them. One of his friends, who sat next to me, says, "Franklin, why do you continue to side with these damn'd Quakers? Had not you better sell them? The proprietor would give you a good price." "The governor," says I, "has not yet blacked them enough." He, indeed, had labored hard to blacken the Assembly in all his messages, but they wip'd off his coloring as fast as he laid it on, and plac'd it, in return, thick upon his own face; so that, finding he was likely to be negrofied himself, he, as well as Mr. Hamilton, grew tir'd of the contest, and quitted the government.
paras.z: 在这场公开的争吵闹得最凶的时候，有一天下午，我们在街上相遇。他说：“富兰克林，你得跟我回家，一起过这个晚上；我要请几位客人，你会喜欢的。”说着挽住我的胳膊，把我领到他家。晚饭后，我们一边喝酒一边谈笑，他开玩笑地告诉我们，他十分欣赏桑丘·潘沙的主意：有人提议让桑丘管一个地方，他要求管一个黑人的地方，这样，万一他同他的百姓合不来，就可以把他们卖掉。坐在我旁边的他的一位朋友说：“富兰克林，你为什么老是站在这些该死的贵格会教徒一边？把他们卖了不是更好吗？业主会给你一个好价钱的。”我说：“总督还没有把他们抹得够黑呢。”他确实在所有的咨文里竭力抹黑议会，可是他一边抹，他们一边擦，转过来把颜色厚厚地涂在他自己脸上；结果，他眼看自己倒要被抹成黑人了，就同汉密尔顿先生一样，对这场争斗感到厌倦，辞去了总督的职位。

paras.e: [13] These public quarrels were all at bottom owing to the proprietaries, our hereditary governors, who, when any expense was to be incurred for the defense of their province, with incredible meanness instructed their deputies to pass no act for levying the necessary taxes, unless their vast estates were in the same act expressly excused; and they had even taken bonds of these deputies to observe such instructions. The Assemblies for three years held out against this injustice, tho' constrained to bend at last. At length Captain Denny, who was Governor Morris's successor, ventured to disobey those instructions; how that was brought about I shall show hereafter.
paras.z: [13] 这些公开的争吵，归根到底都是业主们——我们世袭的统治者——造成的。每逢为了保卫他们的殖民地需要开支的时候，他们竟以令人难以置信的卑鄙，训令他们的代理人不得通过任何征收必要捐税的法案，除非在同一法案里明文豁免他们巨大的产业；他们甚至要这些代理人立下保证书，遵守这样的训令。历届议会抵制这种不公道达三年之久，最后还是被迫屈服。后来莫里斯总督的继任者丹尼上尉终于敢于违抗这些训令；这是怎样促成的，我以后再讲。

paras.e: [13] My acts in Morris's time, military, etc.--[Marg. note.]
paras.z: [13] 我在莫里斯任内的作为，军事等等。——［页边注］

paras.e: But I am got forward too fast with my story: there are still some transactions to be mention'd that happened during the administration of Governor Morris.
paras.z: 不过我的故事讲得太快了：莫里斯总督任内发生的事，还有几件要提一提。

paras.e: War being in a manner commenced with France, the government of Massachusetts Bay projected an attack upon Crown Point, and sent Mr. Quincy to Pennsylvania, and Mr. Pownall, afterward Governor Pownall, to New York, to solicit assistance. As I was in the Assembly, knew its temper, and was Mr. Quincy's countryman, he appli'd to me for my influence and assistance. I dictated his address to them, which was well receiv'd. They voted an aid of ten thousand pounds, to be laid out in provisions. But the governor refusing his assent to their bill (which included this with other sums granted for the use of the crown), unless a clause were inserted exempting the proprietary estate from bearing any part of the tax that would be necessary, the Assembly, tho' very desirous of making their grant to New England effectual, were at a loss how to accomplish it. Mr. Quincy labored hard with the governor to obtain his assent, but he was obstinate.
paras.z: 同法国的战争可以说已经开始了，马萨诸塞湾政府计划进攻克朗波因特，派昆西先生到宾夕法尼亚、波纳尔先生（后来的波纳尔总督）到纽约去请求援助。因为我在议会里，了解它的脾气，又是昆西先生的同乡，他就来找我，请我运用影响帮忙。我替他口授了致议会的呈文，议会反应很好。他们投票通过拨一万镑的援助，用来购买粮食。可是总督拒绝批准他们的法案（这个法案把这笔钱同另几笔拨给国王使用的款子列在一起），除非加进一个条款，豁免业主的产业负担任何一部分所需的捐税。议会虽然很想使他们给新英格兰的拨款落到实处，却不知道怎样才办得到。昆西先生费了很大的劲去争取总督的批准，可是他很固执。

paras.e: I then suggested a method of doing the business without the governor, by orders on the trustees of the Loan Office, which, by law, the Assembly had the right of drawing. There was, indeed, little or no money at that time in the office, and therefore I propos'd that the orders should be payable in a year, and to bear an interest of five per cent. With these orders I suppos'd the provisions might easily be purchas'd. The Assembly, with very little hesitation, adopted the proposal. The orders were immediately printed, and I was one of the committee directed to sign and dispose of them. The fund for paying them was the interest of all the paper currency then extant in the province upon loan, together with the revenue arising from the excise, which being known to be more than sufficient, they obtain'd instant credit, and were not only receiv'd in payment for the provisions, but many money'd people, who had cash lying by them, vested it in those orders, which they found advantageous, as they bore interest while upon hand, and might on any occasion be used as money; so that they were eagerly all bought up, and in a few weeks none of them were to be seen. Thus this important affair was by my means compleated. My Quincy return'd thanks to the Assembly in a handsome memorial, went home highly pleas'd with the success of his embassy, and ever after bore for me the most cordial and affectionate friendship.
paras.z: 于是我提出一个不必经过总督就能办成这件事的办法，就是向贷款局的受托人开出支付令，依照法律，议会有权开这种支付令。那时贷款局里确实没有多少钱，甚至一点没有，所以我提议这些支付令一年后兑付，并且付五厘的利息。我估计用这些支付令可以很容易地买到粮食。议会几乎没有犹豫就采纳了这个建议。支付令立刻印了出来，我是受命签署并发放它们的委员之一。偿付它们的基金，是当时本殖民地所有贷放在外的纸币的利息，加上消费税的收入，人人都知道这笔钱绰绰有余，所以这些支付令立刻就有了信用，不但被人接受作为购买粮食的货款，而且许多手头有闲置现金的有钱人也把钱投在这些支付令上，他们发现这很合算，因为它们留在手里就生利息，需要时又随时可以当钱用。于是它们全都被抢购一空，几个星期之内就一张也见不到了。这件重要的事就这样靠我的办法办成了。昆西先生用一篇措辞得体的呈文向议会致谢，带着对这次使命圆满成功的极大喜悦回了家，此后对我始终怀着最诚挚、最亲切的友谊。

paras.e: The British government, not chusing to permit the union of the colonies as propos'd at Albany, and to trust that union with their defense, lest they should thereby grow too military, and feel their own strength, suspicions and jealousies at this time being entertain'd of them, sent over General Braddock with two regiments of regular English troops for that purpose. He landed at Alexandria, in Virginia, and thence march'd to Frederictown, in Maryland, where he halted for carriages. Our Assembly apprehending, from some information, that he had conceived violent prejudices against them, as averse to the service, wish'd me to wait upon him, not as from them, but as postmaster-general, under the guise of proposing to settle with him the mode of conducting with most celerity and certainty the despatches between him and the governors of the several provinces, with whom he must necessarily have continual correspondence, and of which they propos'd to pay the expense. My son accompanied me on this journey.
paras.z: 英国政府不愿意准许各殖民地照奥尔巴尼会议的提议联合起来，也不愿意把它们的防务托付给这个联盟，唯恐它们因此变得过于有军事力量，感觉到自己的实力——当时对它们已经有了猜疑和戒心——于是为此派布雷多克将军率领两团英国正规军渡海而来。他在弗吉尼亚的亚历山德里亚登陆，由那里进军到马里兰的弗雷德里克镇，在那里停下来等候车辆。我们的议会从一些消息中得知，他对议会抱有强烈的成见，认为他们不愿为这次军事行动出力，就希望我去拜见他，不是以议会代表的名义，而是以邮政总长的身份，借口说要同他商定怎样最迅速、最可靠地传递他同各殖民地总督之间的公文——他必然要同他们不断通信——并且提出由议会负担这笔费用。我的儿子陪我走了这一趟。

paras.e: We found the general at Frederictown, waiting impatiently for the return of those he had sent thro' the back parts of Maryland and Virginia to collect waggons. I stayed with him several days, din'd with him daily, and had full opportunity of removing all his prejudices, by the information of what the Assembly had before his arrival actually done, and were still willing to do, to facilitate his operations. When I was about to depart, the returns of waggons to be obtained were brought in, by which it appear'd that they amounted only to twenty-five, and not all of those were in serviceable condition. The general and all the officers were surpris'd, declar'd the expedition was then at an end, being impossible, and exclaim'd against the ministers for ignorantly landing them in a country destitute of the means of conveying their stores, baggage, etc., not less than one hundred and fifty waggons being necessary.
paras.z: 我们在弗雷德里克镇见到了将军，他正不耐烦地等着他派到马里兰和弗吉尼亚边远地区去征集大车的人回来。我同他一起待了几天，每天同他一起吃饭，有充分的机会消除他的全部成见，告诉他在他到来之前议会实际上已经做了些什么，以及还愿意做些什么，来方便他的行动。我正要动身离开的时候，征集大车的结果报上来了，看来总共只有二十五辆，而且并不都能用。将军和全体军官大吃一惊，宣称这次远征到此为止，因为已经不可能了；他们大骂大臣们无知，把他们送到一个没有办法运送军需、行李等等的地方登陆，因为至少需要一百五十辆大车。

paras.e: I happened to say I thought it was a pity they had not been landed rather in Pennsylvania, as in that country almost every farmer had his waggon. The general eagerly laid hold of my words, and said, "Then you, sir, who are a man of interest there, can probably procure them for us; and I beg you will undertake it." I ask'd what terms were to be offer'd the owners of the waggons; and I was desir'd to put on paper the terms that appeared to me necessary. This I did, and they were agreed to, and a commission and instructions accordingly prepar'd immediately. What those terms were will appear in the advertisement I publish'd as soon as I arriv'd at Lancaster, which being, from the great and sudden effect it produc'd, a piece of some curiosity, I shall insert it at length, as follows:
paras.z: 我随口说了一句，我觉得可惜他们没有在宾夕法尼亚登陆，因为那个地方几乎每个农夫都有自己的大车。将军急切地抓住我的话，说：“那么，先生，你在那里是有影响的人，也许能替我们弄到大车；我恳求你承担这件事。”我问要给大车的主人开什么条件；他要我把我认为必要的条件写在纸上。我写了，他们同意了，立刻照此备好了委任状和训令。这些条件是什么，可以从我一到兰开斯特就发布的告示中看到。这份告示产生了巨大而迅速的效果，算得上一件稀罕的文字，所以我把它全文录在下面：

paras.e: "Advertisement.
paras.z: “告示

paras.e: "LANCASTER, April 26, 1755.
paras.z: “1755 年 4 月 26 日，兰开斯特。

paras.e: "Whereas, one hundred and fifty waggons, with four horses to each waggon, and fifteen hundred saddle or pack horses, are wanted for the service of his majesty's forces now about to rendezvous at Will's Creek, and his excellency General Braddock having been pleased to empower me to contract for the hire of the same, I hereby give notice that I shall attend for that purpose at Lancaster from this day to next Wednesday evening, and at York from next Thursday morning till Friday evening, where I shall be ready to agree for waggons and teams, or single horses, on the following terms, viz.: 1. That there shall be paid for each waggon, with four good horses and a driver, fifteen shillings per diem; and for each able horse with a pack-saddle, or other saddle and furniture, two shillings per diem; and for each able horse without a saddle, eighteen pence per diem. 2. That the pay commence from the time of their joining the forces at Will's Creek, which must be on or before the 20th of May ensuing, and that a reasonable allowance be paid over and above for the time necessary for their travelling to Will's Creek and home again after their discharge. 3. Each waggon and team, and every saddle or pack horse, is to be valued by indifferent persons chosen between me and the owner; and in case of the loss of any waggon, team, or other horse in the service, the price according to such valuation is to be allowed and paid. 4. Seven days' pay is to be advanced and paid in hand by me to the owner of each waggon and team, or horse, at the time of contracting, if required, and the remainder to be paid by General Braddock, or by the paymaster of the army, at the time of their discharge, or from time to time, as it shall be demanded. 5. No drivers of waggons, or persons taking care of the hired horses, are on any account to be called upon to do the duty of soldiers, or be otherwise employed than in conducting or taking care of their carriages or horses. 6. All oats, Indian corn, or other forage that waggons or horses bring to the camp, more than is necessary for the subsistence of the horses, is to be taken for the use of the army, and a reasonable price paid for the same.
paras.z: “兹因国王陛下的军队即将在威尔斯溪集结，需要大车一百五十辆，每车配马四匹，另需鞍马或驮马一千五百匹；布雷多克将军阁下已授权本人订约雇用上述车马。特此通告：自今日起至下星期三晚，本人将在兰开斯特，自下星期四晨至星期五晚在约克，为此办公，届时可按下列条件商订雇用大车连同马匹或单匹马的合约：一、每辆大车配良马四匹、车夫一名，每日付十五先令；每匹带驮鞍或其他鞍具的健马，每日付两先令；每匹不带鞍的健马，每日付十八便士。二、酬金自车马到威尔斯溪与军队会合之日起算，会合日期须在 5 月 20 日或之前；前往威尔斯溪及遣散后回家所需的路程时间，另付合理的津贴。三、每辆大车连同马匹，以及每匹鞍马或驮马，均由本人与车马主人共同选定的公正人估价；服役期间如有大车、马匹损失，按估价赔付。四、订约时如有要求，本人预付每辆大车连同马匹或每匹马的主人七天的酬金，余款由布雷多克将军或军需官在遣散时支付，或者按要求随时支付。五、大车的车夫或照管所雇马匹的人，无论如何不得被征召去尽士兵的职责，也不得被派做赶车或照料车马以外的事。六、大车或马匹带到营地的燕麦、玉米或其他草料，除马匹自用所需外，其余由军队收用，并付给合理的价钱。

paras.e: "Note.--My son, William Franklin, is empowered to enter into like contracts with any person in Cumberland county.
paras.z: “附告：本人之子威廉·富兰克林有权同坎伯兰县的任何人订立同样的合约。

paras.e: "B. Franklin."
paras.z: “本·富兰克林”

paras.e: "To the inhabitants of the Counties of Lancaster, York and Cumberland.
paras.z: “致兰开斯特、约克和坎伯兰各县居民。

paras.e: "Friends and Countrymen,
paras.z: “朋友们，同胞们：

paras.e: "Being occasionally at the camp at Frederic a few days since, I found the general and officers extremely exasperated on account of their not being supplied with horses and carriages, which had been expected from this province, as most able to furnish them; but, through the dissensions between our governor and Assembly, money had not been provided, nor any steps taken for that purpose.
paras.z: “几天前，我偶然到了弗雷德里克的营地，发现将军和军官们因为得不到马匹和车辆而极为恼怒；他们原指望本殖民地供给，因为本殖民地最有能力供给。可是由于我们的总督同议会不和，款项没有拨出，也没有为此采取任何措施。

paras.e: "It was proposed to send an armed force immediately into these counties, to seize as many of the best carriages and horses as should be wanted, and compel as many persons into the service as would be necessary to drive and take care of them.
paras.z: “有人提议立即派一支武装部队进入这几个县，要多少就强征多少最好的车辆和马匹，并且强迫足够的人去服役，赶车并照料车马。

paras.e: "I apprehended that the progress of British soldiers through these counties on such an occasion, especially considering the temper they are in, and their resentment against us, would be attended with many and great inconveniences to the inhabitants, and therefore more willingly took the trouble of trying first what might be done by fair and equitable means. The people of these back counties have lately complained to the Assembly that a sufficient currency was wanting; you have an opportunity of receiving and dividing among you a very considerable sum; for, if the service of this expedition should continue, as it is more than probable it will, for one hundred and twenty days, the hire of these waggons and horses will amount to upward of thirty thousand pounds, which will be paid you in silver and gold of the king's money.
paras.z: “我担心，英国士兵为了这样的事开进这几个县，尤其是考虑到他们眼下的情绪和他们对我们的怨恨，会给居民带来许多很大的不便，所以我更愿意不辞辛苦，先试一试用公平合理的办法能办到什么。这些边远各县的人民近来曾向议会诉苦，说缺少足够的通货；现在你们有机会得到一笔非常可观的款子，在你们中间分配。因为，如果这次远征的服役期持续一百二十天——这是很有可能的——这些大车和马匹的租金就会达到三万镑以上，这笔钱将用国王的金币银币付给你们。

paras.e: "The service will be light and easy, for the army will scarce march above twelve miles per day, and the waggons and baggage-horses, as they carry those things that are absolutely necessary to the welfare of the army, must march with the army, and no faster; and are, for the army's sake, always placed where they can be most secure, whether in a march or in a camp.
paras.z: “这项差事是轻松容易的，因为军队每天行军不大会超过十二英里；大车和驮行李的马匹运的是军队绝对少不了的东西，所以必须同军队一起走，不会更快；而且为了军队自身的缘故，不论行军还是宿营，总是把它们安排在最安全的地方。

paras.e: "If you are really, as I believe you are, good and loyal subjects to his majesty, you may now do a most acceptable service, and make it easy to yourselves; for three or four of such as can not separately spare from the business of their plantations a waggon and four horses and a driver, may do it together, one furnishing the waggon, another one or two horses, and another the driver, and divide the pay proportionately between you; but if you do not this service to your king and country voluntarily, when such good pay and reasonable terms are offered to you, your loyalty will be strongly suspected. The king's business must be done; so many brave troops, come so far for your defense, must not stand idle through your backwardness to do what may be reasonably expected from you; waggons and horses must be had; violent measures will probably be used, and you will be left to seek for a recompense where you can find it, and your case, perhaps, be little pitied or regarded.
paras.z: “如果你们真的像我所相信的那样，是国王陛下善良忠诚的臣民，那么现在你们可以效一次最受欢迎的劳，而且自己也不费事；因为，如果有三四户人家各自都无法从田庄的活计里抽出一辆大车、四匹马和一个车夫，他们可以合起来办，一家出车，一家出一两匹马，另一家出车夫，酬金按比例分配。可是，给你们开出了这样优厚的酬金和合理的条件，如果你们还不自愿为你们的国王和国家效这个劳，你们的忠诚就大可怀疑了。国王的事必须办成；这么多英勇的军队远道而来保卫你们，决不能因为你们不肯去做理应由你们做的事而闲置在那里；大车和马匹非有不可；很可能就要采取强暴的手段，那时你们只好自己去想办法索取补偿，而你们的情形也许不大会有人同情或理睬。

paras.e: "I have no particular interest in this affair, as, except the satisfaction of endeavoring to do good, I shall have only my labour for my pains. If this method of obtaining the waggons and horses is not likely to succeed, I am obliged to send word to the general in fourteen days; and I suppose Sir John St. Clair, the hussar, with a body of soldiers, will immediately enter the province for the purpose, which I shall be sorry to hear, because I am very sincerely and truly your friend and well-wisher,
paras.z: “我在这件事上没有什么个人的利益，因为除了努力行善而得到的满足，我只是白白辛苦一场。如果用这个办法弄不到大车和马匹，我必须在十四天之内通知将军；我估计，骠骑兵约翰·圣克莱尔爵士就会立刻带一队士兵开进本殖民地来办这件事。听到这样的消息我会很难过，因为我是你们十分真诚的朋友，衷心祝愿你们一切都好。

paras.e: B. Franklin."
paras.z: 本·富兰克林”

paras.e: I received of the general about eight hundred pounds, to be disbursed in advance-money to the waggon owners, etc.; but that sum being insufficient, I advanc'd upward of two hundred pounds more, and in two weeks the one hundred and fifty waggons, with two hundred and fifty-nine carrying horses, were on their march for the camp. The advertisement promised payment according to the valuation, in case any waggon or horse should be lost. The owners, however, alleging they did not know General Braddock, or what dependence might be had on his promise, insisted on my bond for the performance, which I accordingly gave them.
paras.z: 我从将军那里领到大约八百镑，用来预付给大车主人等等；但这个数目不够，我又垫了二百多镑。两个星期之内，一百五十辆大车和二百五十九匹驮马就上路开往营地了。告示上许诺，如果大车或马匹有损失，按估价赔付。可是车马的主人们说，他们不认识布雷多克将军，也不知道他的许诺靠得住靠不住，坚持要我出具保证书担保履约，我就给了他们。

paras.e: While I was at the camp, supping one evening with the officers of Colonel Dunbar's regiment, he represented to me his concern for the subalterns, who, he said, were generally not in affluence, and could ill afford, in this dear country, to lay in the stores that might be necessary in so long a march, thro' a wilderness, where nothing was to be purchas'd. I commiserated their case, and resolved to endeavor procuring them some relief. I said nothing, however, to him of my intention, but wrote the next morning to the committee of the Assembly, who had the disposition of some public money, warmly recommending the case of these officers to their consideration, and proposing that a present should be sent them of necessaries and refreshments. My son, who had some experience of a camp life, and of its wants, drew up a list for me, which I enclos'd in my letter. The committee approv'd, and used such diligence that, conducted by my son, the stores arrived at the camp as soon as the waggons. They consisted of twenty parcels, each containing
paras.z: 我在营地的时候，有一天晚上同邓巴上校那个团的军官们一起吃晚饭，上校向我说起他替下级军官们担忧。他说，他们大都不宽裕，在这个物价昂贵的地方，实在置办不起这样长途行军所需的物品，而且要穿过一片什么也买不到的荒野。我同情他们的处境，决心设法替他们弄些接济。不过我没有向他透露我的打算，只在第二天早晨写信给议会里有权支配一部分公款的那个委员会，热心地请他们考虑这些军官的情形，建议送给他们一批必需品和食品作为礼物。我儿子对军营生活和其中的需要有些经验，替我开了一张单子，我把它附在信里。委员会同意了，而且办得那样迅速，在我儿子的押送下，这批物品同大车一起到了营地。物品共二十包，每包内有：

paras.e: 6 lbs. loaf sugar.            1 Gloucester cheese. 6 lbs. good Muscovado do.     1 kegg containing 20 lbs. good butter. 1 lb. good green tea.         2 doz. old Madeira wine. 1 lb. good bohea do.          2 gallons Jamaica spirits. 6 lbs. good ground coffee.    1 bottle flour of mustard. 6 lbs. chocolate.             2 well-cur'd hams. 1-2 cwt. best white biscuit.  1-2 dozen dry'd tongues. 1-2 lb. pepper.               6 lbs. rice. 1 quart best white wine       6 lbs. raisins. vinegar.
paras.z: 方糖 6 磅；上等粗红糖 6 磅；上等绿茶 1 磅；上等武夷茶 1 磅；上等咖啡粉 6 磅；巧克力 6 磅；上等白饼干半英担；胡椒半磅；上等白葡萄酒醋 1 夸脱；格洛斯特干酪 1 块；上等黄油 1 小桶（20 磅）；陈年马德拉葡萄酒 2 打；牙买加烈酒 2 加仑；芥末粉 1 瓶；腌制精良的火腿 2 只；干舌半打；大米 6 磅；葡萄干 6 磅。

paras.e: These twenty parcels, well pack'd, were placed on as many horses, each parcel, with the horse, being intended as a present for one officer. They were very thankfully receiv'd, and the kindness acknowledg'd by letters to me from the colonels of both regiments, in the most grateful terms. The general, too, was highly satisfied with my conduct in procuring him the waggons, etc., and readily paid my account of disbursements, thanking me repeatedly, and requesting my farther assistance in sending provisions after him. I undertook this also, and was busily employ'd in it till we heard of his defeat, advancing for the service of my own money, upwards of one thousand pounds sterling, of which I sent him an account. It came to his hands, luckily for me, a few days before the battle, and he return'd me immediately an order on the paymaster for the round sum of one thousand pounds, leaving the remainder to the next account. I consider this payment as good luck, having never been able to obtain that remainder, of which more hereafter.
paras.z: 这二十包东西包扎得很好，驮在二十匹马上，每一包连同那匹马算作送给一位军官的礼物。他们十分感激地收下了，两个团的上校都写信给我，用最感激的言辞表示谢意。将军对我替他弄到大车等等的作为也十分满意，爽快地付清了我的垫款账目，一再向我道谢，并且请我继续帮忙，随后给他运送粮食。这件事我也承担下来，忙着办理，直到我们听到他战败的消息；我为这项差事垫付了自己的钱一千多英镑，把账目寄给了他。算我运气好，账目在战斗前几天到了他手里，他立刻给我开了一张向军需官领款的支付令，整数一千镑，余数留待下次结算。我把收到这笔款看作好运，因为那余数我始终没能拿到，这件事后面再说。

paras.e: This general was, I think, a brave man, and might probably have made a figure as a good officer in some European war. But he had too much self-confidence, too high an opinion of the validity of regular troops, and too mean a one of both Americans and Indians. George Croghan, our Indian interpreter, join'd him on his march with one hundred of those people, who might have been of great use to his army as guides, scouts, etc., if he had treated them kindly; but he slighted and neglected them, and they gradually left him.
paras.z: 我认为这位将军是个勇敢的人，在欧洲的某场战争里也许会成为一名出色的军官。可是他太自信了，把正规军的效能看得太高，把美洲人和印第安人都看得太低。我们的印第安语翻译乔治·克罗根带着一百名印第安人在行军途中加入了他的队伍；如果他善待他们，这些人作为向导、侦察兵等等，本来可以对他的军队大有用处。可是他轻视他们，冷落他们，他们就渐渐离开了他。

paras.e: In conversation with him one day, he was giving me some account of his intended progress. "After taking Fort Duquesne," says he, "I am to proceed to Niagara; and, having taken that, to Frontenac, if the season will allow time; and I suppose it will, for Duquesne can hardly detain me above three or four days; and then I see nothing that can obstruct my march to Niagara." Having before revolv'd in my mind the long line his army must make in their march by a very narrow road, to be cut for them thro' the woods and bushes, and also what I had read of a former defeat of fifteen hundred French, who invaded the Iroquois country, I had conceiv'd some doubts and some fears for the event of the campaign. But I ventur'd only to say, "To be sure, sir, if you arrive well before Duquesne, with these fine troops, so well provided with artillery, that place not yet compleatly fortified, and as we hear with no very strong garrison, can probably make but a short resistance. The only danger I apprehend of obstruction to your march is from ambuscades of Indians, who, by constant practice, are dexterous in laying and executing them; and the slender line, near four miles long, which your army must make, may expose it to be attack'd by surprise in its flanks, and to be cut like a thread into several pieces, which, from their distance, can not come up in time to support each other."
paras.z: 有一天同他谈话，他向我讲了一些他预定的进军计划。他说：“拿下迪凯纳堡以后，我要向尼亚加拉进军；拿下尼亚加拉以后，如果季节还来得及，再向弗朗特纳克进军；我想是来得及的，因为迪凯纳堡未必能耽搁我三四天以上；然后我看不出有什么能阻挡我向尼亚加拉进军。”在这之前我已经在心里琢磨过，他的军队要沿着一条在树林和灌木丛中为他们开辟出来的极窄的路行军，必然拉成很长的一线；我也想起读到过的从前一千五百名法国人侵入易洛魁地区而战败的事，所以对这场战役的结局有了几分怀疑和担忧。但我只敢这样说：“当然，先生，如果您带着这样精良的军队，又有这样充足的炮兵，顺利到达迪凯纳堡前面，那个地方工事还没有完全筑好，据我们听说守军也不很强，大概只能抵抗很短的时间。我担心会妨碍您进军的唯一危险，是印第安人的埋伏；他们靠着经常的实践，设伏和打伏击都十分熟练。您的军队势必拉成将近四英里长的细细一线，这可能使它的两翼遭到突然袭击，像一根线一样被切成几段，各段相隔太远，来不及赶上来互相支援。”

paras.e: He smil'd at my ignorance, and reply'd, "These savages may, indeed, be a formidable enemy to your raw American militia, but upon the king's regular and disciplin'd troops, sir, it is impossible they should make any impression." I was conscious of an impropriety in my disputing with a military man in matters of his profession, and said no more. The enemy, however, did not take the advantage of his army which I apprehended its long line of march expos'd it to, but let it advance without interruption till within nine miles of the place; and then, when more in a body (for it had just passed a river, where the front had halted till all were come over), and in a more open part of the woods than any it had pass'd, attack'd its advanced guard by a heavy fire from behind trees and bushes, which was the first intelligence the general had of an enemy's being near him. This guard being disordered, the general hurried the troops up to their assistance, which was done in great confusion, thro' waggons, baggage, and cattle; and presently the fire came upon their flank: the officers, being on horseback, were more easily distinguish'd, pick'd out as marks, and fell very fast; and the soldiers were crowded together in a huddle, having or hearing no orders, and standing to be shot at till two-thirds of them were killed; and then, being seiz'd with a panick, the whole fled with precipitation.
paras.z: 他笑我无知，回答说：“这些野蛮人对你们美洲那些没经过训练的民兵来说，也许确实是可怕的敌人；可是先生，要他们对国王训练有素的正规军有什么影响，那是不可能的。”我意识到同一位军人争论他本行的事是不得体的，就没有再说什么。不过，敌人并没有像我担心的那样，利用他的军队拉成长线行军的弱点，而是让它毫无阻挡地前进到离那个地方不到九英里的地方；这时军队比较集中了（因为它刚渡过一条河，前锋停下来等全军过完），又是在它经过的树林里最开阔的一处，敌人就从树木和灌木后面用猛烈的火力攻击它的前卫。这是将军头一回得知敌人就在附近。前卫乱了阵脚，将军催促部队上前增援，部队穿过大车、行李和牲畜，乱成一团；不一会儿，火力又打到了他们的侧翼。军官们骑在马上，容易辨认，被挑出来当靶子，很快地一个个倒下；士兵们挤作一堆，接不到也听不到命令，站在那里挨打，直到三分之二的人被打死；然后他们惊慌失措，全军仓皇溃逃。

paras.e: The waggoners took each a horse out of his team and scamper'd; their example was immediately followed by others; so that all the waggons, provisions, artillery, and stores were left to the enemy. The general, being wounded, was brought off with difficulty; his secretary, Mr. Shirley, was killed by his side; and out of eighty-six officers, sixty-three were killed or wounded, and seven hundred and fourteen men killed out of eleven hundred. These eleven hundred had been picked men from the whole army; the rest had been left behind with Colonel Dunbar, who was to follow with the heavier part of the stores, provisions, and baggage. The flyers, not being pursu'd, arriv'd at Dunbar's camp, and the panick they brought with them instantly seiz'd him and all his people; and, tho' he had now above one thousand men, and the enemy who had beaten Braddock did not at most exceed four hundred Indians and French together, instead of proceeding, and endeavoring to recover some of the lost honour, he ordered all the stores, ammunition, etc., to be destroy'd, that he might have more horses to assist his flight towards the settlements, and less lumber to remove. He was there met with requests from the governors of Virginia, Maryland, and Pennsylvania, that he would post his troops on the frontiers, so as to afford some protection to the inhabitants; but he continu'd his hasty march thro' all the country, not thinking himself safe till he arriv'd at Philadelphia, where the inhabitants could protect him. This whole transaction gave us Americans the first suspicion that our exalted ideas of the prowess of British regulars had not been well founded.
paras.z: 车夫们各从自己的车上解下一匹马，逃之夭夭；别人马上学他们的样；于是全部大车、粮食、大炮和军需都丢给了敌人。将军受了伤，好不容易才被救下来；他的秘书雪利先生在他身边阵亡；八十六名军官中，六十三名伤亡，一千一百名士兵中，七百一十四人阵亡。这一千一百人是从全军中挑选出来的精兵；其余的人留在后面，由邓巴上校率领，带着较重的军需、粮食和行李随后跟进。溃兵没有受到追击，逃到了邓巴的营地，他们带来的恐慌立刻传染了他和他的全部人马。虽然他这时有一千多人，而打败布雷多克的敌人，印第安人和法国人加在一起最多不过四百，他却不前进，不设法挽回一点丢掉的荣誉，反而下令把全部军需、弹药等等销毁，好腾出更多的马匹帮助他逃向有居民的地方，也少一些累赘要搬运。他在那里接到弗吉尼亚、马里兰和宾夕法尼亚总督的请求，要他把军队驻扎在边境上，给居民一些保护；可是他继续匆忙行军，穿过整个地区，直到抵达费城，有居民可以保护他，才觉得自己安全了。这整件事头一次使我们美洲人怀疑：我们对英国正规军的英勇抱有的那种崇高的看法，并没有充分的根据。

paras.e: In their first march, too, from their landing till they got beyond the settlements, they had plundered and stripped the inhabitants, totally ruining some poor families, besides insulting, abusing, and confining the people if they remonstrated. This was enough to put us out of conceit of such defenders, if we had really wanted any. How different was the conduct of our French friends in 1781, who, during a march thro' the most inhabited part of our country from Rhode Island to Virginia, near seven hundred miles, occasioned not the smallest complaint for the loss of a pig, a chicken, or even an apple.
paras.z: 再说，他们最初行军的时候，从登陆起直到走出有居民的地区，一路抢劫搜刮居民，使一些穷苦人家彻底破产；百姓如果抗议，还要受到侮辱、虐待和拘禁。就凭这一点，即使我们真的需要保护者，也足以使我们不稀罕这样的保护者了。我们的法国朋友在 1781 年的行为是多么不同啊！他们从罗得岛到弗吉尼亚，行军将近七百英里，穿过我国人烟最稠密的地区，没有因为丢了一头猪、一只鸡，甚至一个苹果，而引起过一点点抱怨。

paras.e: Captain Orme, who was one of the general's aids-de-camp, and, being grievously wounded, was brought off with him, and continu'd with him to his death, which happen'd in a few days, told me that he was totally silent all the first day, and at night only said, "Who would have thought it?" That he was silent again the following day, saying only at last, "We shall better know how to deal with them another time;" and dy'd in a few minutes after.
paras.z: 奥姆上尉是将军的副官之一，他身负重伤，同将军一起被救下来，一直陪着他直到他去世，那是几天以后的事。他告诉我，将军头一天整天一言不发，到夜里只说了一句：“谁想得到呢？”第二天他又沉默了，最后只说了一句：“下一回我们就更知道怎样对付他们了。”说完几分钟就死了。

paras.e: The secretary's papers, with all the general's orders, instructions, and correspondence, falling into the enemy's hands, they selected and translated into French a number of the articles, which they printed, to prove the hostile intentions of the British court before the declaration of war. Among these I saw some letters of the general to the ministry, speaking highly of the great service I had rendered the army, and recommending me to their notice. David Hume, too, who was some years after secretary to Lord Hertford, when minister in France, and afterward to General Conway, when secretary of state, told me he had seen among the papers in that office, letters from Braddock highly recommending me. But, the expedition having been unfortunate, my service, it seems, was not thought of much value, for those recommendations were never of any use to me.
paras.z: 秘书的文件，连同将军的全部命令、训令和往来信件，都落到了敌人手里。他们从中挑选了若干件，译成法文印了出来，用来证明英国朝廷在宣战之前就怀有敌意。我在其中看到将军写给内阁的几封信，对我为军队出的大力赞扬备至，并且向他们推荐我。大卫·休谟几年以后先是给驻法大使赫特福德勋爵当秘书，后来又给国务大臣康韦将军当秘书，他也告诉我，他在那个部门的文件里见过布雷多克极力推荐我的信。可是这次远征失败了，我出的力看来也就不被认为有多大价值，因为那些推荐对我从来没有起过任何作用。

paras.e: As to rewards from himself, I ask'd only one, which was, that he would give orders to his officers not to enlist any more of our bought servants, and that he would discharge such as had been already enlisted. This he readily granted, and several were accordingly return'd to their masters, on my application. Dunbar, when the command devolv'd on him, was not so generous. He being at Philadelphia, on his retreat, or rather flight, I apply'd to him for the discharge of the servants of three poor farmers of Lancaster county that he had enlisted, reminding him of the late general's orders on that head. He promised me that, if the masters would come to him at Trenton, where he should be in a few days on his march to New York, he would there deliver their men to them. They accordingly were at the expense and trouble of going to Trenton, and there he refus'd to perform his promise, to their great loss and disappointment.
paras.z: 至于他本人的酬谢，我只要求了一件事，就是请他下令给他的军官，不要再招募我们的契约仆人入伍，并且把已经招募的放回来。这一点他爽快地答应了，于是经我申请，有几个仆人被送还给了他们的主人。指挥权落到邓巴手里以后，他就没有这样大方了。他在撤退——不如说是逃跑——途中到了费城，我请求他把他招募的兰开斯特县三个穷苦农夫的仆人放回来，并且提醒他已故的将军在这方面下过的命令。他答应我，只要主人们到特伦顿去找他，他几天后在去纽约的行军途中会到那里，他就在那里把人交还给他们。他们于是花了钱、费了事去了特伦顿，到了那里他却不肯履行诺言，使他们大受损失，大失所望。

paras.e: As soon as the loss of the waggons and horses was generally known, all the owners came upon me for the valuation which I had given bond to pay. Their demands gave me a great deal of trouble, my acquainting them that the money was ready in the paymaster's hands, but that orders for paying it must first be obtained from General Shirley, and my assuring them that I had apply'd to that general by letter; but, he being at a distance, an answer could not soon be receiv'd, and they must have patience, all this was not sufficient to satisfy, and some began to sue me. General Shirley at length relieved me from this terrible situation by appointing commissioners to examine the claims, and ordering payment. They amounted to near twenty thousand pound, which to pay would have ruined me.
paras.z: 大车和马匹损失的消息一传开，所有的车马主人都来找我，要我照我出具保证书担保的估价赔偿。他们的要求给我添了极大的麻烦。我告诉他们，钱已经准备好，在军需官手里，但必须先得到雪利将军的付款命令；我向他们保证我已经写信向那位将军申请了，可是他离得远，一时收不到回信，他们必须耐心等待。这一切都不足以使他们满意，有些人开始控告我。雪利将军终于把我从这可怕的处境中解救出来，他指派了专员审查各项索赔，并下令付款。索赔总数将近两万镑，要是由我来付，我就倾家荡产了。

paras.e: Before we had the news of this defeat, the two Doctors Bond came to me with a subscription paper for raising money to defray the expense of a grand firework, which it was intended to exhibit at a rejoicing on receipt of the news of our taking Fort Duquesne. I looked grave, and said it would, I thought, be time enough to prepare for the rejoicing when we knew we should have occasion to rejoice. They seem'd surpris'd that I did not immediately comply with their proposal. "Why the d--l!" says one of them, "you surely don't suppose that the fort will not be taken?" "I don't know that it will not be taken, but I know that the events of war are subject to great uncertainty." I gave them the reasons of my doubting; the subscription was dropt, and the projectors thereby missed the mortification they would have undergone if the firework had been prepared.
