Dr. Bond, on some other occasion afterward, said that he did not like Franklin's forebodings.
paras.z: 在我们得到这次战败的消息之前，两位邦德医生拿着一张捐款单来找我，要筹钱举办一场盛大的焰火，打算在接到我们攻下迪凯纳堡的消息时庆祝一番。我神情严肃地说，我想，等我们知道确有可庆祝的事，再准备庆祝也来得及。他们见我没有立刻答应他们的提议，似乎很惊讶。其中一位说：“怎么，见鬼！你总不会以为那座堡垒拿不下来吧？”“我不知道它拿不下来，但我知道战争中的事是很没有准的。”我把我怀疑的理由告诉了他们；捐款的事就作罢了，发起的人因此免去了一场难堪——要是焰火备好了，他们是要受这场难堪的。后来在另一个场合，邦德医生说，他不喜欢富兰克林的不祥预感。

paras.e: Governor Morris, who had continually worried the Assembly with message after message before the defeat of Braddock, to beat them into the making of acts to raise money for the defense of the province, without taxing, among others, the proprietary estates, and had rejected all their bills for not having such an exempting clause, now redoubled his attacks with more hope of success, the danger and necessity being greater. The Assembly, however, continu'd firm, believing they had justice on their side, and that it would be giving up an essential right if they suffered the governor to amend their money-bills. In one of the last, indeed, which was for granting fifty thousand pounds, his propos'd amendment was only of a single word. The bill expressed "that all estates, real and personal, were to be taxed, those of the proprietaries not excepted." His amendment was, for not read only: a small, but very material alteration. However, when the news of this disaster reached England, our friends there, whom we had taken care to furnish with all the Assembly's answers to the governor's messages, rais'd a clamor against the proprietaries for their meanness and injustice in giving their governor such instructions; some going so far as to say that, by obstructing the defense of their province, they forfeited their right to it. They were intimidated by this, and sent orders to their receiver-general to add five thousand pounds of their money to whatever sum might be given by the Assembly for such purpose.
paras.z: 莫里斯总督在布雷多克战败之前，就一份接一份地用咨文不断地纠缠议会，要逼他们制定法案为本殖民地的防务筹款，而又不向业主的产业（以及其他）征税；议会的法案凡是没有这样的豁免条款，全都被他否决了。这时危险和需要都更大了，他就加倍进攻，指望更能得手。可是议会仍然坚定不移，相信正义在他们一边，认为如果容许总督修改他们的财政法案，那就是放弃了一项根本的权利。其实在最后的几个法案之一，就是拨款五万镑的那一个里，他提议的修改只有一个词。法案写的是“所有不动产和动产均须课税，业主的产业亦不例外（not excepted）”。他的修改是把“不（not）”改成“唯（only）”：改动很小，关系却极大。可是，这场灾难的消息传到英国，我们在那里的朋友——我们一直留心把议会对总督咨文的全部答复都寄给他们——就对业主们发出一片责难，说他们给总督下这样的训令是卑鄙而不公道的；有人甚至说，他们阻挠保卫自己的殖民地，就丧失了对它的权利。业主们被这吓住了，下令给他们的总收税官，不管议会为此拨款多少，都从他们的钱里再加上五千镑。

paras.e: This, being notified to the House, was accepted in lieu of their share of a general tax, and a new bill was form'd, with an exempting clause, which passed accordingly. By this act I was appointed one of the commissioners for disposing of the money, sixty thousand pounds. I had been active in modelling the bill and procuring its passage, and had, at the same time, drawn a bill for establishing and disciplining of a voluntary militia, which I carried thro' the House without much difficulty, as care was taken in it to leave the Quakers at their liberty. To promote the association necessary to form the militia, I wrote a dialogue, [14] stating and answering all the objections I could think of to such a militia, which was printed, and had, as I thought, great effect.
paras.z: 议院接到通知，就接受了这笔钱，作为他们在普遍课税中应摊份额的替代；于是另拟了一个新法案，带有豁免条款，就这样通过了。根据这项法令，我被任命为支配这笔款项——六万镑——的专员之一。在拟定这个法案并促成它通过的过程中，我一直很积极；同时，我还起草了一项建立并训练志愿民兵的法案，没费多大困难就让它在议院通过了，因为其中特别留意让贵格会教徒可以自便。为了促成组建民兵所必需的结社，我写了一篇对话[14]，把我能想到的对这种民兵的一切反对意见一一列出并加以答复；这篇对话印了出来，照我看效果很大。

paras.e: [14] This dialogue and the militia act are in the "Gentleman's Magazine" for February and March, 1756.--[Marg. note.]
paras.z: [14] 这篇对话和民兵法载于 1756 年 2 月和 3 月的《绅士杂志》。——［页边注］

paras.e: While the several companies in the city and country were forming and learning their exercise, the governor prevail'd with me to take charge of our North-western frontier, which was infested by the enemy, and provide for the defense of the inhabitants by raising troops and building a line of forts. I undertook this military business, tho' I did not conceive myself well qualified for it. He gave me a commission with full powers, and a parcel of blank commissions for officers, to be given to whom I thought fit. I had but little difficulty in raising men, having soon five hundred and sixty under my command. My son, who had in the preceding war been an officer in the army rais'd against Canada, was my aid-de-camp, and of great use to me. The Indians had burned Gnadenhut, a village settled by the Moravians, and massacred the inhabitants; but the place was thought a good situation for one of the forts.
paras.z: 城里和乡下的各个连队正在组建并学习操练的时候，总督说服我去负责我们的西北边境——那里正受敌人的骚扰——招募军队，修筑一线堡垒，为居民提供防卫。我承担了这项军务，虽然我并不认为自己很有资格。他给了我一份有全权的委任状，还有一叠空白的军官委任状，由我发给我认为合适的人。招募人手没有多大困难，不久我麾下就有了五百六十人。我儿子在上一次战争中曾在征讨加拿大的军队里当过军官，这时做我的副官，对我大有用处。印第安人烧毁了摩拉维亚教徒定居的村子格纳登胡特，屠杀了那里的居民；但那个地方被认为是修筑一座堡垒的好位置。

paras.e: In order to march thither, I assembled the companies at Bethlehem, the chief establishment of those people. I was surprised to find it in so good a posture of defense; the destruction of Gnadenhut had made them apprehend danger. The principal buildings were defended by a stockade; they had purchased a quantity of arms and ammunition from New York, and had even plac'd quantities of small paving stones between the windows of their high stone houses, for their women to throw down upon the heads of any Indians that should attempt to force into them. The armed brethren, too, kept watch, and reliev'd as methodically as in any garrison town. In conversation with the bishop, Spangenberg, I mention'd this my surprise; for, knowing they had obtained an act of Parliament exempting them from military duties in the colonies, I had suppos'd they were conscientiously scrupulous of bearing arms. He answer'd me that it was not one of their established principles, but that, at the time of their obtaining that act, it was thought to be a principle with many of their people. On this occasion, however, they, to their surprise, found it adopted by but a few. It seems they were either deceiv'd in themselves, or deceiv'd the Parliament; but common sense, aided by present danger, will sometimes be too strong for whimsical opinions.
paras.z: 为了向那里进军，我把各连集合在伯利恒，那是摩拉维亚教徒的主要据点。我惊讶地发现它的防御布置得那样好；格纳登胡特的毁灭使他们感到了危险。主要的建筑物有木栅防护；他们从纽约买了一批武器弹药，甚至在他们高大的石头房子的窗户之间堆了许多铺路用的小石块，好让妇女们在印第安人企图闯入时往他们头上扔。武装的教友们也轮流放哨、换岗，同任何驻军城镇一样有条不紊。我同主教施潘根贝格谈话时，提到我的这种惊讶；因为我知道他们曾取得国会的一项法令，免除他们在殖民地的兵役，我原以为他们是出于良心而不肯拿武器的。他回答我说，那并不是他们既定的原则之一，只是在他们取得那项法令的时候，人们以为他们中间许多人把它当作原则。可是到了这一回，他们惊讶地发现，只有很少的人持这种原则。看来他们不是自己骗了自己，就是骗了国会；不过，常识加上眼前的危险，有时会比古怪的见解更强有力。

paras.e: It was the beginning of January when we set out upon this business of building forts. I sent one detachment toward the Minisink, with instructions to erect one for the security of that upper part of the country, and another to the lower part, with similar instructions; and I concluded to go myself with the rest of my force to Gnadenhut, where a fort was tho't more immediately necessary. The Moravians procur'd me five waggons for our tools, stores, baggage, etc.
paras.z: 我们出发去办修筑堡垒这件事，是在一月初。我派一支分队到米尼辛克方向去，指示他们修一座堡垒，保卫那一带上游地区的安全；又派另一支到下游地区去，给了同样的指示；我自己决定带着其余的兵力去格纳登胡特，那里被认为更迫切需要一座堡垒。摩拉维亚教徒替我弄到五辆大车，装运我们的工具、军需、行李等等。

paras.e: Just before we left Bethlehem, eleven farmers, who had been driven from their plantations by the Indians, came to me requesting a supply of firearms, that they might go back and fetch off their cattle. I gave them each a gun with suitable ammunition. We had not march'd many miles before it began to rain, and it continued raining all day; there were no habitations on the road to shelter us, till we arriv'd near night at the house of a German, where, and in his barn, we were all huddled together, as wet as water could make us. It was well we were not attack'd in our march, for our arms were of the most ordinary sort, and our men could not keep their gun locks dry. The Indians are dextrous in contrivances for that purpose, which we had not. They met that day the eleven poor farmers above mentioned, and killed ten of them. The one who escap'd inform'd that his and his companions' guns would not go off, the priming being wet with the rain.
paras.z: 我们正要离开伯利恒的时候，有十一个被印第安人赶出自己田庄的农夫来找我，请求发给他们火器，好回去把牲口赶出来。我给了他们每人一支枪和相应的弹药。我们没走几英里就下起雨来，一直下了一整天；路上没有人家可以让我们避雨，直到天快黑时才到了一个德国人的家，我们大家全都挤在他的屋子和谷仓里，浑身湿得透透的。幸亏我们在行军途中没有遭到袭击，因为我们的武器是最普通的那一种，我们的人没法使枪机保持干燥。印第安人在这方面很有巧妙的办法，我们却没有。那一天他们遇上了前面说的那十一个可怜的农夫，杀了其中十个。逃出来的那一个报告说，他和同伴们的枪都打不响，因为引火药被雨淋湿了。

paras.e: The next day being fair, we continu'd our march, and arriv'd at the desolated Gnadenhut. There was a saw-mill near, round which were left several piles of boards, with which we soon hutted ourselves; an operation the more necessary at that inclement season, as we had no tents. Our first work was to bury more effectually the dead we found there, who had been half interr'd by the country people.
paras.z: 第二天天晴了，我们继续行军，到了荒无人烟的格纳登胡特。附近有一座锯木厂，周围留着几堆木板，我们很快就用这些木板搭起了棚屋；在那样严寒的季节，我们又没有帐篷，这件事更是必不可少。我们的头一件工作是把在那里发现的死者埋得更严实些，乡下人先前只是草草地埋了一半。

paras.e: The next morning our fort was plann'd and mark'd out, the circumference measuring four hundred and fifty-five feet, which would require as many palisades to be made of trees, one with another, of a foot diameter each. Our axes, of which we had seventy, were immediately set to work to cut down trees, and, our men being dextrous in the use of them, great despatch was made. Seeing the trees fall so fast, I had the curiosity to look at my watch when two men began to cut at a pine; in six minutes they had it upon the ground, and I found it of fourteen inches diameter. Each pine made three palisades of eighteen feet long, pointed at one end. While these were preparing, our other men dug a trench all round, of three feet deep, in which the palisades were to be planted; and, our waggons, the bodys being taken off, and the fore and hind wheels separated by taking out the pin which united the two parts of the perch, we had ten carriages, with two horses each, to bring the palisades from the woods to the spot. When they were set up, our carpenters built a stage of boards all round within, about six feet high, for the men to stand on when to fire thro' the loopholes. We had one swivel gun, which we mounted on one of the angles, and fir'd it as soon as fix'd, to let the Indians know, if any were within hearing, that we had such pieces; and thus our fort, if such a magnificent name may be given to so miserable a stockade, was finish'd in a week, though it rain'd so hard every other day that the men could not work.
paras.z: 第二天早晨，我们规划并标出了堡垒的范围，周长四百五十五英尺，这就需要用树做成同样数目的木桩，平均每根直径一英尺。我们有七十把斧子，立刻全都用上去伐树；我们的人使斧子很在行，进展很快。看到树倒得那样快，我出于好奇，在两个人开始砍一棵松树的时候看了看表；六分钟他们就把它放倒了，我量了一下，直径十四英寸。每棵松树可以做三根十八英尺长的木桩，一头削尖。准备这些木桩的时候，其余的人在四周挖了一条三英尺深的沟，木桩就栽在里面。我们把大车的车厢卸下来，拔掉连接前后两部分车辕的销子，把前后轮分开，这样就有了十辆车，每辆套两匹马，把木桩从树林里运到工地。木桩立起来以后，我们的木匠在里面四周用木板搭了一圈平台，大约六英尺高，供人站在上面从枪眼里射击。我们有一门回旋炮，把它架在一个角上，一装好就放了一炮，让印第安人知道——如果有人在听得见的范围内——我们有这样的家伙。这样，我们的堡垒——如果这样简陋的木栅也当得起这样堂皇的名字——一个星期就完工了，尽管每隔一天就下一场大雨，人们无法干活。

paras.e: This gave me occasion to observe, that, when men are employ'd, they are best content'd; for on the days they worked they were good-natur'd and cheerful, and, with the consciousness of having done a good day's work, they spent the evening jollily; but on our idle days they were mutinous and quarrelsome, finding fault with their pork, the bread, etc., and in continual ill-humor, which put me in mind of a sea-captain, whose rule it was to keep his men constantly at work; and, when his mate once told him that they had done every thing, and there was nothing further to employ them about, "Oh," says he, "Make them scour the anchor."
paras.z: 这使我有机会观察到，人有事做的时候最满足；因为在干活的日子里，他们脾气好，心情愉快，自觉干了一整天好活，晚上过得很快活；可是在闲着的日子里，他们就不服管教，爱吵架，挑剔他们的猪肉、面包等等，老是没有好气。这使我想起一位船长，他的规矩是让手下人不停地干活；有一回大副告诉他，什么活都干完了，再没有什么可让他们干的了，他说：“哦，叫他们去擦锚。”

paras.e: This kind of fort, however contemptible, is a sufficient defense against Indians, who have no cannon. Finding ourselves now posted securely, and having a place to retreat to on occasion, we ventur'd out in parties to scour the adjacent country. We met with no Indians, but we found the places on the neighboring hills where they had lain to watch our proceedings. There was an art in their contrivance of those places, that seems worth mention. It being winter, a fire was necessary for them; but a common fire on the surface of the ground would by its light have discovered their position at a distance. They had therefore dug holes in the ground about three feet diameter, and somewhat deeper; we saw where they had with their hatchets cut off the charcoal from the sides of burnt logs lying in the woods. With these coals they had made small fires in the bottom of the holes, and we observ'd among the weeds and grass the prints of their bodies, made by their laying all round, with their legs hanging down in the holes to keep their feet warm, which, with them, is an essential point. This kind of fire, so manag'd, could not discover them, either by its light, flame, sparks, or even smoke: it appear'd that their number was not great, and it seems they saw we were too many to be attacked by them with prospect of advantage.
paras.z: 这种堡垒不管多么不起眼，对付没有大炮的印第安人却是足够的防御。我们发觉自己已经驻扎稳妥，万一有事也有了退守的地方，就大着胆子分队出去搜索附近的地区。我们没有遇到印第安人，但在邻近的小山上发现了他们埋伏着窥探我们动静的地方。他们布置这些地方的办法颇有技巧，似乎值得一提。时值冬天，他们非生火不可；可是在地面上生一堆普通的火，火光会让人老远就发现他们的位置。所以他们在地上挖了些洞，直径大约三英尺，深度还要多一点；我们看到他们用小斧子从树林里烧过的倒木边上砍下木炭的痕迹。他们用这些木炭在洞底生了小火；我们在杂草丛中看到他们身体留下的印迹，那是他们围着洞躺成一圈，把腿垂在洞里暖脚留下的——暖脚在他们是头等要紧的事。这样生的火，无论是火光、火焰、火星，甚至烟，都不会暴露他们。看来他们人数不多，大概是看到我们人太多，进攻占不到便宜。

paras.e: We had for our chaplain a zealous Presbyterian minister, Mr. Beatty, who complained to me that the men did not generally attend his prayers and exhortations. When they enlisted, they were promised, besides pay and provisions, a gill of rum a day, which was punctually serv'd out to them, half in the morning, and the other half in the evening; and I observ'd they were as punctual in attending to receive it; upon which I said to Mr. Beatty, "It is, perhaps, below the dignity of your profession to act as steward of the rum, but if you were to deal it out and only just after prayers, you would have them all about you." He liked the tho't, undertook the office, and, with the help of a few hands to measure out the liquor, executed it to satisfaction, and never were prayers more generally and more punctually attended; so that I thought this method preferable to the punishment inflicted by some military laws for non-attendance on divine service.
paras.z: 我们的随军牧师是一位热心的长老会牧师贝蒂先生，他向我抱怨说，士兵们多半不来参加他的祈祷和劝勉。他们入伍的时候，除了饷银和口粮，还答应每天给一及耳朗姆酒，这酒是按时发给他们的，早晨一半，晚上一半；我注意到他们来领酒也同样准时。于是我对贝蒂先生说：“让您来当朗姆酒的管事，也许有失您这一行的尊严；可是如果由您来分酒，而且只在祈祷刚结束的时候分，他们就会全都围到您身边来了。”他喜欢这个主意，承担了这个差事，在几个人帮着量酒的情况下，办得很令人满意；从来没有哪一次祈祷到的人更齐、更准时。所以我认为，这个办法比某些军法对不参加礼拜的人所施加的惩罚要好。

paras.e: I had hardly finish'd this business, and got my fort well stor'd with provisions, when I receiv'd a letter from the governor, acquainting me that he had call'd the Assembly, and wished my attendance there, if the posture of affairs on the frontiers was such that my remaining there was no longer necessary. My friends, too, of the Assembly, pressing me by their letters to be, if possible, at the meeting, and my three intended forts being now compleated, and the inhabitants contented to remain on their farms under that protection, I resolved to return; the more willingly, as a New England officer, Colonel Clapham, experienced in Indian war, being on a visit to our establishment, consented to accept the command. I gave him a commission, and, parading the garrison, had it read before them, and introduc'd him to them as an officer who, from his skill in military affairs, was much more fit to command them than myself; and, giving them a little exhortation, took my leave. I was escorted as far as Bethlehem, where I rested a few days to recover from the fatigue I had undergone. The first night, being in a good bed, I could hardly sleep, it was so different from my hard lodging on the floor of our hut at Gnaden wrapt only in a blanket or two.
paras.z: 我刚办完这件事，把堡垒里的粮食储备充足，就收到总督的一封信，告诉我他已经召集议会，如果边境上的形势已经不再需要我留在那里，希望我出席。我在议会里的朋友们也来信催我，要我尽可能参加会议；我预定的三座堡垒这时已经完工，居民们在这样的保护下也安心留在自己的田庄上了，我就决定回去。我更乐意回去，是因为一位新英格兰的军官克拉彭上校正好来我们这里访问，他在同印第安人作战方面很有经验，答应接受指挥权。我给了他一份委任状，把守军集合起来，当众宣读，并把他介绍给他们，说这位军官精通军事，远比我适合指挥他们；我又勉励了他们几句，就告辞了。他们把我护送到伯利恒，我在那里休息了几天，从经受的劳累中恢复过来。头一夜睡在一张好床上，我几乎睡不着，这同我在格纳登胡特只裹一两条毯子、睡在棚屋地板上的硬铺太不一样了。

paras.e: While at Bethlehem, I inquir'd a little into the practice of the Moravians: some of them had accompanied me, and all were very kind to me. I found they work'd for a common stock, eat at common tables, and slept in common dormitories, great numbers together. In the dormitories I observed loopholes, at certain distances all along just under the ceiling, which I thought judiciously placed for change of air. I was at their church, where I was entertain'd with good musick, the organ being accompanied with violins, hautboys, flutes, clarinets, etc. I understood that their sermons were not usually preached to mixed congregations of men, women, and children, as is our common practice, but that they assembled sometimes the married men, at other times their wives, then the young men, the young women, and the little children, each division by itself. The sermon I heard was to the latter, who came in and were plac'd in rows on benches; the boys under the conduct of a young man, their tutor, and the girls conducted by a young woman. The discourse seem'd well adapted to their capacities, and was deliver'd in a pleasing, familiar manner, coaxing them, as it were, to be good. They behav'd very orderly, but looked pale and unhealthy, which made me suspect they were kept too much within doors, or not allow'd sufficient exercise.
paras.z: 在伯利恒的时候，我稍稍了解了一下摩拉维亚教徒的习俗；他们中有几个人陪过我，大家对我都很好。我发现他们为公共的积蓄而劳动，在公共的饭桌上吃饭，睡在公共的宿舍里，许多人睡在一起。我注意到宿舍里紧挨天花板的地方，每隔一定距离就有一个通气孔，我认为这是为了换气而设的，安排得很有见地。我去了他们的教堂，在那里听到了很好的音乐，管风琴由小提琴、双簧管、长笛、单簧管等等伴奏。我听说，他们的讲道通常不像我们一般的做法那样对着男女老少混在一起的会众讲，而是有时召集已婚的男子，有时召集他们的妻子，然后是青年男子、青年女子和小孩子，每一类人各自单独听讲。我听的那一次讲道是讲给小孩子的，他们进来，一排排坐在长凳上；男孩由一个年轻男子——他们的教师——带领，女孩由一个年轻女子带领。讲道似乎很适合他们的理解力，讲得亲切动听，可以说是在哄着他们学好。他们举止很守规矩，但看上去脸色苍白，不大健康，这使我疑心他们被关在屋里的时间太多，或者没有得到足够的活动。

paras.e: I inquir'd concerning the Moravian marriages, whether the report was true that they were by lot. I was told that lots were us'd only in particular cases; that generally, when a young man found himself dispos'd to marry, he inform'd the elders of his class, who consulted the elder ladies that govern'd the young women. As these elders of the different sexes were well acquainted with the tempers and dispositions of their respective pupils, they could best judge what matches were suitable, and their judgments were generally acquiesc'd in; but if, for example, it should happen that two or three young women were found to be equally proper for the young man, the lot was then recurred to. I objected, if the matches are not made by the mutual choice of the parties, some of them may chance to be very unhappy. "And so they may," answer'd my informer, "if you let the parties chuse for themselves;" which, indeed, I could not deny.
paras.z: 我问起摩拉维亚教徒的婚姻，问传闻说他们靠抽签定亲是不是真的。人家告诉我，只在特殊的情形下才用抽签；一般说来，一个青年男子觉得自己想结婚了，就告诉他那一班的长老，长老再同管理青年女子的年长妇女商量。因为这些男女长老对各自管教的人的脾气和性情都很了解，他们最能判断哪些亲事合适，他们的判断一般也都被接受。但是，比方说，如果碰巧发现有两三个青年女子对那个青年男子同样合适，那时才诉诸抽签。我提出异议说，如果亲事不是由当事人双方自己选择而定的，其中有些人说不定会很不幸福。告诉我这些情况的人回答说：“让当事人自己选择，他们也可能这样。”这一点，我确实无法否认。

paras.e: Being returned to Philadelphia, I found the association went on swimmingly, the inhabitants that were not Quakers having pretty generally come into it, formed themselves into companies, and chose their captains, lieutenants, and ensigns, according to the new law. Dr. B. visited me, and gave me an account of the pains he had taken to spread a general good liking to the law, and ascribed much to those endeavors. I had had the vanity to ascribe all to my Dialogue; however, not knowing but that he might be in the right, I let him enjoy his opinion, which I take to be generally the best way in such cases. The officers, meeting, chose me to be colonel of the regiment, which I this time accepted. I forget how many companies we had, but we paraded about twelve hundred well-looking men, with a company of artillery, who had been furnished with six brass field-pieces, which they had become so expert in the use of as to fire twelve times in a minute. The first time I reviewed my regiment they accompanied me to my house, and would salute me with some rounds fired before my door, which shook down and broke several glasses of my electrical apparatus. And my new honour proved not much less brittle; for all our commissions were soon after broken by a repeal of the law in England.
paras.z: 回到费城，我发现结社进行得十分顺利，不是贵格会教徒的居民相当普遍地参加了，按照新法律自己编成连队，选出了上尉、中尉和少尉。B 医生来看我，向我讲了他为使大家普遍喜欢这项法律而花的力气，并把很多功劳归于这些努力。我原本很虚荣地把一切都归功于我的《对话》；不过，我不敢说他一定不对，就让他去享受他的看法，我认为在这类事情上这一般是最好的办法。军官们开会，推选我当团的上校，这一回我接受了。我忘了我们有多少个连，但我们列队检阅的有大约一千二百名仪表堂堂的士兵，还有一个炮兵连，配备了六门黄铜野战炮，他们使用得那样熟练，一分钟能放十二炮。我头一次检阅我的团的时候，他们把我送到家门口，一定要在我门前放几排枪向我致敬，结果把我电学仪器上的几件玻璃器皿震下来摔碎了。而我新得的荣誉也不比它们结实多少；因为不久以后，那项法律在英国被废除，我们所有的委任状也都随之作废了。

paras.e: During this short time of my colonelship, being about to set out on a journey to Virginia, the officers of my regiment took it into their heads that it would be proper for them to escort me out of town, as far as the Lower Ferry. Just as I was getting on horseback they came to my door, between thirty and forty, mounted, and all in their uniforms. I had not been previously acquainted with the project, or I should have prevented it, being naturally averse to the assuming of state on any occasion; and I was a good deal chagrin'd at their appearance, as I could not avoid their accompanying me. What made it worse was, that, as soon as we began to move, they drew their swords and rode with them naked all the way. Somebody wrote an account of this to the proprietor, and it gave him great offense. No such honor had been paid him when in the province, nor to any of his governors; and he said it was only proper to princes of the blood royal, which may be true for aught I know, who was, and still am, ignorant of the etiquette in such cases.
paras.z: 在我当上校的这段短短的时间里，有一回我要动身去弗吉尼亚，我那个团的军官们忽然想到，他们应该把我护送出城，一直送到下渡口。我正要上马的时候，他们到了我的门口，有三四十人，都骑着马，穿着军服。我事先并不知道这个计划，不然我会制止的，因为我生性不喜欢在任何场合摆排场；他们一出现，我十分懊恼，因为我没法不让他们陪我。更糟的是，我们刚一动身，他们就拔出剑来，一路举着出鞘的剑骑行。有人把这件事写信告诉了业主，这使他大为恼火。他在本殖民地的时候，从没有人对他表示过这样的敬意，对他的任何一位总督也没有过；他说，这只适用于王室的亲王——这也许是真的，我可不知道，我过去不懂、现在仍然不懂这类场合的礼仪。

paras.e: This silly affair, however, greatly increased his rancour against me, which was before not a little, on account of my conduct in the Assembly respecting the exemption of his estate from taxation, which I had always oppos'd very warmly, and not without severe reflections on his meanness and injustice of contending for it. He accused me to the ministry as being the great obstacle to the king's service, preventing, by my influence in the House, the proper form of the bills for raising money, and he instanced this parade with my officers as a proof of my having an intention to take the government of the province out of his hands by force. He also applied to Sir Everard Fawkener, the postmaster-general, to deprive me of my office; but it had no other effect than to procure from Sir Everard a gentle admonition.
paras.z: 可是这件无聊的事大大加深了他对我的怨恨。这种怨恨原先就不小，因为我在议会里对于豁免他的产业捐税一事的所作所为：我一向非常激烈地反对，而且不免严厉地指责他力争这种豁免是卑鄙而不公道的。他向内阁控告我，说我是为国王效力的一大障碍，利用我在议院里的影响，阻止筹款法案采取适当的形式；他还举出我同我的军官们的这次游行，作为我有意用武力从他手里夺取本殖民地统治权的证据。他还请求邮政总长埃弗拉德·福克纳爵士撤掉我的职务；但这没有别的效果，只是使埃弗拉德爵士给了我一个温和的告诫。

paras.e: Notwithstanding the continual wrangle between the governor and the House, in which I, as a member, had so large a share, there still subsisted a civil intercourse between that gentleman and myself, and we never had any personal difference. I have sometimes since thought that his little or no resentment against me, for the answers it was known I drew up to his messages, might be the effect of professional habit, and that, being bred a lawyer, he might consider us both as merely advocates for contending clients in a suit, he for the proprietaries and I for the Assembly. He would, therefore, sometimes call in a friendly way to advise with me on difficult points, and sometimes, tho' not often, take my advice.
paras.z: 尽管总督同议院之间争吵不休，而我作为议员在其中占了那么大的一份，那位绅士和我之间仍然保持着客客气气的往来，我们从没有过个人的不和。后来我有时想，人人都知道他的咨文是我起草答复的，他却很少或者根本不怨恨我，这也许是职业习惯的结果：他是学法律出身的，也许把我们两个仅仅看作一场官司里替相争的当事人辩护的律师，他替业主，我替议会。所以他有时会友好地来访，在疑难的问题上同我商量，有时——虽然不常——也采纳我的意见。

paras.e: We acted in concert to supply Braddock's army with provisions; and, when the shocking news arrived of his defeat, the governor sent in haste for me, to consult with him on measures for preventing the desertion of the back counties. I forget now the advice I gave; but I think it was, that Dunbar should be written to, and prevail'd with, if possible, to post his troops on the frontiers for their protection, till, by re-enforcements from the colonies, he might be able to proceed on the expedition. And, after my return from the frontier, he would have had me undertake the conduct of such an expedition with provincial troops, for the reduction of Fort Duquesne, Dunbar and his men being otherwise employed; and he proposed to commission me as general. I had not so good an opinion of my military abilities as he profess'd to have, and I believe his professions must have exceeded his real sentiments; but probably he might think that my popularity would facilitate the raising of the men, and my influence in Assembly, the grant of money to pay them, and that, perhaps, without taxing the proprietary estate. Finding me not so forward to engage as he expected, the project was dropt, and he soon after left the government, being superseded by Captain Denny.
paras.z: 我们协力为布雷多克的军队供应粮食；他战败的惊人消息传来的时候，总督急忙派人来叫我，同他商量采取什么措施防止边远各县的居民逃离。我现在忘了我出的是什么主意；但我想是：应当写信给邓巴，尽可能说服他把军队驻扎在边境上保护居民，等各殖民地的援军到了，他也许还能继续远征。我从边境回来以后，他又想让我率领本殖民地的军队进行这样一次远征，去攻取迪凯纳堡，因为邓巴和他的人马另有任用；他提出要委任我为将军。我对自己的军事才能并不像他口头上说的那样有好评，我相信他口头上说的一定超过了他真实的想法；不过他大概是认为，我的人望会有助于招募士兵，我在议会里的影响会有助于拨款给他们发饷，而且也许还不用向业主的产业征税。他见我并不像他预期的那样踊跃，这个计划就作罢了；不久以后他卸了任，由丹尼上尉接替。

paras.e: Before I proceed in relating the part I had in public affairs under this new governor's administration, it may not be amiss here to give some account of the rise and progress of my philosophical reputation.
paras.z: 在我接着讲我在这位新总督任内所参与的公共事务之前，在这里讲一讲我在哲学（科学）上的名声是怎样起来、怎样发展的，也许并无不妥。

paras.e: In 1746, being at Boston, I met there with a Dr. Spence, who was lately arrived from Scotland, and show'd me some electric experiments. They were imperfectly perform'd, as he was not very expert; but, being on a subject quite new to me, they equally surpris'd and pleased me. Soon after my return to Philadelphia, our library company receiv'd from Mr. P. Collinson, Fellow of the Royal Society of London, a present of a glass tube, with some account of the use of it in making such experiments. I eagerly seized the opportunity of repeating what I had seen at Boston; and, by much practice, acquir'd great readiness in performing those, also, which we had an account of from England, adding a number of new ones. I say much practice, for my house was continually full, for some time, with people who came to see these new wonders.
paras.z: 1746 年我在波士顿，遇见了一位斯彭斯博士，他新近从苏格兰来，给我表演了几个电学实验。实验做得不大完美，因为他不很在行；但这个题目对我完全是新的，所以这些实验使我又惊又喜。我回到费城不久，我们的图书馆公司收到伦敦皇家学会会员 P. 柯林森先生赠送的一根玻璃管，还附有怎样用它做这类实验的说明。我急切地抓住这个机会，重做我在波士顿看到的实验；经过大量练习，我做那些从英国得到说明的实验也十分熟练了，还添了好些新的。我说“大量练习”，是因为有一段时间，我家里总是挤满了来看这些新奇迹的人。

paras.e: To divide a little this incumbrance among my friends, I caused a number of similar tubes to be blown at our glass-house, with which they furnish'd themselves, so that we had at length several performers. Among these, the principal was Mr. Kinnersley, an ingenious neighbor, who, being out of business, I encouraged to undertake showing the experiments for money, and drew up for him two lectures, in which the experiments were rang'd in such order, and accompanied with such explanations in such method, as that the foregoing should assist in comprehending the following. He procur'd an elegant apparatus for the purpose, in which all the little machines that I had roughly made for myself were nicely form'd by instrument-makers. His lectures were well attended, and gave great satisfaction; and after some time he went thro' the colonies, exhibiting them in every capital town, and pick'd up some money. In the West India islands, indeed, it was with difficulty the experiments could be made, from the general moisture of the air.
paras.z: 为了在朋友们中间分担一点这种负担，我让我们的玻璃厂吹制了一批同样的玻璃管，他们各自备了一根，这样我们终于有了好几位表演者。其中最主要的是金纳斯利先生，一位心灵手巧的邻居；他当时没有事做，我鼓励他以表演这些实验来挣钱，并替他写了两篇讲稿，把实验按这样的次序排列，配上这样有条理的解释，使前面的有助于理解后面的。他为此置办了一套精致的仪器，我自己粗粗做成的那些小器械，在这套仪器里都由仪器匠精工制成了。他的讲演听众很多，大家非常满意；过了些时候，他走遍各殖民地，在每个首府表演，挣了一些钱。不过在西印度群岛，因为空气普遍潮湿，这些实验是很难做成的。

paras.e: Oblig'd as we were to Mr. Collinson for his present of the tube, etc., I thought it right he should be inform'd of our success in using it, and wrote him several letters containing accounts of our experiments. He got them read in the Royal Society, where they were not at first thought worth so much notice as to be printed in their Transactions. One paper, which I wrote for Mr. Kinnersley, on the sameness of lightning with electricity, I sent to Dr. Mitchel, an acquaintance of mine, and one of the members also of that society, who wrote me word that it had been read, but was laughed at by the connoisseurs. The papers, however, being shown to Dr. Fothergill, he thought them of too much value to be stifled, and advis'd the printing of them. Mr. Collinson then gave them to Cave for publication in his Gentleman's Magazine; but he chose to print them separately in a pamphlet, and Dr. Fothergill wrote the preface. Cave, it seems, judged rightly for his profit, for by the additions that arrived after they swell'd to a quarto volume, which has had five editions, and cost him nothing for copy-money.
paras.z: 我们既然受惠于柯林森先生赠送的玻璃管等等，我想应当让他知道我们使用它的成绩，就给他写了几封信，叙述我们的实验。他让人在皇家学会宣读了这些信，起初学会并不认为它们值得那样重视、要印在《会报》上。有一篇论文，是我为金纳斯利先生写的，论闪电同电是一回事，我把它寄给了我的熟人、也是那个学会的会员米切尔博士；他来信告诉我，论文宣读了，但被行家们嘲笑了一番。不过这些论文拿给福瑟吉尔医生看了，他认为它们很有价值，不该被埋没，建议付印。于是柯林森先生把它们交给凯夫，要登在他的《绅士杂志》上；但凯夫决定把它们单独印成一本小册子，由福瑟吉尔医生写了序言。看来凯夫对自己的利益判断得很对，因为加上后来陆续寄到的补充，它们扩充成了一本四开的书，印了五版，而他没有花一文稿费。

paras.e: It was, however, some time before those papers were much taken notice of in England. A copy of them happening to fall into the hands of the Count de Buffon, a philosopher deservedly of great reputation in France, and, indeed, all over Europe, he prevailed with M. Dalibard to translate them into French, and they were printed at Paris. The publication offended the Abbé Nollet, preceptor in Natural Philosophy to the royal family, and an able experimenter, who had form'd and publish'd a theory of electricity, which then had the general vogue. He could not at first believe that such a work came from America, and said it must have been fabricated by his enemies at Paris, to decry his system. Afterwards, having been assur'd that there really existed such a person as Franklin at Philadelphia, which he had doubted, he wrote and published a volume of Letters, chiefly address'd to me, defending his theory, and denying the verity of my experiments, and of the positions deduc'd from them.
paras.z: 不过，这些论文过了一段时间才在英国受到较多的注意。有一本碰巧落到了布丰伯爵手里，他是一位在法国、其实在全欧洲都享有应得盛名的哲学家；他说服达利巴尔先生把它们译成法文，在巴黎印了出来。这本书的出版得罪了诺莱神父，他是王室的自然哲学教师，也是一位能干的实验家，曾经建立并发表过一种电学理论，当时普遍风行。他起初不能相信这样一部著作来自美洲，说一定是他在巴黎的敌人伪造出来贬低他的体系的。后来有人向他保证，费城确实有富兰克林这样一个人——这一点他原先是怀疑的——他就写了一卷《书信集》发表，主要是写给我的，为他的理论辩护，否认我的实验以及由实验推出的论点是真实的。

paras.e: I once purpos'd answering the abbé, and actually began the answer; but, on consideration that my writings contain'd a description of experiments which any one might repeat and verify, and if not to be verifi'd, could not be defended; or of observations offer'd as conjectures, and not delivered dogmatically, therefore not laying me under any obligation to defend them; and reflecting that a dispute between two persons, writing in different languages, might be lengthened greatly by mistranslations, and thence misconceptions of one another's meaning, much of one of the abbé's letters being founded on an error in the translation, I concluded to let my papers shift for themselves, believing it was better to spend what time I could spare from public business in making new experiments, than in disputing about those already made. I therefore never answered M. Nollet, and the event gave me no cause to repent my silence; for my friend M. le Roy, of the Royal Academy of Sciences, took up my cause and refuted him; my book was translated into the Italian, German, and Latin languages; and the doctrine it contain'd was by degrees universally adopted by the philosophers of Europe, in preference to that of the abbé; so that he lived to see himself the last of his sect, except Monsieur B------, of Paris, his élève and immediate disciple.
paras.z: 我一度打算答复这位神父，而且确实动手写了；但是考虑到，我的著作里所写的，一类是实验的描述，任何人都可以重做并加以验证，如果验证不了，辩护也无用；另一类是观察所得，是作为推测提出的，并没有武断地下结论，所以我并没有任何义务为它们辩护；又想到，两个用不同语言写作的人之间的争论，可能因为误译、从而误解对方的意思而大大拖长——神父的一封信里就有很多内容是建立在一处翻译错误上的——我就决定让我的论文自己去闯，相信把我从公务中能抽出的时间用来做新的实验，比用来争论已经做过的实验要好。所以我始终没有答复诺莱先生，而结果也没有让我后悔自己的沉默；因为我的朋友、皇家科学院的勒鲁瓦先生替我出面，驳倒了他；我的书被译成了意大利文、德文和拉丁文；书中所含的学说逐渐为欧洲的哲学家们普遍采纳，取代了神父的学说；结果他活着看到自己成了他那一派的最后一人，只有他的门生和嫡传弟子、巴黎的 B 先生除外。

paras.e: What gave my book the more sudden and general celebrity, was the success of one of its proposed experiments, made by Messrs. Dalibard and De Lor at Marly, for drawing lightning from the clouds. This engag'd the public attention every where. M. de Lor, who had an apparatus for experimental philosophy, and lectur'd in that branch of science, undertook to repeat what he called the Philadelphia Experiments; and, after they were performed before the king and court, all the curious of Paris flocked to see them. I will not swell this narrative with an account of that capital experiment, nor of the infinite pleasure I receiv'd in the success of a similar one I made soon after with a kite at Philadelphia, as both are to be found in the histories of electricity.
paras.z: 使我的书更加迅速、更加普遍地出名的，是书中提出的一个实验的成功：达利巴尔先生和德洛尔先生在马尔利做了从云中引下闪电的实验。这件事到处引起了公众的注意。德洛尔先生有一套实验哲学的仪器，并且讲授这门科学，他着手重做他所谓的“费城实验”；这些实验在国王和宫廷面前表演之后，巴黎所有好奇的人都蜂拥去看。我不想用那个重大实验的叙述来加长这篇记述，也不想讲我不久以后在费城用风筝做了一个类似的实验并且成功时所感到的无限快乐，因为这两件事在电学史里都可以找到。

paras.e: Dr. Wright, an English physician, when at Paris, wrote to a friend, who was of the Royal Society, an account of the high esteem my experiments were in among the learned abroad, and of their wonder that my writings had been so little noticed in England. The society, on this, resum'd the consideration of the letters that had been read to them; and the celebrated Dr. Watson drew up a summary account of them, and of all I had afterwards sent to England on the subject, which he accompanied with some praise of the writer. This summary was then printed in their Transactions; and some members of the society in London, particularly the very ingenious Mr. Canton, having verified the experiment of procuring lightning from the clouds by a pointed rod, and acquainting them with the success, they soon made me more than amends for the slight with which they had before treated me. Without my having made any application for that honor, they chose me a member, and voted that I should be excus'd the customary payments, which would have amounted to twenty-five guineas; and ever since have given me their Transactions gratis. They also presented me with the gold medal of Sir Godfrey Copley for the year 1753, the delivery of which was accompanied by a very handsome speech of the president, Lord Macclesfield, wherein I was highly honoured.
paras.z: 英国医生赖特博士在巴黎的时候，写信给一位皇家学会的朋友，讲到我的实验在国外学者中间享有多么高的声誉，以及他们对我的著作在英国竟那样不受注意感到多么惊讶。学会于是重新审议那些曾经向他们宣读过的信；著名的沃森博士把这些信，以及我后来就这个题目寄到英国的全部材料，写了一份概述，并附上对作者的一些赞扬。这份概述随后印在他们的《会报》上；伦敦的几位会员，特别是非常聪明的坎顿先生，用尖头的杆子验证了从云中取得闪电的实验，并把成功的消息告诉了学会。于是他们不久就对先前怠慢我的事作了绰绰有余的补偿。我并没有申请过那份荣誉，他们就选我为会员，并且表决免除我照例应缴的费用，那本来要二十五个几尼；此后一直免费赠送我他们的《会报》。他们还把 1753 年度的戈弗雷·科普利爵士金质奖章授予我，颁奖时会长麦克尔斯菲尔德勋爵发表了一篇非常漂亮的演说，对我备加推崇。

paras.e: Our new governor, Captain Denny, brought over for me the before-mentioned medal from the Royal Society, which he presented to me at an entertainment given him by the city. He accompanied it with very polite expressions of his esteem for me, having, as he said, been long acquainted with my character. After dinner, when the company, as was customary at that time, were engag'd in drinking, he took me aside into another room, and acquainted me that he had been advis'd by his friends in England to cultivate a friendship with me, as one who was capable of giving him the best advice, and of contributing most effectually to the making his administration easy; that he therefore desired of all things to have a good understanding with me, and he begg'd me to be assur'd of his readiness on all occasions to render me every service that might be in his power. He said much to me, also, of the proprietor's good disposition towards the province, and of the advantage it might be to us all, and to me in particular, if the opposition that had been so long continu'd to his measures was dropt, and harmony restor'd between him and the people; in effecting which, it was thought no one could be more serviceable than myself; and I might depend on adequate acknowledgments and recompenses, etc., etc. The drinkers, finding we did not return immediately to the table, sent us a decanter of Madeira, which the governor made liberal use of, and in proportion became more profuse of his solicitations and promises.
paras.z: 我们的新总督丹尼上尉替我从皇家学会带来了前面提到的那枚奖章，在本市为他举行的宴会上交给了我。他同时用十分客气的话表示了对我的敬重，说他早就熟知我的为人了。饭后，客人们照当时的习惯喝起酒来，他把我拉到另一个房间，告诉我，他在英国的朋友们劝他同我结交，因为我是能给他最好的建议、最有效地帮助他顺利施政的人；所以他最希望的就是同我保持融洽的关系，并且请我相信，他随时乐意尽他的力量为我效劳。他还对我说了许多业主对本殖民地怀有好意的话，说如果长期以来对他的措施的反对能够停止，他同人民之间恢复和谐，这对我们大家，尤其对我，会有多大的好处；人们认为，要促成这件事，没有谁比我更能出力；而我可以指望得到相应的酬谢和报偿，等等，等等。喝酒的人见我们没有立刻回到桌边，就给我们送来一瓶马德拉酒，总督喝了不少，酒喝得越多，他的恳求和许诺也越发滔滔不绝。

paras.e: My answers were to this purpose: that my circumstances, thanks to God, were such as to make proprietary favours unnecessary to me; and that, being a member of the Assembly, I could not possibly accept of any; that, however, I had no personal enmity to the proprietary, and that, whenever the public measures he propos'd should appear to be for the good of the people, no one should espouse and forward them more zealously than myself; my past opposition having been founded on this, that the measures which had been urged were evidently intended to serve the proprietary interest, with great prejudice to that of the people; that I was much obliged to him (the governor) for his professions of regard to me, and that he might rely on every thing in my power to make his administration as easy as possible, hoping at the same time that he had not brought with him the same unfortunate instruction his predecessor had been hamper'd with.
paras.z: 我的回答大意是：感谢上帝，我的境况使我不需要业主的恩惠；而且我身为议会议员，决不可能接受任何恩惠；不过，我对业主并没有个人的敌意，只要他提出的公共措施看来是为人民谋利益的，没有人会比我更热心地拥护和推动；我过去所以反对，是因为那些被极力推行的措施显然是要为业主的利益服务，而大大损害人民的利益；我非常感谢他（总督）表示对我的看重，他可以信赖我会尽我的一切力量使他的施政尽可能顺利，同时希望他没有带来他的前任曾受其束缚的那种不幸的训令。

paras.e: On this he did not then explain himself; but when he afterwards came to do business with the Assembly, they appear'd again, the disputes were renewed, and I was as active as ever in the opposition, being the penman, first, of the request to have a communication of the instructions, and then of the remarks upon them, which may be found in the votes of the time, and in the Historical Review I afterward publish'd. But between us personally no enmity arose; we were often together; he was a man of letters, had seen much of the world, and was very entertaining and pleasing in conversation. He gave me the first information that my old friend Jas. Ralph was still alive; that he was esteem'd one of the best political writers in England; had been employ'd in the dispute between Prince Frederic and the king, and had obtain'd a pension of three hundred a year; that his reputation was indeed small as a poet, Pope having damned his poetry in the Dunciad; but his prose was thought as good as any man's.
paras.z: 对这一点他当时没有表明态度；但是后来他同议会打起交道来，那些训令又出现了，争执重新开始，我在反对派中同以往一样积极；先是要求出示训令的请求书，后来是对训令的评论，都出自我的手笔，这些可以在当时的表决记录和我后来出版的《历史评论》里找到。但我们个人之间并没有产生敌意；我们常在一起；他是个有文才的人，见过许多世面，谈吐非常有趣，令人愉快。是他最先告诉我，我的老朋友詹姆斯·拉尔夫还活着；他被认为是英国最好的政论作家之一；曾在弗雷德里克亲王同国王的争执中受雇执笔，得到了每年三百镑的年金；他作为诗人确实没有什么名气，蒲柏在《愚人志》里把他的诗骂得一文不值；但他的散文被认为不输任何人。

paras.e: [15] The Assembly finally finding the proprietary obstinately persisted in manacling their deputies with instructions inconsistent not only with the privileges of the people, but with the service of the crown, resolv'd to petition the king against them, and appointed me their agent to go over to England, to present and support the petition. The House had sent up a bill to the governor, granting a sum of sixty thousand pounds for the king's use (ten thousand pounds of which was subjected to the orders of the then general, Lord Loudoun), which the governor absolutely refus'd to pass, in compliance with his instructions.
paras.z: [15] 议会终于发现，业主们顽固地坚持用训令束缚他们的代理人，而这些训令不仅同人民的权利相抵触，也同为国王效力相抵触，于是决定向国王请愿控告他们，并指派我为代表，到英国去呈递这份请愿书并为它申辩。议院曾向总督送去一项法案，拨款六万镑供国王使用（其中一万镑交由当时的将军劳登勋爵支配），总督遵照他的训令断然拒绝批准。

paras.e: [15] The many unanimous resolves of the Assembly--what date?--[Marg. note.]
paras.z: [15] 议会的多次一致决议——是什么日期？——［页边注］

paras.e: I had agreed with Captain Morris, of the paquet at New York, for my passage, and my stores were put on board, when Lord Loudoun arriv'd at Philadelphia, expressly, as he told me, to endeavor an accommodation between the governor and Assembly, that his majesty's service might not be obstructed by their dissensions. Accordingly, he desir'd the governor and myself to meet him, that he might hear what was to be said on both sides. We met and discuss'd the business. In behalf of the Assembly, I urg'd all the various arguments that may be found in the public papers of that time, which were of my writing, and are printed with the minutes of the Assembly; and the governor pleaded his instructions; the bond he had given to observe them, and his ruin if he disobey'd, yet seemed not unwilling to hazard himself if Lord Loudoun would advise it. This his lordship did not chuse to do, though I once thought I had nearly prevail'd with him to do it; but finally he rather chose to urge the compliance of the Assembly; and he entreated me to use my endeavours with them for that purpose, declaring that he would spare none of the king's troops for the defense of our frontiers, and that, if we did not continue to provide for that defense ourselves, they must remain expos'd to the enemy.
paras.z: 我已经同纽约那艘邮船的船长莫里斯讲定了船位，我的食品等物也已装上了船，这时劳登勋爵到了费城。他告诉我，他是专程来设法调解总督和议会的，免得他们的不和妨碍为国王陛下效力。因此他要总督和我去见他，好听听双方有什么话要说。我们见了面，讨论了这件事。我代表议会，提出了种种论据——这些都可以在当时的公文里找到，那些公文是我写的，同议会的会议记录印在一起；总督则以他的训令为由，说他立过保证书要遵守训令，如果违抗就要身败名裂，不过看来只要劳登勋爵劝他，他也不是不愿意冒这个险。勋爵阁下不愿这样做，虽然有一回我以为差不多已经说动了他；最后他还是宁愿敦促议会让步；他恳求我尽力去劝他们，并且声明他不会抽调任何国王的军队来保卫我们的边境，如果我们自己不继续为这项防务出力，边境就只能暴露在敌人面前。

paras.e: I acquainted the House with what had pass'd, and, presenting them with a set of resolutions I had drawn up, declaring our rights, and that we did not relinquish our claim to those rights, but only suspended the exercise of them on this occasion thro' force, against which we protested, they at length agreed to drop that bill, and frame another conformable to the proprietary instructions. This of course the governor pass'd, and I was then at liberty to proceed on my voyage. But, in the meantime, the paquet had sailed with my sea-stores, which was some loss to me, and my only recompense was his lordship's thanks for my service, all the credit of obtaining the accommodation falling to his share.
paras.z: 我把经过告诉了议院，并向他们提交了我起草的一组决议，宣告我们的权利，声明我们并没有放弃对这些权利的要求，只是这一回迫于强力而暂停行使，对这种强力我们表示抗议。他们终于同意撤回那项法案，另拟一项符合业主训令的法案。这项法案总督当然批准了，于是我可以动身启程了。可是这期间，邮船已经带着我的食品开走了，这对我是一笔损失；而我唯一的报偿是勋爵阁下对我出力的感谢，促成和解的全部功劳都落到了他的名下。

paras.e: He set out for New York before me; and, as the time for dispatching the paquet-boats was at his disposition, and there were two then remaining there, one of which, he said, was to sail very soon, I requested to know the precise time, that I might not miss her by any delay of mine. His answer was, "I have given out that she is to sail on Saturday next; but I may let you know, entre nous, that if you are there by Monday morning, you will be in time, but do not delay longer." By some accidental hinderance at a ferry, it was Monday noon before I arrived, and I was much afraid she might have sailed, as the wind was fair; but I was soon made easy by the information that she was still in the harbor, and would not move till the next day. One would imagine that I was now on the very point of departing for Europe. I thought so; but I was not then so well acquainted with his lordship's character, of which indecision was one of the strongest features. I shall give some instances. It was about the beginning of April that I came to New York, and I think it was near the end of June before we sail'd. There were then two of the paquet-boats, which had been long in port, but were detained for the general's letters, which were always to be ready to-morrow. Another paquet arriv'd; she too was detain'd; and, before we sail'd, a fourth was expected. Ours was the first to be dispatch'd, as having been there longest. Passengers were engag'd in all, and some extremely impatient to be gone, and the merchants uneasy about their letters, and the orders they had given for insurance (it being war time) for fall goods! but their anxiety avail'd nothing; his lordship's letters were not ready; and yet whoever waited on him found him always at his desk, pen in hand, and concluded he must needs write abundantly.
paras.z: 他比我先动身去纽约；邮船什么时候发出由他决定，当时那里还停着两艘，他说其中一艘很快就要开，我就请他告诉我确切的时间，免得我因为耽搁而误了船。他的回答是：“我对外说的是下星期六开船；不过我可以私下告诉你，如果你星期一早晨到，还来得及，但不要再迟了。”因为在一个渡口遇到意外的耽搁，我到的时候已是星期一中午，我很怕船已经开了，因为正刮着顺风；但我很快放了心，听说船还在港里，要到第二天才动。人家也许会以为，我这下马上就要启程去欧洲了。我也这样以为；可是那时我还不那么了解勋爵阁下的性格，优柔寡断正是他最突出的特点之一。我举几个例子。我到纽约大约是四月初，我想我们直到将近六月底才开船。当时有两艘邮船，已经在港里停了很久，却为了等将军的信件而被扣着，而那些信总是“明天就好”。又到了一艘邮船，它也被扣下了；在我们开船之前，第四艘眼看也要到了。我们那艘是第一个要发出的，因为在那里停得最久。每艘船都订满了乘客，有些人急得不得了想走；商人们为他们的信件，为他们给秋季货物下的保险单（当时是战时）而坐立不安！可是他们着急也没有用；勋爵阁下的信还没有写好；然而不管谁去见他，总见他坐在书桌前，手里拿着笔，都以为他一定写了很多很多。

paras.e: Going myself one morning to pay my respects, I found in his antechamber one Innis, a messenger of Philadelphia, who had come from thence express with a paquet from Governor Denny for the General. He delivered to me some letters from my friends there, which occasion'd my inquiring when he was to return, and where he lodg'd, that I might send some letters by him. He told me he was order'd to call to-morrow at nine for the general's answer to the governor, and should set off immediately. I put my letters into his hands the same day. A fortnight after I met him again in the same place. "So, you are soon return'd, Innis?" "Returned! no, I am not gone yet." "How so?" "I have called here by order every morning these two weeks past for his lordship's letter, and it is not yet ready." "Is it possible, when he is so great a writer? for I see him constantly at his escritoire." "Yes," says Innis, "but he is like St. George on the signs, always on horseback, and never rides on." This observation of the messenger was, it seems, well founded; for, when in England, I understood that Mr. Pitt gave it as one reason for removing this general, and sending Generals Amherst and Wolfe, that the minister never heard from him, and could not know what he was doing.
paras.z: 有一天早晨我自己去向他问安，在他的前厅里遇见一个叫英尼斯的费城信差，他是专程从费城送丹尼总督给将军的一包公文来的。他交给我几封那里的朋友写来的信，我就问他什么时候回去，住在哪里，好托他带几封信。他告诉我，他奉命明天九点来取将军给总督的回信，拿到就立刻动身。我当天就把信交到了他手里。两个星期以后，我又在同一个地方遇见他。“哦，英尼斯，你这么快就回来了？”“回来！不，我还没走呢。”“怎么回事？”“这两个星期我每天早晨奉命到这里来取勋爵阁下的信，可是它还没有写好。”“这怎么可能？他那么勤于动笔，我总看见他坐在写字台前。”英尼斯说：“是啊，可是他就像招牌上的圣乔治，老是骑在马上，却从来不往前走。”这个信差的话看来很有根据；因为我到了英国才听说，皮特先生把这一点作为撤换这位将军、改派阿默斯特和沃尔夫两位将军的一个理由：大臣从来得不到他的消息，无从知道他在干什么。

paras.e: This daily expectation of sailing, and all the three paquets going down to Sandy Hook, to join the fleet there, the passengers thought it best to be on board, lest by a sudden order the ships should sail, and they be left behind. There, if I remember right, we were about six weeks, consuming our sea-stores, and oblig'd to procure more. At length the fleet sail'd, the General and all his army on board, bound to Louisburg, with intent to besiege and take that fortress; all the paquet-boats in company ordered to attend the General's ship, ready to receive his dispatches when they should be ready. We were out five days before we got a letter with leave to part, and then our ship quitted the fleet and steered for England. The other two paquets he still detained, carried them with him to Halifax, where he stayed some time to exercise the men in sham attacks upon sham forts, then alter'd his mind as to besieging Louisburg, and return'd to New York, with all his troops, together with the two paquets above mentioned, and all their passengers! During his absence the French and savages had taken Fort George, on the frontier of that province, and the savages had massacred many of the garrison after capitulation.
paras.z: 人们天天盼着开船，三艘邮船又全都开到桑迪胡克去同那里的舰队会合，乘客们认为最好待在船上，免得突然一声令下，船开了，把他们丢在后面。如果我没有记错，我们在那里待了大约六个星期，把航海的食品都吃光了，不得不再去置办。舰队终于启航了，将军和他的全部军队都在船上，开往路易斯堡，打算围攻并夺取那座要塞；所有的邮船都奉命随同将军的座舰，准备在他的公文写好时接取。我们出海五天，才拿到一封准许我们离开的信，于是我们的船离开舰队，驶向英国。另外两艘邮船他仍然扣着，带着它们到了哈利法克斯；他在那里停了一段时间，让士兵们对着假堡垒操练假进攻，然后改变了围攻路易斯堡的主意，带着全部军队，连同上面说的那两艘邮船和船上所有的乘客，回到了纽约！在他离开期间，法国人和野蛮人攻占了那个殖民地边境上的乔治堡，守军投降以后，野蛮人屠杀了其中许多人。

paras.e: I saw afterwards in London Captain Bonnell, who commanded one of those paquets. He told me that, when he had been detain'd a month, he acquainted his lordship that his ship was grown foul, to a degree that must necessarily hinder her fast sailing, a point of consequence for a paquet-boat, and requested an allowance of time to heave her down and clean her bottom. He was asked how long that would require. He answer'd, three days. The general replied, "If you can do it in one day, I give leave; otherwise not; for you must certainly sail the day after to-morrow." So he never obtain'd leave, though detained afterwards from day to day during full three months.
paras.z: 后来我在伦敦见到了博内尔船长，他指挥的是那两艘邮船之一。他告诉我，他被扣了一个月的时候，向勋爵阁下报告说，他的船底已经长满了附着物，势必妨碍船的航速，而航速对邮船是要紧的事，请求给他一点时间把船侧倾过来清理船底。勋爵问他需要多久。他回答说三天。将军答道：“如果你一天能办完，我就准许；否则不行；因为你后天一定得开船。”所以他始终没有得到许可，可是此后他一天天被扣着，足足扣了三个月。

paras.e: I saw also in London one of Bonnell's passengers, who was so enrag'd against his lordship for deceiving and detaining him so long at New York, and then carrying him to Halifax and back again, that he swore he would sue for damages. Whether he did or not, I never heard; but, as he represented the injury to his affairs, it was very considerable.
paras.z: 我在伦敦还见到了博内尔船上的一位乘客，他对勋爵阁下恨之入骨，因为勋爵欺骗了他，把他在纽约扣了那么久，又把他带到哈利法克斯再带回来，他发誓要告勋爵赔偿损失。他后来告了没有，我没有听说；但照他讲的，他的生意所受的损害是非常大的。

paras.e: On the whole, I wonder'd much how such a man came to be intrusted with so important a business as the conduct of a great army; but, having since seen more of the great world, and the means of obtaining, and motives for giving places, my wonder is diminished. General Shirley, on whom the command of the army devolved upon the death of Braddock, would, in my opinion, if continued in place, have made a much better campaign than that of Loudoun in 1757, which was frivolous, expensive, and disgraceful to our nation beyond conception; for, tho' Shirley was not a bred soldier, he was sensible and sagacious in himself, and attentive to good advice from others, capable of forming judicious plans, and quick and active in carrying them into execution. Loudoun, instead of defending the colonies with his great army, left them totally expos'd while he paraded idly at Halifax, by which means Fort George was lost, besides, he derang'd all our mercantile operations, and distress'd our trade, by a long embargo on the exportation of provisions, on pretence of keeping supplies from being obtain'd by the enemy, but in reality for beating down their price in favor of the contractors, in whose profits, it was said, perhaps from suspicion only, he had a share. And, when at length the embargo was taken off, by neglecting to send notice of it to Charlestown, the Carolina fleet was detain'd near three months longer, whereby their bottoms were so much damaged by the worm that a great part of them foundered in their passage home.
paras.z: 总之，我十分纳闷，这样一个人怎么会被委以指挥一支大军这样重要的职责；不过后来我对上层社会，对谋取职位的手段和授予职位的动机见得多了，我的纳闷也就减少了。布雷多克死后，军队的指挥权落到了雪利将军身上；照我看，如果让他继续任职，他会打出一场比劳登 1757 年那场好得多的战役——劳登的那场战役无聊、靡费，给我们的国家带来的耻辱超乎想象。因为雪利虽然不是科班出身的军人，他本人却明白事理、有见识，肯听别人的好意见，能订出审慎的计划，执行起来又迅速而积极。劳登非但没有用他的大军保卫各殖民地，反而在他闲逛哈利法克斯的时候让它们完全暴露在外，乔治堡就是这样丢掉的。此外，他还长期禁止粮食出口，打乱了我们全部的商业活动，使我们的贸易陷入困境；借口是不让敌人得到补给，实际上是为了压低粮价，让承包商得利，据说——也许只是出于猜疑——那些利润里有他的一份。等到禁运终于解除，又因为疏忽没有通知查尔斯顿，卡罗来纳的船队又多耽搁了将近三个月，船底被船蛆蛀得很厉害，其中很大一部分在回航途中沉没了。

paras.e: Shirley was, I believe, sincerely glad of being relieved from so burdensome a charge as the conduct of an army must be to a man unacquainted with military business. I was at the entertainment given by the city of New York to Lord Loudoun, on his taking upon him the command. Shirley, tho' thereby superseded, was present also. There was a great company of officers, citizens, and strangers, and, some chairs having been borrowed in the neighborhood, there was one among them very low, which fell to the lot of Mr. Shirley. Perceiving it as I sat by him, I said, "They have given you, sir, too low a seat." "No matter," says he, "Mr. Franklin, I find a low seat the easiest."
paras.z: 我相信，雪利是真心高兴卸下这样沉重的担子的；对一个不熟悉军事的人来说，指挥一支军队一定是这样的担子。劳登勋爵接任指挥的时候，纽约市为他举行了宴会，我也在场。雪利虽然因此被取代，也出席了。军官、市民和外地来客济济一堂；因为向邻近人家借了一些椅子，其中有一把非常矮，恰好轮到雪利先生坐。我坐在他旁边，看到了，就说：“先生，他们给您的座位太低了。”他说：“不要紧，富兰克林先生，我觉得低的座位最舒服。”

paras.e: While I was, as afore mention'd, detain'd at New York, I receiv'd all the accounts of the provisions, etc., that I had furnish'd to Braddock, some of which accounts could not sooner be obtain'd from the different persons I had employ'd to assist in the business. I presented them to Lord Loudoun, desiring to be paid the ballance. He caus'd them to be regularly examined by the proper officer, who, after comparing every article with its voucher, certified them to be right; and the balance due for which his lordship promis'd to give me an order on the paymaster. This was, however, put off from time to time; and, tho' I call'd often for it by appointment, I did not get it. At length, just before my departure, he told me he had, on better consideration, concluded not to mix his accounts with those of his predecessors. "And you," says he, "when in England, have only to exhibit your accounts at the treasury, and you will be paid immediately."
paras.z: 前面说过，我被滞留在纽约的时候，收齐了我为布雷多克供应粮食等物的全部账目，其中有些是我雇来协办这件事的各色人等先前一直没能交来的。我把账目呈给劳登勋爵，请求付清余额。他让主管官员照章审核，那位官员把每一项同凭单核对之后，证明账目无误；勋爵阁下答应就应付的余额给我开一张向军需官领款的支付令。可是这件事一拖再拖；我虽然常常如约去取，却始终没有拿到。最后，就在我启程之前，他对我说，他经过更周详的考虑，决定不把他的账目同前任的混在一起。他说：“至于你，到了英国，只要把账目拿给财政部看，他们马上就会付给你。”

paras.e: I mention'd, but without effect, the great and unexpected expense I had been put to by being detain'd so long at New York, as a reason for my desiring to be presently paid; and on my observing that it was not right I should be put to any further trouble or delay in obtaining the money I had advanc'd, as I charged no commission for my service, "O, sir," says he, "you must not think of persuading us that you are no gainer; we understand better those affairs, and know that every one concerned in supplying the army finds means, in the doing it, to fill his own pockets." I assur'd him that was not my case, and that I had not pocketed a farthing; but he appear'd clearly not to believe me; and, indeed, I have since learnt that immense fortunes are often made in such employments. As to my ballance, I am not paid it to this day, of which more hereafter.
paras.z: 我提到，因为在纽约被扣了那么久，我花了一大笔意想不到的开销，以此作为我希望立刻得到付款的理由，但是没有用；我又说，我替他们办事并没有收取佣金，为了拿回我垫付的钱而再让我费事、再让我等，是不应该的。他说：“哦，先生，你别想让我们相信你没有捞到好处；这些事我们懂得更清楚，知道凡是经手供应军需的人，都有办法在经手的时候装满自己的腰包。”我向他保证我不是这样，我没有往腰包里装过一个铜板；可是他显然不相信我；说实在的，我后来才知道，干这类差事的人常常发大财。至于我的余款，至今没有付给我，这件事后面再说。

paras.e: Our captain of the paquet had boasted much, before we sailed, of the swiftness of his ship; unfortunately, when we came to sea, she proved the dullest of ninety-six sail, to his no small mortification. After many conjectures respecting the cause, when we were near another ship almost as dull as ours, which, however, gain'd upon us, the captain ordered all hands to come aft, and stand as near the ensign staff as possible. We were, passengers included, about forty persons. While we stood there, the ship mended her pace, and soon left her neighbour far behind, which prov'd clearly what our captain suspected, that she was loaded too much by the head. The casks of water, it seems, had been all plac'd forward; these he therefore order'd to be mov'd further aft, on which the ship recover'd her character, and proved the sailer in the fleet.
paras.z: 我们那艘邮船的船长在开船之前曾大大夸耀他的船跑得快；不幸的是，到了海上，它却是九十六艘船里最慢的一艘，使他十分难堪。大家对原因作了许多猜测；后来我们靠近了另一艘几乎同我们一样慢的船，可它还是渐渐超过了我们，船长就命令全体人员到船尾去，尽量靠近旗杆站着。连乘客在内，我们大约有四十人。我们站在那里的时候，船加快了速度，不久就把邻船远远甩在后面，这清楚地证明了船长的猜想：船头装得太重了。看来水桶全都放在了前面；他于是下令把它们往后挪，船就恢复了它的名声，成了船队里跑得最快的一艘。

paras.e: The captain said she had once gone at the rate of thirteen knots, which is accounted thirteen miles per hour. We had on board, as a passenger, Captain Kennedy, of the Navy, who contended that it was impossible, and that no ship ever sailed so fast, and that there must have been some error in the division of the log-line, or some mistake in heaving the log. A wager ensu'd between the two captains, to be decided when there should be sufficient wind. Kennedy thereupon examin'd rigorously the log-line, and, being satisfi'd with that, he determin'd to throw the log himself. Accordingly some days after, when the wind blew very fair and fresh, and the captain of the paquet, Lutwidge, said he believ'd she then went at the rate of thirteen knots, Kennedy made the experiment, and own'd his wager lost.
paras.z: 船长说它有一回跑到过十三节，也就是算作每小时十三海里。我们船上有一位乘客，海军的肯尼迪舰长，他坚持说这是不可能的，从来没有哪条船跑得这样快，一定是测程绳的刻度有误，或者抛测程仪的时候出了差错。两位船长于是打了赌，等风力足够的时候见分晓。肯尼迪随即严格地检查了测程绳，对它满意之后，决定亲自抛测程仪。几天以后，风刮得又顺又劲，邮船的船长勒特威奇说，他相信船这时的速度有十三节，肯尼迪就做了测试，承认自己赌输了。

paras.e: The above fact I give for the sake of the following observation. It has been remark'd, as an imperfection in the art of ship-building, that it can never be known, till she is tried, whether a new ship will or will not be a good sailer; for that the model of a good-sailing ship has been exactly follow'd in a new one, which has prov'd, on the contrary, remarkably dull. I apprehend that this may partly be occasion'd by the different opinions of seamen respecting the modes of lading, rigging, and sailing of a ship; each has his system; and the same vessel, laden by the judgment and orders of one captain, shall sail better or worse than when by the orders of another. Besides, it scarce ever happens that a ship is form'd, fitted for the sea, and sail'd by the same person. One man builds the hull, another rigs her, a third lades and sails her. No one of these has the advantage of knowing all the ideas and experience of the others, and, therefore, can not draw just conclusions from a combination of the whole.
paras.z: 我讲上面这件事，是为了下面这点看法。人们说过，造船术有一个缺陷：一艘新船是不是跑得快，不经试航是永远无法知道的；因为有人完全照一艘快船的样子造了一艘新船，结果新船反而出奇地慢。我想这也许部分是由于水手们对装载、装帆和驾驶一艘船的方式各有不同的意见；各人有各人的一套；同一艘船，照这位船长的判断和命令来装载，同照另一位的命令来装载，航行起来就会有好有坏。此外，一艘船由同一个人建造、装备出海并驾驶，这样的事几乎从来没有。一个人造船身，另一个人装帆索，第三个人装货并驾驶。他们当中谁也没有便利去了解其他人的全部想法和经验，因此不能把全部情况综合起来得出正确的结论。

paras.e: Even in the simple operation of sailing when at sea, I have often observ'd different judgments in the officers who commanded the successive watches, the wind being the same. One would have the sails trimm'd sharper or flatter than another, so that they seem'd to have no certain rule to govern by. Yet I think a set of experiments might be instituted, first, to determine the most proper form of the hull for swift sailing; next, the best dimensions and properest place for the masts: then the form and quantity of sails, and their position, as the wind may be; and, lastly, the disposition of the lading. This is an age of experiments, and I think a set accurately made and combin'd would be of great use. I am persuaded, therefore, that ere long some ingenious philosopher will undertake it, to whom I wish success.
paras.z: 即使在海上驾驶这样简单的操作上，我也常常观察到，在风向相同的情况下，指挥前后各班的军官判断不一。这一位要把帆收得比那一位更紧些或者更平些，看来他们并没有一定的规则可循。可是我想，可以设计一套实验：首先确定最适于快速航行的船身形状；其次是桅杆的最佳尺寸和最合适的位置；然后是帆的形状和数量，以及在各种风向下帆的位置；最后是货物的安排。这是一个实验的时代，我想，精确地做出并综合起来的一套实验会大有用处。所以我相信，不久就会有某位聪明的哲学家来承担这件事，我祝他成功。

paras.e: We were several times chas'd in our passage, but outsail'd every thing, and in thirty days had soundings. We had a good observation, and the captain judg'd himself so near our port, Falmouth, that, if we made a good run in the night, we might be off the mouth of that harbor in the morning, and by running in the night might escape the notice of the enemy's privateers, who often crus'd near the entrance of the channel. Accordingly, all the sail was set that we could possibly make, and the wind being very fresh and fair, we went right before it, and made great way. The captain, after his observation, shap'd his course, as he thought, so as to pass wide of the Scilly Isles; but it seems there is sometimes a strong indraught setting up St. George's Channel, which deceives seamen and caused the loss of Sir Cloudesley Shovel's squadron. This indraught was probably the cause of what happened to us.
paras.z: 我们在航程中被追赶了好几次，但是把什么船都甩在了后面，三十天后就测到了水深。我们作了一次很好的天文观测，船长判断自己离我们的港口法尔茅斯已经很近，如果夜里航行顺利，早晨就可以到达港口外面；而且夜里航行可以躲过敌方私掠船的注意，它们常在海峡入口附近巡弋。于是我们张起了所能张的全部风帆，风又顺又劲，我们顺风直驶，走得很快。船长观测之后定了航向，照他的想法是要远远绕过锡利群岛；可是看来圣乔治海峡有时有一股向里的强流，常使水手上当，克劳兹利·肖维尔爵士的舰队就是因此覆没的。我们遇到的事，大概也是这股强流造成的。

paras.e: We had a watchman plac'd in the bow, to whom they often called, "Look well out before there," and he as often answered, "Ay ay;" but perhaps had his eyes shut, and was half asleep at the time, they sometimes answering, as is said, mechanically; for he did not see a light just before us, which had been hid by the studdingsails from the man at the helm, and from the rest of the watch, but by an accidental yaw of the ship was discover'd, and occasion'd a great alarm, we being very near it, the light appearing to me as big as a cart-wheel. It was midnight, and our captain fast asleep; but Captain Kennedy, jumping upon deck, and seeing the danger, ordered the ship to wear round, all sails standing; an operation dangerous to the masts, but it carried us clear, and we escaped shipwreck, for we were running right upon the rocks on which the light-house was erected. This deliverance impressed me strongly with the utility of light-houses, and made me resolve to encourage the building more of them in America, if I should live to return there.
paras.z: 我们在船头安排了一个瞭望的人，他们常常朝他喊：“前面留神看着！”他也每次都答应：“是，是。”可是也许他当时闭着眼睛，半睡半醒——据说他们有时是机械地答应的——因为他没有看见就在我们正前方的一盏灯。这盏灯被翼帆挡住了，舵手和当班的其余的人都看不见，只是因为船身偶然一偏才被发现，引起了一片惊慌，因为我们离它已经很近，那灯光在我看来有车轮那么大。当时是半夜，我们的船长睡得正熟；可是肯尼迪舰长跳上甲板，看到危险，下令让船满帆掉头。这个操作对桅杆是危险的，但它使我们脱了险，我们逃过了一场船难，因为我们正朝着建有灯塔的那片礁石直冲过去。这次得救使我深深感到灯塔的用处，使我下定决心，如果我能活着回到美洲，要鼓励在那里多建灯塔。

paras.e: In the morning it was found by the soundings, etc., that we were near our port, but a thick fog hid the land from our sight. About nine o'clock the fog began to rise, and seem'd to be lifted up from the water like the curtain at a play-house, discovering underneath, the town of Falmouth, the vessels in its harbor, and the fields that surrounded it. This was a most pleasing spectacle to those who had been so long without any other prospects than the uniform view of a vacant ocean, and it gave us the more pleasure as we were now free from the anxieties which the state of war occasion'd.
paras.z: 早晨，从测深等等判断，我们已经靠近我们的港口，但是浓雾遮住了陆地。九点钟左右，雾开始升起，仿佛像戏院里的幕布一样从水面上提了起来，露出下面的法尔茅斯城、港里的船只和四周的田野。对于这么久以来除了空荡荡的海洋那一成不变的景象之外什么也看不到的人，这是一幅极其悦目的景色；它更使我们高兴的是，我们现在摆脱了战争状态所引起的种种忧虑。

paras.e: I set out immediately, with my son, for London, and we only stopt a little by the way to view Stonehenge on Salisbury Plain, and Lord Pembroke's house and gardens, with his very curious antiquities at Wilton. We arrived in London the 27th of July, 1757. [16]
paras.z: 我立刻同我儿子动身去伦敦，路上只稍稍停留，看了索尔兹伯里平原上的巨石阵，以及彭布罗克勋爵在威尔顿的宅邸和花园，还有他那些非常珍奇的古物。我们在 1757 年 7 月 27 日到了伦敦。[16]

paras.e: [16] Here terminates the Autobiography, as published by Wm. Temple Franklin and his successors. What follows was written in the last year of Dr. Franklin's life, and was first printed (in English) in Mr. Bigelow's edition of 1868.--Ed.
paras.z: [16] 威廉·坦普尔·富兰克林及其后继者所刊行的《自传》到此为止。以下是富兰克林博士在生命的最后一年写的，最初（以英文）刊印于比奇洛先生 1868 年的版本。——编者注

paras.e: As soon as I was settled in a lodging Mr. Charles had provided for me, I went to visit Dr. Fothergill, to whom I was strongly recommended, and whose counsel respecting my proceedings I was advis'd to obtain. He was against an immediate complaint to government, and thought the proprietaries should first be personally appli'd to, who might possibly be induc'd by the interposition and persuasion of some private friends, to accommodate matters amicably. I then waited on my old friend and correspondent, Mr. Peter Collinson, who told me that John Hanbury, the great Virginia merchant, had requested to be informed when I should arrive, that he might carry me to Lord Granville's, who was then President of the Council and wished to see me as soon as possible. I agreed to go with him the next morning. Accordingly Mr. Hanbury called for me and took me in his carriage to that nobleman's, who receiv'd me with great civility; and after some questions respecting the present state of affairs in America and discourse thereupon, he said to me: "You Americans have wrong ideas of the nature of your constitution; you contend that the king's instructions to his governors are not laws, and think yourselves at liberty to regard or disregard them at your own discretion. But those instructions are not like the pocket instructions given to a minister going abroad, for regulating his conduct in some trifling point of ceremony. They are first drawn up by judges learned in the laws; they are then considered, debated, and perhaps amended in Council, after which they are signed by the king. They are then, so far as they relate to you, the law of the land, for the king is the Legislator of the Colonies." I told his lordship this was new doctrine to me. I had always understood from our charters that our laws were to be made by our Assemblies, to be presented indeed to the king for his royal assent, but that being once given the king could not repeal or alter them. And as the Assemblies could not make permanent laws without his assent, so neither could he make a law for them without theirs. He assur'd me I was totally mistaken. I did not think so, however, and his lordship's conversation having a little alarm'd me as to what might be the sentiments of the court concerning us, I wrote it down as soon as I return'd to my lodgings. I recollected that about 20 years before, a clause in a bill brought into Parliament by the ministry had propos'd to make the king's instructions laws in the colonies, but the clause was thrown out by the Commons, for which we adored them as our friends and friends of liberty, till by their conduct towards us in 1765 it seem'd that they had refus'd that point of sovereignty to the king only that they might reserve it for themselves.
paras.z: 我在查尔斯先生替我找好的寓所里一安顿下来，就去拜访福瑟吉尔医生；有人向他极力推荐过我，也有人劝我就自己该怎样行事听听他的意见。他反对立刻向政府申诉，认为应当先亲自同业主们交涉，也许靠几位私人朋友从中斡旋劝说，可以使他们和和气气地把事情解决。然后我去拜访我的老朋友、老通信者彼得·柯林森先生，他告诉我，弗吉尼亚大商人约翰·汉伯里曾要求在我到达时通知他，好带我去见格兰维尔勋爵；勋爵当时是枢密院议长，希望尽早见到我。我答应第二天早晨同他去。于是汉伯里先生来接我，用他的马车把我带到那位贵族的府上。勋爵十分客气地接待了我，就美洲目前的形势问了几个问题，谈了一阵之后，对我说：“你们美洲人对自己政体的性质有错误的看法；你们争辩说，国王给他的总督们的训令不是法律，认为自己可以随意遵守或者不遵守。可是那些训令不像给出国的使臣随身带的、规定他在某些礼节小事上怎样行事的那种训令。它们先由精通法律的法官们起草；然后在枢密院里审议、辩论，也许还加以修改，最后由国王签署。那么，就同你们有关的而言，它们就是国家的法律，因为国王是殖民地的立法者。”我对勋爵阁下说，这对我是新的说法。我从我们的特许状里一向理解的是，我们的法律由我们的议会制定，固然要呈请国王御准，但一经御准，国王就不能废除或更改。议会没有他的同意不能制定永久的法律，同样，他没有议会的同意也不能替它们制定法律。他向我断言我完全错了。可是我并不这样认为；勋爵阁下的这番话使我对朝廷可能对我们抱什么看法有点警觉，我一回到寓所就把它记了下来。我记起大约二十年前，内阁向国会提出的一项法案里有一个条款，提议使国王的训令在殖民地成为法律，但这个条款被下院否决了，我们为此把他们当作我们的朋友和自由的朋友来敬爱；直到 1765 年他们对我们的所作所为才使人看出，他们当初拒绝把那一点主权给国王，只是为了把它留给他们自己。

paras.e: After some days, Dr. Fothergill having spoken to the proprietaries, they agreed to a meeting with me at Mr. T. Penn's house in Spring Garden. The conversation at first consisted of mutual declarations of disposition to reasonable accommodations, but I suppose each party had its own ideas of what should be meant by reasonable. We then went into consideration of our several points of complaint, which I enumerated. The proprietaries justify'd their conduct as well as they could, and I the Assembly's. We now appeared very wide, and so far from each other in our opinions as to discourage all hope of agreement. However, it was concluded that I should give them the heads of our complaints in writing, and they promis'd then to consider them. I did so soon after, but they put the paper into the hands of their solicitor, Ferdinand John Paris, who managed for them all their law business in their great suit with the neighbouring proprietary of Maryland, Lord Baltimore, which had subsisted 70 years, and wrote for them all their papers and messages in their dispute with the Assembly. He was a proud, angry man, and as I had occasionally in the answers of the Assembly treated his papers with some severity, they being really weak in point of argument and haughty in expression, he had conceived a mortal enmity to me, which discovering itself whenever we met, I declin'd the proprietary's proposal that he and I should discuss the heads of complaint between our two selves, and refus'd treating with any one but them. They then by his advice put the paper into the hands of the Attorney and Solicitor-General for their opinion and counsel upon it, where it lay unanswered a year wanting eight days, during which time I made frequent demands of an answer from the proprietaries, but without obtaining any other than that they had not yet received the opinion of the Attorney and Solicitor-General. What it was when they did receive it I never learnt, for they did not communicate it to me, but sent a long message to the Assembly drawn and signed by Paris, reciting my paper, complaining of its want of formality, as a rudeness on my part, and giving a flimsy justification of their conduct, adding that they should be willing to accommodate matters if the Assembly would send out some person of candour to treat with them for that purpose, intimating thereby that I was not such.
paras.z: 过了几天，福瑟吉尔医生同业主们谈过之后，他们同意在斯普林花园 T. 佩恩先生的家里同我会面。谈话一开始，双方都表示愿意合理地和解，但我想，所谓“合理”是什么意思，各方都有自己的理解。然后我们逐项讨论我们申诉的各点，由我一一列举。业主们尽力为他们的行为辩解，我也为议会的行为辩解。这时看来我们相去甚远，意见如此悬殊，使人对达成协议不抱任何希望。不过最后商定，由我把我们申诉的要点写成书面交给他们，他们答应到时加以考虑。不久我照办了；可是他们把那份文件交到了他们的律师费迪南德·约翰·帕里斯手里。在他们同邻近的马里兰业主巴尔的摩勋爵打的那场拖了七十年的大官司里，他们的全部法律事务都由此人经办；在他们同议会的争执中，他们的全部文件和咨文也都由他执笔。他是个骄傲而易怒的人；我在议会的答复里曾不时相当严厉地对待他的文字，因为那些文字实在论证无力而措辞傲慢，他因此对我怀了不共戴天的仇恨，我们每次见面这种仇恨都流露出来。所以业主提议由他同我两个人来讨论申诉的各项要点，我谢绝了，除了同业主本人，不肯同任何人谈判。于是他们照他的主意，把那份文件交给检察总长和副检察长，征求他们的意见和建议。文件在那里搁了差八天一年，没有答复；这期间我一再要求业主们答复，得到的回答始终只是：他们还没有收到检察总长和副检察长的意见。他们后来收到的意见是什么，我始终不知道，因为他们没有告诉我，而是给议会送去一份由帕里斯起草并署名的长篇咨文，复述了我的文件，抱怨它不合格式，是我的无礼，并为他们的行为作了一番站不住脚的辩解，还说如果议会派一位公正坦率的人来同他们谈判，他们是愿意把事情解决的，言外之意是我不是这样的人。

paras.e: The want of formality or rudeness was, probably, my not having address'd the paper to them with their assum'd titles of True and Absolute Proprietaries of the Province of Pennsylvania, which I omitted as not thinking it necessary in a paper, the intention of which was only to reduce to a certainty by writing, what in conversation I had delivered viva voce.
paras.z: 所谓不合格式或者无礼，大概是指我在文件上没有用他们自封的头衔“宾夕法尼亚殖民地真正而绝对的业主”来称呼他们。我省去这个称呼，是认为没有必要，因为这份文件的用意只是把我在谈话中口头说过的话用文字确定下来。

paras.e: But during this delay, the Assembly having prevailed with Gov'r Denny to pass an act taxing the proprietary estate in common with the estates of the people, which was the grand point in dispute, they omitted answering the message.
paras.z: 可是在这拖延期间，议会已经说服丹尼总督通过了一项法案，对业主的产业同人民的产业一体课税，这正是争执的要点所在，所以他们就没有答复那份咨文。

paras.e: When this act however came over, the proprietaries, counselled by Paris, determined to oppose its receiving the royal assent. Accordingly they petition'd the king in Council, and a hearing was appointed in which two lawyers were employ'd by them against the act, and two by me in support of it. They alledg'd that the act was intended to load the proprietary estate in order to spare those of the people, and that if it were suffer'd to continue in force, and the proprietaries who were in odium with the people, left to their mercy in proportioning the taxes, they would inevitably be ruined. We reply'd that the act had no such intention, and would have no such effect. That the assessors were honest and discreet men under an oath to assess fairly and equitably, and that any advantage each of them might expect in lessening his own tax by augmenting that of the proprietaries was too trifling to induce them to perjure themselves. This is the purport of what I remember as urged by both sides, except that we insisted strongly on the mischievous consequences that must attend a repeal, for that the money, £100,000, being printed and given to the king's use, expended in his service, and now spread among the people, the repeal would strike it dead in their hands to the ruin of many, and the total discouragement of future grants, and the selfishness of the proprietors in soliciting such a general catastrophe, merely from a groundless fear of their estate being taxed too highly, was insisted on in the strongest terms. On this, Lord Mansfield, one of the counsel rose, and beckoning me took me into the clerk's chamber, while the lawyers were pleading, and asked me if I was really of opinion that no injury would be done the proprietary estate in the execution of the act. I said certainly. "Then," says he, "you can have little objection to enter into an engagement to assure that point." I answer'd, "None at all." He then call'd in Paris, and after some discourse, his lordship's proposition was accepted on both sides; a paper to the purpose was drawn up by the Clerk of the Council, which I sign'd with Mr. Charles, who was also an Agent of the Province for their ordinary affairs, when Lord Mansfield returned to the Council Chamber, where finally the law was allowed to pass. Some changes were however recommended and we also engaged they should be made by a subsequent law, but the Assembly did not think them necessary; for one year's tax having been levied by the act before the order of Council arrived, they appointed a committee to examine the proceedings of the assessors, and on this committee they put several particular friends of the proprietaries. After a full enquiry, they unanimously sign'd a report that they found the tax had been assess'd with perfect equity.
paras.z: 可是这项法案送到英国以后，业主们在帕里斯的指点下，决心反对它得到国王的御准。于是他们向枢密院里的国王提出请愿，定了日期听审；他们雇了两位律师反对这项法案，我雇了两位支持它。他们声称，这项法案意在加重业主产业的负担，以便减轻人民产业的负担；如果听任它继续有效，而业主们在人民中间已经招人怨恨，摊派捐税的时候任凭人民摆布，他们就非破产不可。我们回答说，这项法案没有这样的用意，也不会有这样的后果。估税员都是诚实而审慎的人，宣过誓要公平合理地估税；他们每个人靠增加业主的税来减少自己的税所能指望的好处微不足道，不值得为此作伪誓。我所记得的双方陈述的大意就是这些；此外我们还极力强调废除这项法案必然带来的祸害：因为那笔钱，十万镑，已经印出来交给国王使用，花在了为他效力上，如今已经散布在人民手里，一旦废除，这些钱在他们手里就成了废纸，许多人会因此破产，今后的拨款也会完全受挫；业主们仅仅因为毫无根据地害怕自己的产业被课税过重，就去恳求造成这样一场普遍的灾难，这种自私我们用最强烈的言辞加以指出。说到这里，律师之一曼斯菲尔德勋爵站了起来，向我招手，趁律师们还在辩论，把我带进书记室，问我是否真的认为执行这项法案不会损害业主的产业。我说当然。他说：“那么，你大概不会反对立一个保证来担保这一点吧。”我回答说：“一点也不反对。”他于是把帕里斯叫了进来，谈了一阵之后，双方都接受了勋爵的提议；枢密院的书记起草了一份相应的文件，我同查尔斯先生一起签了字——他也是本殖民地办理日常事务的代理人——然后曼斯菲尔德勋爵回到枢密院会议室，最后这项法律获准通过了。不过枢密院建议作几处改动，我们也保证这些改动将由以后的一项法律来完成；但议会认为没有必要，因为在枢密院的命令到达之前，已经按这项法案征了一年的税，他们指派了一个委员会审查估税员的做法，并且把业主的几位特别要好的朋友也放进了这个委员会。经过充分调查，他们一致签署了一份报告，说他们发现税是完全公平地估定的。

paras.e: The Assembly looked into my entering into the first part of the engagement, as an essential service to the Province, since it secured the credit of the paper money then spread over all the country. They gave me their thanks in form when I return'd. But the proprietaries were enraged at Governor Denny for having pass'd the act, and turn'd him out with threats of suing him for breach of instructions which he had given bond to observe. He, however, having done it at the instance of the General, and for His Majesty's service, and having some powerful interests at court, despis'd the threats and they were never put in execution.... [Unfinished].
paras.z: 议会认为，我立下保证的前一部分，是对本殖民地的一项重大贡献，因为它保住了当时流通全境的纸币的信用。我回去的时候，他们正式向我表示了感谢。可是业主们对丹尼总督通过了那项法案十分恼怒，把他撤了职，还威胁要控告他违反了他立过保证书要遵守的训令。不过，他这样做是应将军的要求，为了替国王陛下效力，而且他在朝廷里有几位有势力的靠山，所以对这些威胁不屑一顾，这些威胁也始终没有付诸实行……［未完］
